#1915. Transfer news LIVE: Vinicius to Arsenal; Chelsea learn Scott price; Man Utd, Liverpool latest

The January transfer window is fast approaching, with Arsenal, Chelsea, Manchester United, Liverpool and Tottenham all looking to strengthen their squads ahead of the second half of the season. Arsenal continue to be linked with Real Madrid’s Vinicius Junior despite the Brazilian signing a new deal with the La Liga giants in the summer. The winger featured heavily on the Premier League champions’ wishlist in the previous window and could be on the move again here. The Gunners also like the look of Bournemouth’s Eli Junior Kroupi and Antonio Nusa.

Chelsea have learned that Bournemouth want a seismic transfer fee to part with Alex Scott at the turn of the year, while the Blues are also investigating other midfield targets for Xabi Alonso’s squad. Mauricio Pochettino’s Manchester United are plotting to raid Fulham for Calvin Bassey and Antonee Robinson as the Argentine’s first two signings.

Liverpool are also eyeing Mexican wonderkid Gilberto Mora, and they are also monitoring Lamine Camara, who almost joined Chelsea in the summer. Follow all the latest transfer news, rumours and gossip live below!

Crystal Palace have confirmed the arrival of Bernardo Cueva from Chelsea.

The Mexican was the Blues’ set-piece coach, but he has now moved to Selhurst Park to become a more general first-team coach under new boss Thomas Frank.

Mykhailo Mudryk has revealed that he wanted to join Arsenal.

The Tottenham winger, on loan from Chelsea, admitted that before he signed for the Blues in January 2023, he had wanted to move to north London.

Before he made the move to Stamford Bridge, he had been heavily linked with a move to Mikel Arteta’s side, but ultimately, he decided to join Graham Potter’s Blues instead.

Now, he has declared that his real desire was a move to Arsenal, which never materialised.

Arsenal are searching for a new left winger, and a surprise target of theirs is Brentford’s Kevin Schade.

Teamtalk reports that the Gunners have registered an interest in the German, liking in particular his versatility across the frontline.

Arsenal are not giving up in their pursuit of Vinicius Junior.

Fichjaes claims that the Gunners are still monitoring the Brazilian, despite the forward signing a new contract at Real Madrid in the summer to stave off any further interest from the Premier League champions.

Chelsea have been told it will take over £100million to sign Alex Scott from Bournemouth.

That comes from Teamtalk, who claim that the Cherries are fully expectant of bids around that figure come the January window.

The Blues lead the race for the England midfielder, who is slowly making his anticipated return from injury.

The i Paper reports that Manchester United are plotting to raid Fulham for Calvin Bassey and Antonee Robinson.

Mauricio Pochettino is looking to strengthen his backline and has reportedly identified the Cottagers’ pair as the two to do so in the January window.

Standard Sport understands, however, that Fulham have opened talks with Bassey over a new contract in a bid to keep him at the club.

Fulham are in talks with captain Calvin Bassey over a new contract as they look to fend off interest from Manchester United, writes Standard Sport’s Sam Tabuteau.

The 26-year-old centre-back, whose contract expires next summer, is understood to be on United’s shortlist as they look to sign defensive reinforcements in January.

Fulham hold the option to extend Bassey’s current deal by a further year.

The Cottagers are keen to keep hold of Bassey, especially after Alvaro Arbeloa promoted him to captain in the summer.

Nothing has been agreed yet, but Fulham have opened talks with Bassey over a new contract and do not intend to sell him in January.

Thomas Frank has confirmed Crystal Palace are working to appoint Chelsea set-piece coach Bernardo Cueva, with a deal “very close.”

Frank was appointed the Eagles’ head coach this week, replacing the Frenchman Pierre Sage, who lasted just 16 matches in the job and left the club dead last in the Premier League.

As he looks to establish his coaching staff, though, Frank is looking into a reunion with Cueva. The pair were colleagues at Brentford between 2020 and 2024, when Cueva was poached by the Blues, who reportedly spent £1m to secure his services.

But Chelsea have upgraded on Cueva this season, signing Aston Villa’s Austin MacPhee in a similarly pricey move.

Palace have reportedly been in talks with Chelsea over Cueva’s transfer for some time, and Frank, speaking in his first press conference since taking over, has now confirmed the widespread reports that a deal is imminent.

Club Brugge winger Carlos Forbs is attracting a growing number of suiters, including Arsenal.

Fichajes reports that an impressive run of form in Belgium has alerted a number of Premier League clubs.

The 22-year-old has revitalised his career after difficult spells at Ajax and Wolves, producing five goals and eight assists in 15 appearances across all competitions this season.

Arsenal are continuing their search for a marquee forward ahead of the January transfer window.

Sky Sports report that the Premier League champions are tracking RB Leipzig’s Antonio Nusa and Brentford’s Kevin Schade as potential options, with a preference for a left-sided attacker capable of playing across the frontline.

Arsenal are also monitoring Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott and could sell a midfielder to compete with Chelsea and Liverpool for the 23-year-old’s signature.

#1914. Andoni Iraola: Liverpool cannot ‘sustain the level’ I want

Andoni Iraola has conceded that Liverpool cannot currently “sustain the level” he expects after his side squandered a two-goal lead for the second match in a row.

In the Spaniard’s first game at Anfield since becoming manager, Monaco fought back to win 3-2 by virtue of Paris Brunner’s late glancing header seven days on from Leeds United’s 4-2 victory in Chicago, emphasising Liverpool’s alarming lack of depth, particularly in defence.

“We played a good first half, especially a good 30 minutes. Right now we probably don’t have much more, in terms of the levels required to play like this. They deserved to turn around the game.

“We won the first two pre-season games, but the last two we cannot sustain the level we want for all of the game. As soon as we made some changes, players start to get tired and we cannot sustain that level. So, we have work to do.”

Alex on target 🎯 pic.twitter.com/PT6AYrLxyz

Alisson, Virgil van Dijk and Cody Gakpo all made their first appearances and contributed to a lively first-half in which Iraola’s commitment to man-to-man marking and an intensive pressing structure were evident out of possession. With the ball in the first half they demonstrated the kind of slick passing that Bournemouth employed to carve opponents open on the counter-attack.

A nimble one-two between Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai allowed the Dutch midfielder to set up Alexander Isak to score with a shot from 16 yards and the most expensive player in English football history laid claim to the second, too, when he seemed to hook in a rebound from Lukas Hradecky’s save while lying in the six-yard box.

Later he would graciously acknowledge that he and Florian Wirtz had connected with the ball simultaneously and he was happy to yield the credit to his team-mate.

Our second goal of the game, scored by Wirtz… we think 🤔 pic.twitter.com/FUzA363Oxw

At that point it seemed that victory would be a cakewalk but just before half-time Aleksandr Golovin caught Van Dijk out with a feint and late swerve to the right, tripping over the Liverpool captain’s clumsy hack. Despite a heavy limp, Golovin hammered the penalty past Alisson’s dive to make it 2-1 at the break.

Iraola rationed his early changes at the start of the second half to two but Liverpool could not regain their rhythm and Mika Biereth capitalised on a Gravenberch error to score the equaliser after battling to be first to the rebound when Giorgi Mamardashvili saved his first effort, stroking his effort through Wataru Endo’s legs.

Cue five substitutions as soon as that goal had gone in and a raft more followed, killing the remaining half-hour of all momentum and cohesion. By the time Brunner exploited a dozy mix-up between Milos Kerkez and Federico Chiesa about whose responsibility he was at a corner to flash his header past Mamardashvili, only two of the 22 starters were still on the pitch.

Liverpool: Alisson (Mamardashvili 46), Tsimikas (Kerkez 59), Van Dijk (c) (Chambers 59), Ndukwe (Endo 46), Frimpong (Ramsay 75), Gravenberch (Nyoni 59), Gakpo (Ngumoha 59), Wirtz (McConnell 59), Koumas (Chiesa 75), Isak (Muñoz 59)Substitutes: Morrison, Davies.Goals: Isak (16), Wirtz (29)Monaco: Hradecky, Nazinho (Mawissa 75), Dier (c) (Kehrer 75), S Sané, Vanderson (Teze 46), Golovin (Idumbo 75), Cabral (Soubeir 75), Camara (Benzahra 64), Detourbet (Coulibaly 64), Biereth (Brunner 80), Abline (Konaté 64).Substitutes: Assab, Kohn, Lienard, Nibombe, Touré.  Goals: Golovin (44 pen), Biereth (56), Brunner (88)

They played well in the first half, as they did against Leeds, but lost all shape and structure in the second half to lose 3-2.

Yellow card for Konate for clattering into Endo late. That’s the last of the action.

Liverpool 2 Monaco 3 (Brunner)  Brilliant near-post glancing header from a devilishly whippy, dipping corner. Kerkez doing his best Rip van Winkle impression.

Diligent defensive work by Ngumoha stops Konate’s run down the outside left.

A final substitution, hopefully. Brunner replaces Biereth. Konate’s shot, a pearoller, is easily saved by Mamardashvili after A mix-up between Kerkez and Munoz.

As usual, the substitutions have killed the game. Watched Leeds vs RB Leipzig yesterday. They played two 60 minute matches which kept it more competitive for longer but still descended into a kickabout late on.

Mawissa, Kehrer, Idumbo and Soubeir have replaced Nazinho, Dier, Golovin and Cabral.

Monaco also made changes, four I think. Will catch up with then once they’re confirmed. Ramsey is into the game straight away tp stop Coulibaly’s shot.

Ramsay, Chiesa and Elliott are coming on for Szoboszlai, Frimpong and Koumas. Lovely applause for Elliott.

Konate sweeps a left-foot shot from the left of the box past the right post with Mamardashvili forced into a headlong dive. Liverpool have lost their defensive shape and intensity, allowing Monaco to punch holes through the lines with some direct running.

Nazinho gets round Frimpong down the Monaco left and cuts back the perfect pass to put it on a plate for Coulibaly who hammers a left-foot shot from the right of the D that Mamardashvili throws up his hands to block. That would have stung. Good save. A flag would have meant it wouldn’t have counted but even so Frimpong’s defensive work wasn’t good enough.

It’s been very scrappy since the changes but then Ngumoha pounces on to a loose ball, glides up the right and tries to play Koumas in behind the back four. Sadly, he overhits the pass which trickles out for a goal-kick. Cue an ovation and cries of ‘Rio! Rio!’

Three changes for Monaco with Detoubet, Abline and Camara departing for Benzhara, Coulibaly and Konaté.

Ngumoha has gone to the right wing and Koumas is playing through the middle as a false nine.

Liverpool make five changes with Gakpo, Van Dijk, Wirtz, Tsimikas and Isak departing while Munoz makes his ‘debut’ with Ngumoha, Nyoni, Chambers, McConell and Kerkez.

Liverpool 2 Monaco 2 (Biereth) Mistake by Gravenberch allows Golovin to play a pass into the left half of the box for Biereth. His first shot is well saved by Mamardashvili at full stretch but his tenacity allowed him to get to the rebound ahead of Endo, swivel and stick his second effort in to equalise.

Monaco overplay at the edge of the box, Detourbet, Biereth and Abline playing ‘after you. Claud’, instead of shooting.

A slick, short passing move between Gravenberch, Wirtz and Isak ends with Isak on the deck in the box after Gravenberch’s step-over allowed the ball to run to him. Isak took a touch to move the ball on to his left but gave the defender a glimmer of it and he hacked it away before felling Isak as well as collateral damage.

Quiet start to the half. Biereth just pressed Mamardashvili but the keeper managed to sweep the ball away even though under more pressure than he would have expected.

Liverpool try to play out from the back with Mamardashvili spearing a straight pass to Gravenberch who tried to knock it round the corner for Endo but the ball skidded under his studs and out for a throw-in.

Isak is apparently claiming both goals. Replays are indistinct. He could have clipped it in off his heel as he had a swing at the ball while grounded at the same time as Wirtz.

Our second goal of the game, scored by Wirtz… we think 🤔 pic.twitter.com/FUzA363Oxw

Endo has slotted in at centre-back alongside Van Dijk.

Half-time changes: Mamardashvili for Alisson and Endo for Ndukwe.

For Monaco, Teze for Vanderson at right-back.

Much to admire in that first-half performance from Liverpool’s front six and centre-backs, the latter two particularly out of possession and winning it back. The man-to-man system is working well for them. But they should be out of sight by now instead of leading by only a goal.

Liverpool free-kick on the right after a foul on Koumas. Szoboszlai whips in the cross and Van Dijk gets up first to the left of the penalty spot but bludgeons his header about a foot wide of the right post.

Charlie Adam says the penalty was ‘a soft one’ but Van Dijk did not adjust when Golovin shifted it to his right, stuck out a leg and Golovim understandably decided to topple over the hurdle.

Liverpool 2 Monaco 1 (Golovin, pen) Speared it into the top right. Alisson went the right way but was beaten for pace and power.

The referee, Jarred Gillett, gives Monaco a penalty. It was deserved, too. Golovin went on a driving run down the middle, shifted it to his right and was tripped by Van Dijk.

Liverpool are well worth their lead. They are streets ahead of Monaco.

A microcosm of the game so far: Liverpool pass goes astray, a player wins it back – this time Gakpo – by snapping into a tackle before laying it off to his left for the unmarked Tsimikas to skim a low shot about a foot wide of the left post from 25 yards.

Monaco have done very little since that wee salvo in the opening minute but just now Abline was given too much space from distance but whacked his shot into the Kop.

Big cheer from the crowd for Hugo Ekitike

The impressive Koumas diddles Nazinho with a Cruyff turn but then thumps his shot straight into Hradecky’s chest.

Liverpool 2 Monaco 0 (Wirtz) Pass chipped out to Koumas down the right who arcs a cross to the back post. Gakpo meets it with a header back across goal to Isak whose first effort from a couple of yards is blocked but the ball gets stuck under Isak’s falling body and Wirtz is Johnny on the Spot to stab it in from a 18 inches as Dier tried to scramble it away.

Liverpool have been impressive so far but if there has been a weakness it’s still the balance in central midfield defensively. Going forward both Gravenberch and Szobiszlai have dovetailed together well. They win the ball back when Van Dijk steps out and the midfield two fly forward to tee up Koumas for a shot that strikes Dier.

Chance for Wirtz, who opens his body from the left of the D to try to bend a shot into the bottom right corner but fizzes it the wrong side of the post.

It’s been pretty breathless since the goal, Liverpool dozily letting Monaco through the middle before twice cutting Monaco apart in midfield only for Isak to overrun a pass in the box delivered by Wirtz and then Koumas to shoot over.

Liverpool 1 Monaco 0 (Isak) Chip to Gakpo down the left of the box, he clips it first time back to Gravenberch in the D who lays it off to Szoboszlai. Ping-ping-ping. Szoboszlai keeps the tempo high with return, the one in the one-two with Gravenberch who picks out Isak to bury a shot from about 15 yards into the bottom left corner.

Alex on target 🎯 pic.twitter.com/PT6AYrLxyz

Excellent move from Liverpool, instigated by Ndukwe’s fine tackle on Biereth. He knocks it short to Gravenberch who arrows a 60-yard pass out to Koumas hurtling down the right. He measures his cross perfectly for Gakpo stealing in off the left wing and though he connects powerfully with the meat of his brow, he bashes it straight at the keeper. He was offside in any case, it transpires.

Charlie Adam on co-comms points out that Liverpool are going man-to-man now in classic Iraola/Bielsa style and when the camera goes high you can see it, especially with the full-backs.

Liverpool are carving the middle of the park up with incisive passing. Szoboszlai starts a move that sends Isak down the left of the box. He traps the chip, turns back to face away from goal and taps a pass back to Wirtz who gallops on to it and bends a shot that Hradecky dives low to his left to beat away with a firm left wrist. Frimpong pounces on the rebound and clips a tame effort straight at Hradecky who had quickly restored himself to the vertical.

Van Dijk gobbles up a long pass over Ndukwe, snuffing out any possibility of Biereth getting there first.

Tsimikas is free down the left but overhits his cross on the run when Isak was begging for a cut-back. The left-back went for the back post and ballooned his centre behind, miles beyond Koumas and Wirtz.

Liverpool defend the corner solidly and Frimpong races away on the counter, bombing on to the ball and sprinting into the Monaco half. But his touch is not as sound as his pace and Monaco deal with him when he fluffs his control.

A period of applause in memory of Kevin Keegan ❤️ pic.twitter.com/AkPZG7babe

Liverpool kick off defending the Kop. They roll the ball back to Frimpong who chips a long pass up the right to Koumas who hares on to the pass down the right and crosses, just beyond Isak. Hradecky gathers and bowls the ball out. A mistake by Tisimikas lets Biereth barrel through the inside-right to hammer a shot that Alisson turns behind for a corner.

The crowd applauds in the modern way. My goodness he was a terrific player. Saw him play for Liverpool, Southampton and Newcastle. Absolutely relentless.

Virgil van Dijk has the pennant. Liverpool are wearing all red with the paint splashes of the 1990 kit. Monaco are in a very pale green.

For me it’s a special game, most of the players and people will be ‘it’s [just] a pre-season friendly’, but for me it’s a lot more than this. It will be the first time I have the chance to go out, to feel this stadium and I hope we can also perform well.

It’s a good game for us, because it’s going to be demanding, it’s a team that wants to dominate and they also want to press high so we will see how we are.

I think the cases of Ali[sson], Cody, and Virgil I think it’s their first game. It shouldn’t go longer than 45 minutes, maybe a little bit more if they feel comfortable.

Also for some of the others Ryan, Flo, and Alex, it’s the second game so we have to be aware of those things.

But the league starts in two weeks, so we cannot wait also too much; we have to give them quality minutes.

I think today is going to be a good reference, two games – Monaco and Como – teams that try dominate the game, they are very good in possession, so they will demand us the best without the ball. If we want to control the game and also physical teams, they are probably a very good test.

I hope we are at the level and we can do very good games.

Liverpool Alisson; Frimpong, Ndukwe, Van Dijk, Tsimikas; Szoboszlai, Gakpo; Koumaz, Wirtz, Gakpo; Isak.

Le 𝐗𝐈 qui débutera cette rencontre face à 𝐋𝐢𝐯𝐞𝐫𝐩𝐨𝐨𝐥 📋 pic.twitter.com/2cOYRbzUEN

🥳 Feliz aniversário, 𝐅𝐢𝐥𝐢𝐩𝐞 𝐋𝐮𝐢́𝐬! 🎉Notre coach fête aujourd'hui ses 41 ans 🎂 pic.twitter.com/VTd4BQ5rRK

Alisson, Van Dijk and Gakpo return, Ndukwe continues in defence.

The Reds to take on AS Monaco at Anfield!Watch the match LIVE on All Red Video 📺

Good afternoon and welcome to live coverage of the first of two Liverpool home friendlies after their preseason tour of the United States. Andoni Iraola’s side saw off Wrexham and Sunderland in their first two matches but gave away a two-goal lead at half-time in the final fixture and ended up being beaten 4-2 by Leeds United in Chicago in the last game after multiple changes. What did we learn? Not a huge amount in the absence of Virgil van Dijk, Alisson, Víctor Muñoz, Cody Gakpo and Alexis Mac Allister, the first four of whom are available today other than an ongoing vulnerability from set-pieces and Curtis Jones looking like he is in desperate need of a fresh start.

This afternoon at Anfield they take on AS Monaco who finished seventh in Ligue 1 this season but are under new management with the recruitment of the former Chelsea and Atlético left-back Filipe Luís as head coach. It’s quite the coup for Le Rocher given he led Flamengo to their first Brazilian title in five years, the Copa Libertadores and the Copa do Brasil in his 18 months in charge.

In pre-season so far he has overseen a 5-2 win over fourth-tier AS Saint-Priest, a 2-0 defeat by Sporting Clube, a 2-2 draw with Cercle Bruges and a 1-0 victory over Getafe. They have sold their best player, Maghnes Akliouche, to PSG for £43m and Aladji Bamba to Newcastle for £34m but have so far retained Mamadou Coulibaly and Folarin Balogun, signed and made Ansu Fati’s loan move into a long-term deal.

Iraola may well persevere with Trey Nyoni in midfield who, after his performances on tour, ought to be on the threshold of a breakthrough season and it would be interesting to see him paired with Ryan Gravenberch just behind Dominik Szoboszlai.

Ifeanyi Ndukwe, who played well in America after coming on for the injured Joe Gomez, does not have a UK work permit and will have to go abroad on loan for the season but Jérémy Jacquet, who has yet to feature, was due to have a fitness test this morning and would be a welcome to boost to a squad whose defence still requires significant reinforcements.

#1913. Real Madrid vs Celta Vigo - prediction, team news, lineups

By Matt Law | 19 Nov 2026 11:55, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 11:59

Real Madrid will aim to post a ninth straight win in all competitions when they resume their La Liga campaign at home to Celta Vigo on Saturday night.

Jose Mourinho's side have serious momentum heading towards a period which will see them play eight times before the winter break in Spain halts the season.

There were serious questions asked of Real Madrid following their defeat to Atletico Madrid before the September/October international break, but the response from Mourinho's side to the loss in the Madrid derby has been seriously impressive.

Indeed, Los Blancos have won each of their last eight games in all competitions, including their last five in the league, which has allowed them to sit firmly in the title hunt.

Real Madrid have a record of 10 wins and two draws from their 12 league matches this season, with 30 points leaving them second in the La Liga table, only three points behind the leaders Barcelona, who had been threatening to run away with it earlier this season.

Los Blancos actually have the joint-best defensive record in La Liga this season with only 10 conceded - the same as both Celta and Atletico Madrid.

Real Madrid will have revenge on their minds in this weekend's contest, having suffered a stunning 2-0 defeat to Celta in the corresponding match at Bernabeu last term.

The victory for Celta at Bernabeu last season proved to be their first win over Real Madrid since January 2017, while it was their first league success against Los Blancos since May 2014, with this fixture dominated by the capital giants throughout history.

Celta have been solid defensively this season but have found it incredibly difficult down the other end of the field, netting only 10 times in 12 league matches, which is among the worst attacking records in the division at this stage of proceedings.

That said, Claudio Giraldez's side did manage to put five unanswered goals past Salamanca in the first round of the Copa del Rey on November 13.

Celta's last league match ended in a goalless draw with Levante on November 8, and they currently sit 11th in the table, boasting a record of two wins, seven draws and three defeats.

The Sky Blues are also playing in the Europa League this season, currently sitting 27th in the overall table, picking up three points from their first four games of the campaign.

Real Madrid have been boosted by the news that Aurelien Tchouameni and Bernardo Silva are both back in training ahead of this match.

Tchouameni pulled out of the latest France squad with a groin issue, while Bernardo left Portugal duty early due to an injury problem - both are seen as fit for this match at this stage, although it is unlikely that either will be in the starting side.

The returning Vinicius Junior - back from a domestic suspension - is set to feature down the left, with Yan Diomande, Jude Bellingham and Kylian Mbappe potentially also all starting.

However, Rodrygo (knee), Raul Asencio (leg) and Ferland Mendy (hip) are still unavailable for the capital giants.

As for Celta, all of Ilaix Moriba (knee), Manuel Sanchez (hamstring), Alvaro Nunez (groin), Borja Iglesias (calf), Carl Starfelt (hamstring), Miguel Roman (knee) and Jones El-Abdellaoui (knee) are regarded as doubts at this stage of proceedings.

Ferran Jutgla scored twice against Salamanca in the Copa del Rey last time out, but it is expected that Pablo Duran will be given the nod down the middle.

There is also likely to be a position in the side for the experienced Iago Aspas, who has scored five career goals against Real Madrid.

Celta are capable of making this a tricky match for Real Madrid, but we are expecting Mourinho's side to pick up another valuable three points on Saturday.

#1911. Chelsea star Mykhailo Mudryk in stunning Arsenal transfer admission ahead of Tottenham return

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Mykhailo Mudryk has revealed that he wanted to join Arsenal.

The Tottenham winger, on loan from Chelsea, admitted that before he signed for the Blues in January 2023, he had wanted to move to north London.

He made the switch from Shakhtar Dontesk in Ukraine for an initial £61million fee, that could rise to as high as £89m.

Before he made the move to Stamford Bridge, he had been heavily linked with a move to Mikel Arteta’s side, but ultimately, he decided to join Graham Potter’s Blues instead.

Now, he has declared that his real desire was a move to Arsenal, which never materialised.

“Before going to Chelsea, I wanted to join Arsenal. It’s no secret,” he told the Ukrainian podcast ‘Guest of Gordon’.

“Arsenal were the club I wanted to play for, and moving to the Emirates Stadium was my dream.

“There weren’t even any attempts to make my dream come true and move to Arsenal.

“The attempts from my previous agent were only to earn more money.

“But at the time, I didn’t know about it. I only understood about the commission and all the rest later on.”

Mudryk reunited with his former Shakhtar boss Roberto De Zerbi at Spurs on Deadline Day in the summer transfer window, having been cleared to play after a doping ban for meldonium which began in October 2024.

The winger made headlines on Wednesday when he blamed his country’s football association for his positive drugs test, and ex-Chelsea striker and now-president of the Ukraine FA, Andriy Shevchenko, has demanded an apology from the 25-year-old.

Mudryk played just one match for the north Londoners - away at Nottingham Forest - before suffering a “stupid” ankle injury in training, according to his manager.

He is expected to return to action this weekend, however, when Spurs take on Ipswich Town at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, looking to get back to winning ways after a 1-0 defeat at Leeds before the international break.

#1909. When is Nations League draw? Start time today and confirmed pots as England learn quarter-final fate

England will face Norway in the Nations League quarter-finals, and they could lock horns with a familiar foe in the last four should they make it.

It will be the first time that Thomas Tuchel’s side have played the Scandinavians since the World Cup quarter-finals, where England won out 2-1 in Miami, Florida thanks to a brace from Jude Bellingham after Andreas Schjelderup’s stunning opener.

The Three Lions found out their opponents in Friday’s knockout-stage draw, which took place at UEFA’s headquarters in Nyon, Switzerland.

Tuchel’s men finished top of Group A after a stunning 3-2 victory over world champions Spain in Madrid last weekend.

Luis de la Fuente’s European champions, meanwhile, will take on France in their last-eight clash, with the European giants set to face off for the first time since the World Cup semi-final, where La Roja emerged 2-0 winners thanks to Mikel Oyarzabal and Pedro Porro’s goals.

The remaining two fixtures are the Netherlands against Portugal, and Belgium facing Germany.

The four quarter-finals will take place in March next year, with the winners going through to the finals in June next year.

The semi-finals were also revealed, with England on a collision course with historic rivals Germany, should the Three Lions get through Norway and Jurgen Klopp’s men beat Belgium.

The victors of Spain vs France will take on the winners between the Netherlands and Portugal.

#1908. So much pace and potential, not enough positive impact... surely Scotland must now redefine the role of Ben Gannon-Doak?

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 12:41 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 13:14 EST, 14 November 2026

In an age where much of the football on show in the English Premier League is so robotic as to be almost unwatchable, flashes of individual brilliance are increasingly becoming things to be cherished.

Across his time at Liverpool and Bournemouth, Ben Gannon-Doak has sporadically distinguished himself as someone who can light up a game by doing something out of the blue and out of the ordinary.

As many a defender will testify, that electric burst of pace across a short distance makes him unplayable at times. He has an X-factor which sets him apart from the crowd.

What a shame that injuries have restricted his number of appearances to this point. Since moving south from Celtic in 2022, including a loan spell with Middlesbrough, Gannon-Doak has played fewer than 50 times.

At the very time in his career when he could have done with smoothing off the rough edges, he’s spent far too long rehabilitating from one setback or another.

In the build-up to Friday’s match with North Macedonia, Sebastien Pocognoli spoke about how encouraged he was that the player was finally seeing more game time on the south coast, partly as a result of the team’s maiden voyage in Europe.

Ben Gannon-Doak started in a right wing-back role and had an energetic yet frustrating night

The hope of all concerned was that the recent run of matches which the winger had so evidently needed would translate into a more accomplished display in a Scotland jersey. Alas, this proved to be wishful thinking.

Even against very ordinary opposition, Gannon-Doak’s display proved to be another frustrating watch for the Tartan Army.

Time and time again, he brought them to the edge of their seats by facing up a white jersey and seemingly disappearing in a puff of smoke towards the line. Rarely, however, did the end product materialise.

For a winger with such blinding speed to continually struggle with the all-important final ball is a difficult thing to repeatedly witness.

We shall never know, of course, if the player’s crossing ability would be better by this stage if he hadn’t endured such wretched luck with injuries. But you suspect it’s now just about as good as it’s ever going to be.

The trouble for Pocognoli is that the quality of the delivery from wing-backs into the penalty box is arguably the most important facet of his preferred 3-4-3 system.

When it breaks down, as it did so often against the group outsiders, the whole thing threatens to grind to a halt.

Gannon-Doak's crossing remains an area of concern for Scotland given his wide position

On his record-equalling 102nd cap, Andy Robertson was also guilty of being wasteful on the other flank. Given we know what the skipper has delivered down the years, though, we can write that off as merely a bad night at the office.

The difference with Gannon-Doak is that we’ve rarely seen him tear it up on the flank in a Scotland jersey. So much pace and potential. Not enough positive outcomes when it comes to delivering crosses. In 21 matches, he has three assists and one goal. Those aren’t great numbers.

Just how long do you persevere with a player who doesn’t look to have the requisite skill set for such a specialised and vital position?

Aaron Hickey clearly doesn’t have the pace of the man who he replaced late on, yet he’s hardly a slouch. He is, though, more switched on defensively. And he does know how to cross a football.

It was telling that Gannon-Doak’s most positive contribution of the night against the group outsiders came when he left his station to move infield and take Oli McBurnie’s pass in his stride with the score standing at one-apiece.

His surge towards the goal initially looked like it had been hampered by a heavy touch only for VAR to correctly identify that he’d been impeded by the goalkeeper. He earned his corn in that moment.

John McGinn’s conversion from 12 yards, his second goal of the night, spared Pocognoli’s blushes after a display which didn’t exactly inspire.

That sequence of play certainly raised the possibility that Gannon-Doak could be utilised to better effect in another role.

Gannon-Doak's forward burst led to the award of a penalty and hinted at an alternative role

If played more centrally, his crossing – undoubtedly his weak spot – would not be such an issue. But the acceleration and driving runs would still be there to cause chaos in and around the penalty box. That will always be his strong suit.

To get the best out of him, maybe the manager needs to redefine him.

Any redeployment would, obviously, create another issue. If Pocognoli remains wedded to the current system, it seems likely that Billy Gilmour and Lewis Ferguson will occupy the two holding berths.

Ahead of them, and behind the main striker, McGinn and Scott McTominay are virtually undroppable. It might be the case then, that Gannon-Doak is eventually utilised as an impact sub. Yet, it would not be a plan without its merits.

He’s got a part to play in this set-up. Probably just not where he’s currently being positioned.

You’d be surprised, frankly, if he started in St Gallen on Monday. Switzerland are a far superior side to North Macedonia, already assured of promotion to League A by topping the section and looking to end this campaign with a flourish against a Scotland side they beat comfortably at Hampden.

They’ll ask far more questions of Pocognoli’s side. It feels like a task more suited to Hickey.

Scotland, collectively, will need to buck up their ideas if they are to stand any chance of emerging with a positive outcome or, at the least, some credit.

Scotland fans are desperate to see Gannon-Doak succeed but a little change might be needed

There was a flatness to Friday’s performance, especially in a first half in which the much-vaunted high-press was conspicuous by its absence.

The passing was too safe and predictable. The tempo was low and the play was unimaginative. By half-time, the visitors had fashioned the better chance when Enis Bardhi smashed the ball into the side net.

Scotland were markedly better after the turnaround. After Billy Gilmour’s scarcely believable miss, they were deserving of the opener which came when McGinn burst into the box and lashed home after fine work from Che Adams.

Stemming straight from a corner, North Macedonia’s equaliser – which ended their eight-game goal drought – asked a serious question of Pocognoli’s players.

To their credit, they stepped up with Gannon-Doak’s foray into the box causing the moment of indecision on which the game swung.

The manner of a first Hampden win for Pocognoli won’t live long in the memory. The fervent hope is that it proves to be the start of something.

#1907. Plymouth Argyle vs Peterborough United - prediction, team news, lineups

By Carter White | 19 Nov 2026 11:56, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 20:47

Aiming to avoid back-to-back league defeats, Plymouth Argyle welcome Peterborough United to Home Park for a League One clash on Saturday afternoon.

The Pilgrims were dispatched at the base of title-chasing Sheffield Wednesday last weekend, whereas Posh are in the midst of an on-field crisis despite a recent managerial change.

After missing out on the League One playoffs on the final day of last season, Plymouth Argyle are desperate to crash the top-six conversation this time around; however, a recent result certainly brought supporters back down to Earth.

The Pilgrims were enjoying a four-game unbeaten run (W3 D1) across all competitions before a harrowing afternoon at Hillsborough last weekend, when goals from Billy Mitchell, Davis Keillor-Dunn and Di'Shon Bernard secured a comfortable 3-0 success for Sheffield Wednesday.

Now looking to dodge consecutive defeats, Tom Cleverley's side are currently occupying sixth position in the League One table, just six points behind pacesetters Huddersfield Town and Stockport County in first and second respectively.

The Devonshire outfit are unbeaten across their past three home matches against Reading (0-0), Alvechurch (4-0) and Swindon Town (2-1) in all competitions; however, Plymouth have actually collected more points away from Home Park this season.

The summer departure of fans' favourite Lorent Tolaj to Bristol City has increased the goalscoring burden on Canadian marksman Aribim Pepple, who has netted on five occasions in League One during 2026-27.

In April 2025, Peterborough United experienced one of the proudest days in their humble history, beating a record-breaking Birmingham City side at Wembley Stadium to earn consecutive EFL Trophy crowns.

Eighteen months on, the Posh are enduring a severe fall from grace, with club chairman Darragh MacAnthony admitting that his side are not performing anywhere near the levels expected at the moment.

The form table strongly supports MacAnthony's argument, with Peterborough losing each of their past four competitive matches without finding the net, suffering embarrassing losses to Reading (0-5) and Luton Town (0-3) since the start of November.

Winning just two of his opening nine games in charge, head coach Robbie Savage has failed to turn the tide at Weston Homes Stadium as of yet, with Saturday's visitors sitting in 22nd spot in the League One rankings.

Looking on the positive side, an unexpected victory in Devon could take Posh out of the relegation zone this weekend, with Peterborough victorious on their most recent trip to Plymouth in September 2025.

Plymouth will be without the services of defender Alex Mitchell, who remains sidelined due to an unspecified muscular injury.

The absence of the 25-year-old adds to the Pilgrims' backline issues, with Spaniard Julio Pleguezuelo unavailable because of a calf problem.

As a result, Wes Harding, Mathias Ross and Alex Hatridge are the hosts' only centre-back options for Saturday's clash.

Tom O'Connor injury-plagued 2026 continued earlier this week, with Peterborough's Irish defender picking up another hamstring injury in the loss at Luton.

The 27-year-old is set to be sidelined for up to six weeks, joining youngster Lucca Mendonca in the medical room.

#1906. Who can England face in Nations League quarter-finals? Opponents confirmed

England will face Norway in the Nations League quarter-finals, and they could lock horns with a familiar foe in the last four should they make it.

It will be the first time that Thomas Tuchel’s side have played the Scandinavians since the World Cup quarter-finals, where England won out 2-1 in Miami, Florida thanks to a brace from Jude Bellingham after Andreas Schjelderup’s stunning opener.

The Three Lions found out their opponents in Friday’s knockout-stage draw, which took place at UEFA’s headquarters in Nyon, Switzerland.

Tuchel’s men finished top of Group A after a stunning 3-2 victory over world champions Spain in Madrid last weekend.

Luis de la Fuente’s European champions, meanwhile, will take on France in their last-eight clash, with the European giants set to face off for the first time since the World Cup semi-final, where La Roja emerged 2-0 winners thanks to Mikel Oyarzabal and Pedro Porro’s goals.

The remaining two fixtures are the Netherlands against Portugal, and Belgium facing Germany.

The four quarter-finals will take place in March next year, with the winners going through to the finals in June next year.

The semi-finals were also revealed, with England on a collision course with historic rivals Germany, should the Three Lions get through Norway and Jurgen Klopp’s men beat Belgium.

The victors of Spain vs France will take on the winners between the Netherlands and Portugal.

#1904. Mauricio Pochettino’s first Manchester United training session filmed by drone

Manchester United have been left red-faced after a drone covertly filmed Mauricio Pochettino’s first training session and posted the footage to YouTube.

The Argentine, who signed up to replace Michael Carrick as United’s head coach last week, arrived at Carrington on Wednesday to start work with his new club.

With United languishing in the drop zone, Pochettino faces a brutal opening fixture of his reign, away at Liverpool.

But his preparations for that match have already been compromised in a concerning security breach at United’s training centre, after a drone secretly recorded 12 minutes of Pochettino’s first session with the club, with footage posted on YouTube for all to see.

The drone does not appear to have entered Carrington’s airspace at any point, but footage filmed with a zoom lens shows the session in clear detail.

The YouTube channel which posted the clip followed it up with a statement claiming they had broken no laws by recording the session as the airspace around Carrington is unrestricted.

No players or staff caught in the footage appeared to be aware of the fact they were being filmed. At the time of writing, the clip has accrued over 40,000 views.

The footage shows the United squad working in two groups. One was being put through a rondo on one pitch, while Pochettino led the other through what appeared to be a tactical session on another. Both groups appeared to comprise a blend of first-team and academy players.

Manchester United declined to comment when contacted by Standard Sport.

#1903. Drone operator apologises after Mauricio Pochettino’s Man Utd starting XI for Liverpool test ‘leaked’

A drone operator has apologised for filming Mauricio Pochettino’s first Manchester United training session, admitting that although the flight was legal, his actions were “unethical”.

The operator, behind the YouTube account CC Overview, filmed around 12 minutes of footage at Carrington on Thursday, showing Pochettino working with his new squad ahead of Sunday’s Premier League trip to Liverpool.

It has led to suggestions on social media that Pochettino’s surprise starting line-up at Anfield has been leaked, with out-of-favour Joshua Zirkzee starting up top and Bryan Mbeumo playing in a wing-back role.

In an apology issued after deleting the video, the drone operator, who goes by ‘Colin’, said: “I would like to speak about yesterday's incident. A total error of judgement on my part led to me filming some of the Manchester United training session at Carrington, whilst the flight was legal in terms of drone laws I fully accept it was unethical on my part. My aim was to picture Mauricio Pochettino in his United training kit for the supporters to see for the first time.

"I had wrongly presumed that with it being close to the start of the session that no meaningful training sessions would have started so would have been some harmless warming up shown.

"I also wrongly assumed that the training session would have been open to various media outlets. I would like to apologise to Manchester United, Mauricio Pochettino and the players for my actions and sincerely hope those actions do not affect the outcome of any match.

"I would also like to state that Liverpool Football Club or any other football club were not involved in my decision to film at Carrington yesterday. The video has been removed from my channel.

#1899. Mauricio Pochettino leaves behind a negligible legacy at USMNT... where raised standards never materialized into results as tearful Argentine bolts for Man United

Published: 13:29 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 13:42 EST, 14 November 2026

Perhaps it's incredibly cynical, and maybe too harsh, to call the tears that fell down the face of Mauricio Pochettino 'performative.' But it's the first word that came to mind – followed by 'surprising' and 'a bit much.'

It was only four months ago when the Argentine who had been atop the United States' men's national team since 2024 signed a contract extension to stay on board for another four years.

'We want to try to have a lasting impact on the sport in the country that has welcomed us so warmly and for that impact to extend beyond results on the field,' Pochettino said when his contract was signed.

Yet, after a few months and one international window, that experiment to make a 'lasting impact' has ended. Pochettino may have cried because he fell in love with the country, but it's not like he got fired. Instead, he's off to lead one of the world's greatest football brands in Manchester United.

So now the question turns to the legacy Pochettino leaves behind. Plenty of American soccer writers and fans point to the spirit the former Chelsea boss created and how he helped to energize a team which had been bogged down by past coaches.

But Pochettino's results don't scream success. The World Cup finish was nothing special compared to his peers, his record against the best nations the USA faced was poor and he'll leave as the first full-time USMNT manager in nearly 30 years to not win at least one trophy.

Mauricio Pochettino cried as he left the United States' top job for Manchester United

Pochettino's USMNT played exciting football, but ultimately didn't progress past the norm

But any potential for further growth evaporated when the Argentine returned to England

By all accounts, the greatest thing Pochettino did was install a hungry, all-in-or-nothing culture in a team bogged down by an earth-rocking scandal and a poor 2024 Copa America run.

But he did so in a way that often left the biggest players of the USMNT system behind. Rather than keep a consistent core of his best players around, he seemed intent on tinkering with the lineup in each window.

The results reflect that instability. Leading to the World Cup, Pochettino played 12 games against sides in the top 30 of the FIFA World Rankings. He won just three fixtures – drawing once and losing the remaining eight.

All the while, he was linked to returns to Europe. Pochettino may have said in his exit press conference that he 'never said I wanted to go back to the Premier League' but the Premier League certainly wanted him – especially Tottenham.

Come World Cup time, Pochettino's team finally seemed to gel with a scintillating style of play never before seen in the USMNT.

But it all crashed down after the Round of 32 game against Bosnia when Folarin Balogun's red card was (as this American will admit) deviously overturned. The noise and controversy led to the Americans' embarrassment at the hands of Belgium on home soil.

A summer of exciting soccer for the USMNT followed years of hard resets and mixed results

It all fell apart with a demolition by Belgium, leaving Pochettino without any success

The Yanks were not expected to go much further than the last 16. But branding Pochettino's time atop the USMNT a 'success' on the back of this World Cup performance is giving him too much credit – especially considering the four prior managers to take the US to the World Cup all made it to that stage of the tournament as well.

With his departure confirmed, Pochettino is the first USMNT manager to leave the post without any silverware since the 1998 departure of Steve Sampson, who hadn't been a professional manager before being appointed to the job.

Even though he achieved little in terms of results, players praised Pochettino's leadership and development skills, which shouldn't be ignored.

Middlesbrough midfielder Sebastian Berhalter said: 'He's meant so much to me and he's helped me develop as a player and as a person. And as a player, that's all you can ask for, to have that trust and have that belief in you.'

But not every player in the system was tripping over themselves to play under Poch. Just ask Christian Pulisic, who took the entire summer off in 2025 to rest before the World Cup – only to put up a goose egg in his home country.

Any hope for further progress under Pochettino evaporated when United came calling

All of this being said, there was reason for hope in the future. By re-signing Pochettino, the chance to cement that work ethic, culture and leadership presented itself.

With his extension, Pochettino had the chance to build a foundation in US Soccer to engender future success for decades to come.

Now, that's all gone. Now, Pochettino's time in charge will be remembered more for unfulfilled potential than culture shifting. After all, how do you expect to keep a culture if its chief architect leaves?

US Soccer now is faced with a quagmire of either hiring the biggest possible name again (Guardiola, if you believe the rumors) or hiring someone who will treat the position less like a stepping stone and more like a cornerstone.

It never seemed like Pochettino fully embraced the US, despite the tears on Friday. He'll be off for Old Trafford and a United squad bogged down by perpetual disappointment, all while leaving behind the biggest "What If" in the still-growing history of the American game.

#1898. Thomas Frank calls Arsenal cup gaffe while Tottenham manager a ‘fantastic story’

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

Thomas Frank hopes to not repeat the gaffe of drinking from a rival’s coffee cup after he was reminded of his infamous Tottenham faux pas during his unveiling as Crystal Palace manager.

Frank, who succeeded Pierre Sage as Palace manager this week, came under heavy scrutiny during his time in charge of Spurs after being pictured drinking from an Arsenal-branded coffee cup ahead of their 3-2 defeat to Bournemouth in January.

The incident was the last straw for many Spurs supporters, who had already become disillusioned with the Dane’s style of football, and he was promptly sacked a month later after failing to win any of his next five league games.

Though Frank appeared frustrated that an honest mistake had, to his mind, been blown out of proportion, the moment became a snapshot of his disastrous spell in north London.

Since leaving Spurs, Frank has taken some time out from the game, spending time with friends and family and travelling to Australia and Japan to recharge before agreeing to succeed Pierre Sage as Palace boss.

The time off has seemingly rejuvenated the former Brentford man, and when asked about the coffee cup incident, he appeared in good spirits as he joked that it was a “fantastic story” but one that he did not wish to repeat.

“I hope not,” Frank said when asked if there was a chance he could get caught drinking from a Brighton coffee cup, the Seagulls being one of Palace’s fiercest rivals.

#1896. Wolverhampton Wanderers vs Charlton Athletic - prediction, team news, lineups

By Darren Plant | 19 Nov 2026 12:07

Wolverhampton Wanderers play host to Charlton Athletic on Saturday afternoon looking for the win that would keep the club in contention for top spot in the Championship table.

At a time when the West Midlands outfit sit in fourth place, Charlton's much-needed victory before the international break has moved them into 17th position.

Although some Wolves fans were disappointed with a 1-1 draw at Wrexham before the two-week break, Cesar Peixoto is currently doing an excellent job at Molineux.

Fourteen points have been collected from Wolves' last six matches to keep them one point adrift of leaders Birmingham City.

Furthermore, Wolves have not conceded more than one goal in any of those fixtures, while four points were accumulated from away contests at Bristol City and Wrexham before the international break.

Wolves now have 14 points from eight away games, the second-best record in the division, but they have only scored one goal in four of their most recent five matches at Molineux.

That will be a cause for concern for Peixoto, whose could still potentially move into first place this weekend if results go their way.

Meanwhile, Nathan Jones effectively kept himself in a job at Charlton with victory in their most recent fixture.

The 2-1 win at home to Sheffield United ended a run of 11 matches without success in the Championship, a run stretching back to August 29.

Charlton sit seven points adrift of the playoffs and seven points above the relegation zone courtesy of their win over the Blades.

Despite the London side registering just one away success in seven such fixtures this campaign, that solitary triumph came at relegated Premier League team West Ham United.

Wolverhampton Wanderers Championship form:

Kieran Trippier, Yerson Mosquera and Hugo Bueno could all be recalled to the Wolves defence.

With Fer Lopez and Jean-Ricner Bellegarde both missing international duty due to minor injuries, they are doubts for this fixture.

As Jordan James remains sidelined with a hamstring injury, Tommy Doyle is an option in central midfield, with Marshall Munetsi potentially being used further forward.

Matty Godden is expected to replace Charlie Kelman in the Charlton attack, reward for his decisive goal as a substitute versus Sheffield United.

Oliver Skipp and Harvey Knibbs will also come into contention for recalls, but the remainder of the starting XI could stay the same.

Wolverhampton Wanderers possible starting lineup:

Sa; Trippier, Mosquera, Krejci, Bueno; Andre, Doyle; R Gomes Munetsi, Mane; Armstrong

Charlton Athletic possible starting lineup:

Mannion; McNamara, Bindon, Koumetio, Bell; Coventry; Alli, Rankin-Costello, Knibbs, Campbell; Godden

With Charlton on a high after their win before the international break, they will back themselves to push Wolves, who have not always been convincing at Molineux. However, we can only predict a home win, albeit one by a narrower margin than many people will be anticipating.

There are accounts on social media that track the FPL teams of players and monitor their transfers for hints on team news.

A team that seemingly belongs to Tzolis sparked interest ahead of Arsenal’s trip to face Liverpool earlier this month.

The winger had not played since picking up a hamstring injury at the start of October but he brought himself back into his FPL team before that match at Anfield.

Tzolis also captained himself and when his team then became public once the FPL deadline passed on the Saturday morning, it gave an obvious clue that he would start the game more than 24 hours before kick-off.

He did indeed then start at Anfield, in what was a surprise decision considering he had been out for a month.

At that stage, Tzolis had himself, Riccardo Calafiori and Ezri Konsa in his team. Before the next match, at home to Hull, Tzolis used his wildcard and removed all Arsenal players.

Arteta has confirmed he has intervened and spoken to his squad, and his family, about their FPL decisions, seemingly telling them that Arsenal players are off limits.

“With Christos, with the squad and with my kids as well,” Arteta said.

“They’re constantly asking me about this as well. Because they want to know. It’s a topic. This is again the kind of things that are happening in our society right now and it’s something new.

“We haven’t dealt with it [before] and I wanted to put new things in place. But obviously confidentiality is something critical because it’s about trust and about what you are trying to do and that should be kept as a huge secret.

“We will take measures to make sure it doesn’t happen.”

Pressed on whether those measures had now been taken, Arteta confirmed: “Yes.”

#1894. Mikel Arteta confirms Arsenal plan to combat drones after Manchester United incident

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Arsenal are alert to drones flying over the club’s training ground after footage of Mauricio Pochettino’s first session at Manchester United was captured.

The drone operator involved in that incident at Carrington has since apologised, but not before 12 minutes of the training session was filmed and then uploaded publicly on YouTube.

The United players and staff were clearly visible, as was the shape they were working on ahead of their trip to face Liverpool this weekend.

Arsenal have had a run-in with a drone themselves this season, when their Carabao Cup clash with Fleetwood last month was delayed for eight minutes as the authorities worked to locate the operator.

Asked about the latest incident at United, Arteta said: “Well, very delicate, obviously.

“We had an episode as well against Fleetwood; you see what is happening around the world as well. So I don’t know what the solution is.

“Obviously, the technology is growing, the ability to get into systems is growing at a really rapid rate. We need to be very aware of that, but I cannot tell you what the solution is to that.”

Clubs regularly use their own drones to film training sessions and later review footage.

Arteta confirmed that Arsenal have people in place to ensure there are no outside sources watching their sessions and that the team are protected, but he emphasised that was well beyond his list of responsibilities.

“They are looking after that constantly just in case it happens, but obviously what happened yesterday [at United], it’s a very serious matter,” Arteta said.

“As I said, I’m not a specialist, I don’t have a solution, I don’t have a clue. We have people that are in charge of that.

#1893. Motherwell vs Rangers - prediction, team news, lineups

By Calum Burrowes | 19 Nov 2026 12:39, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 12:46

Returning to Scottish Premiership action for the first time in two weeks, Motherwell welcome an in-form Rangers side to Fir Park on Saturday afternoon.

The Well head into the fixture following a 1-1 draw away to Dundee United, while the Gers extended their unbeaten run in all competitions to 12 matches with a 2-0 victory over St Mirren, leaving them four points behind league leaders Celtic with a game in hand.

After an impressive fourth-placed finish in the Scottish Premiership last season under Jens Berthel Askou, Motherwell secured European football and earned widespread praise for their attacking style of play.

However, Askou left Fir Park over the summer to take charge of Toulouse, with the North Lanarkshire club appointing Swedish coach Alfred Johansson as his replacement, although he has so far struggled to build on the progress made during the 2025-26 campaign.

After 13 Scottish Premiership matches, the Well sit ninth in the table with three wins, four draws and six defeats, having conceded 21 goals, with only three sides shipping more, while just three teams have scored fewer than their 14.

Despite their worrying start to the new season, Motherwell entered the final international break of the year on the back of a three-match unbeaten run, with draws against St Johnstone and Dundee United either side of a narrow 1-0 victory over St Mirren on Halloween.

While that positive end to October and start to November has offered some encouragement to Johansson's side, they will know they must pick up where they left off before the two-week break to create more breathing room above the bottom two and close the gap on the teams higher up the table.

As for Rangers, they appear to have put their difficult start under Derek McInnes behind them, with the Gers heading into the busy festive period in a strong position to challenge for silverware and close in on rivals Celtic in the Premiership title race.

McInnes's side entered the break with a 2-0 away victory over St Mirren, courtesy of goals either side of half-time from Ryan Naderi and Dan Neil, extending their unbeaten run to 12 matches and marking their first defeat-free spell since August, which has also included two victories over their bitter Glasgow rivals.

This impressive turnaround has followed an early European exit and a difficult start to their domestic campaign under the former Hearts boss, but Rangers are now showing significant signs of improvement compared to recent seasons.

At this stage last year, the Gers were fourth in the table and had recently replaced Russell Martin with Danny Rohl, following another difficult managerial spell, while they had also been sitting third 12 months earlier, highlighting the progress McInnes has made since taking charge.

Despite their recent resurgence, Rangers remain four points behind Celtic, although a victory on Saturday would cut that gap to a single point, with a game in hand on the league leaders still to come.

The sides meet for the second time this season following Rangers' narrow 1-0 victory at Ibrox in early September, with the Gers having since turned their home ground into something of a fortress, as no side has taken a point off them there since their defeat on matchweek two.

Motherwell could name the same starting XI that drew 1-1 with Dundee United, although they remain without several first-team players through injury.

Alex Lowry, Johnny Koutroumbis and Dylan Williams are all expected to miss out due to knee, muscle and hamstring problems respectively, although the trio could return by the start of December.

Lukas Fadinger has scored twice in his last two appearances, albeit both goals coming from the penalty spot, and is expected to anchor the midfield while wearing the captain's armband once again.

Meanwhile, the visitors make the short journey south with a longer list of injury concerns, although they at least avoided any fresh setbacks during their victory over St Mirren.

McInnes will remain without Ross McCrorie, Cameron Devlin, Daisuke Yokota, Lawrence Shankland, Youssef Chermiti and Jose Cifuentes, although Chermiti is the only one of the injured players expected to remain sidelined into 2027.

Paulsen; Sparrow, Girdwood-Reich, Moormann, Longelo; Hodge, Fadinger; Maswanhise, Said, Kanga; Palmer-Houlden

Pandur; Sterling, Makhanya, Fernandez, Penrice; Bouanni, Neil, Raskin, Kim Min-Su; Naderi, Kelsy

Motherwell head into the fixture with some encouraging momentum after going three matches unbeaten, but we expect their progress to be halted by an in-form Rangers side, who should secure their ninth league victory of the season and further close the gap on Celtic.

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

Tottenham are set to welcome back a host of players ahead of their Premier League clash at home to Ipswich this weekend.

Destiny Udogie, Savio, James Maddison, and Lucas Bergvall were all pictured in training at Hotspur Way this week and could now be in contention for minutes on Saturday.

Udogie was left out of Roberto De Zerbi’s squad as Spurs lost 1-0 to Leeds before the international break, though the Italian left-back took to social media to suggest he was not injured.

De Zerbi has previously said that Udogie’s injuries were becoming “problematic”, with the 23-year-old starting just two league games this season.

Savio, meanwhile, is in line to return to action for the first time since October’s 1-1 draw with Manchester United. The Brazilian winger has missed Spurs’ last four league games with a muscular issue.

Spurs sorely lacked a creative threat against Leeds. But despite naming Maddison on the bench at Elland Road, De Zerbi didn't bring him on in search of a goal, raising concerns about his fitness.

#1891. Arsenal lose second successive pre-season friendly after parading Guimaraes

Arsenal suffered back-to-back pre-season defeats as they lost 3-2 to Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup on Sunday.

The loss to the German side followed a 3-1 defeat by Real Betis on Wednesday night in Dublin.

Before kick-off, Bruno Guimarães was paraded to the Arsenal faithful after completing his £75m move from Newcastle on Saturday.

But enthusiasm about the Brazilian’s arrival was dampened when Dortmund took the lead at the Emirates inside the opening 10 minutes. Felix Nmecha’s incisive pass into the penalty area was met by the run of Samuele Inácio, who made no mistake with a clinical finish into the far corner.

The Bundesliga side doubled their lead just before the half-hour mark as 18-year-old Greek international Konstantinos Karetsas curled one in from the edge of the box.

Ten minutes after half-time, Arsenal pulled a goal back through Ethan Nwaneri, who scored from Christos Tzolis’s cross. However, moments later Dortmund restored their two-goal advantage as Joane Gadou smashed home from a corner.

Arsenal kept their hopes alive through a Viktor Gyokeres penalty after Tzolis was brought down, but Dortmund were able to hold on to claim victory. After the full-time whistle, there was a penalty shoot-out, which Arsenal won 5-4.

Arsenal still have a number of players to return to action following their World Cup exploits, including Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Noni Madueke. England and Real Madrid midfielder Jude Bellingham was in attendance at the Emirates to watch his younger brother Jobe in action for Dortmund.

As well as Guimarães, there was another addition on display at the Emirates: Arsenal have added last year’s title win to the list of honours displayed inside the stadium.

Arsenal play Cesc Fàbregas’s Como on Wednesday, before taking on Manchester City in the Community Shield next weekend. Mikel Arteta’s side then start the defence of their Premier League crown at home against newly promoted Coventry City.

Arsenal: Kepa (Meslier 46); White (Julienne 78), Mosquera (Ogunnaike 78), Gabriel (Salmon 60), Calafiori (Hincapié 60); Lewis-Skelly (Vieira 78), Havertz (O’Neill 78), Odegaard (Nwaneri 33); Dowman (Ibrahim 78), Gyokeres (Jesus 78), Tzolis (Martinielli 78). Substitutes: Drewes, Lerema, Kabar, Riedl.Goals: Inácio (7), Karetsas (29), Gadou (58).

Nwaneri steps up with the chance to win the shootout and does so with aplomb, sending Meyer the wrong way, and Arsenal win the shootout 5-4.

The former Chelsea man receives some boos as he steps up but calmly slots home to keep Dortmund’s hopes alive.

Meyer goes the right way but there is far too much power on this penalty from Martinelli. Meyer had no chance of saving that one.

We have the first penalty miss of this shootout as Meslier guesses the right way and saves what was a pretty poor penalty from Albert. Advantage Arsenal.

A few stutters in the run-up but Hincapie slots home into the bottom left corner, with Meyer going the wrong way.

He came on right at the end of the game to take a penalty and rewards the decision from his manager to do so as he lifts it over Meslier diving to his left.

Another penalty scored in the left corner. Meyer again guesses the right way but cannot prevent Vieira.

There is a bit of a stutter in the run-up as Reggiani stares down Meslier and sends the Arsenal keeper the wrong way, finding the same corner as Sabitzer and Jesus.

Meyer in the Dortmund goal guesses the right way but Jesus lifts it over him with a quality penalty.

Meslier takes an age to get ready but Sabitzer does not care, sending the Arsenal keeper the wrong way and emphatically finding the left corner.

Right, we are ready for penalties. Dortmund will take first, with Sabitzer to take their opening penalty up against Meslier.

Arsenal have the ball in the net in the final few seconds and think they have a very late equaliser but Martinelli’s effort is ruled out for an offside. Meyer will be a relieved man in the Dortmund goal as he allowed Martinelli’s shot to go through him.

The final whistle is then blown and Dortmund have beaten Arsenal 3-2 to take the Emirates Cup.

It is perhaps not a massive surprise but the game has lost some flow with all the changes both sides have made during this second half.

There is set to be a penalty shootout at the end of this one, no matter what the final result is.

Former Arsenal midfielder Cesc Fabregas is in attendance, with his Como side taking on Arsenal here on Wednesday.

Jude Bellingham is supporting his younger brother Jobe today at the Emirates:

With just under 15 minutes to go at the Emirates, Arsenal are going to make a number of changes. Plenty of youngsters are entering the fray as are a few experienced players like Jesus and Martinelli.

The Swede sends Meyer the wrong way and slots into the bottom right corner. It is now 3-2 and this game is not over with 20 minutes to go.

Tzolis goes down inside the Dortmund penalty area and referee Chris Kavanagh points to the spot. He was caught inside the box and there did not appear to be too many complaints from the visitors.

Nwaneri comes close to getting his second goal of the half. Tzolis rolls it across the face of the penalty area to Nwaneri, who hits it first time and forces Meyer into a good save to his right, pushing it onto the post.

In the aftermath of that Dortmund goal, there are a raft of changes for both sides. Arsenal have brought on Salmon and Hincapie for Calafiori and Gabriel.

Dortmund have brought on the experience of the likes of Sabitzer and Guirassy.

Arsenal had some problems from corners the other day against Betis and they concede minutes after getting a goal back. Arsenal fail to deal with a corner from the right and the ball ends up with Gadou at the back post. Gadou takes one touch before finding the net, despite the best efforts of numerous Arsenal defenders on the line.

Should Inacio have gone down? The young Italian is played in behind the Arsenal defence and has Calafiori all over his back. Inacio ends up losing possession on the edge of the Arsenal penalty area but had he gone down Calafiori could have been in trouble.

Mikel Arteta’s side reduce Dortmund’s lead to just the one goal. Tzolis cuts it back from the left side of the box and picks out Nwaneri eight yards out from goal in the centre of the box. Nwaneri makes no mistake, smashing home and Arsenal are back in this game.

That is good defending from Nwaneri. Just as Chukwuemeka was lining up a shot just outside the box, Nwaneri tracks back and steals it off Chukwuemeka.

White is found on the right side of the box but is denied by Meyer in the Dortmund goal. The subsequent corner comes to nothing.

Dortmund are not far off scoring their third a couple of minutes into this second half. The ball is rolled into the feet of Nmecha outside the box. The German midfielder, who scored a stunner for his country against Curacao at the World Cup, nearly picks out the top corner but it goes just over Meslier’s bar.

Dortmund have brought on former Chelsea and Aston Villa man Chukwuemeka on at the break. Arsenal have made an alteration at the break with Meslier replacing Kepa in goal.

During half-time at the Emirates, the official song of the 2026 Fifa World Cup Dai Dai by Shakira and Burna Boy is being belted out over the tannoy. The World Cup final was exactly three weeks ago today, with three of Arsenal’s players in Spain’s winning squad; David Raya, Mikel Merino and Martin Zubimendi.

Konstantinos Karetsas has arrived. 🇬🇷🇬🇷🇬🇷 pic.twitter.com/nI4A7KPT4o

The first half in north London is brought to an end and it is the visitors Borussia Dortmund who lead 2-0 at the break courtesy of goals from Inacio and Karetsas.

Gabriel is into the book. He is in possession but his touch allows the ball to slightly get away from him. He then slides in to try and retain possession and catches Karetsas.

Two added minutes at the end of this first half.

Nmecha eyes up a repeat of Dortmund’s first goal as he tries to find the run of Inacio into the Arsenal box but this time they cannot quite link up.

After Gyokeres was fouled, Arsenal have a free-kick inside the Dortmund half. Tzolis clips it in and picks out Havertz in space inside the Dortmund box but the German is a fair way out from goal and his header is easily saved by Meyer.

Arsenal want a penalty but the appeals are turned down. It all stems from good work defensively from Tzolis, who drives forward from the edge of his own box and then finds Gyokeres out to his left. Tzolis continues his run into the Dortmund half and is found. Tzolis then finds Gyokeres again, who goes down inside the Dortmund penalty area after a challenge from Gadou but the Swedish striker went down far too easily and that is never a penalty.

Dowman does brilliantly down Arsenal’s right to get past Beier but then goes down just before the byline. Referee Chris Kavanagh blows his whistle and Beier cannot believe it. Replays show that Dowman threw himself to the ground and it was a dive.

Tzolis takes the free-kick and delivers it to the far post, where Gabriel meets it but his powerful header goes over the bar. The Brazilian probably should have scored.

Mikel Arteta has made a change as Nwaneri has replaced Odegaard, who has only recently returned to training after the World Cup.

With it being a warm day in north London, we have a water break. Hopefully they do not catch on after the World Cup. Mikel Arteta is looking pretty animated talking to his side.

What a finish that is to put the German side 2-0 up! 18-year-old Karetsas, who has joined Dortmund from Genk this summer, is afforded too much space outside the Arsenal penalty area as he drives towards the box and punishes the hosts for that, curling a sublime shot into the far corner.

Odegaard slides a clever pass into the right channel to pick out the run of Gyokeres towards the Dortmund box. Mane though slides in with a perfectly-timed challenge to take it off Gyokeres. Mane had to time that right with the challenge being right on the edge of his own box.

Arsenal hit the bar. Dowman does well down Arsenal’s right to drive into the Dortmund box and cuts it back to Gyokeres. The Swedish striker takes a few touches before getting his shot away, which clips the top of the bar.

A dangerous cross from the left comes all the way to Svensson at the back post but he lacked conviction with his header and it goes wide. Perhaps he should be hitting the target.

Down at the other end Arsenal have a headed chance of their own. Havertz clips in a cross from the left and picks out Gyokeres. The Swede is a fair way out from goal and his header goes wide.

Should Havertz have done better with this opportunity? The German is played in down the right channel and has Gyokeres calling for the cross in space in the centre of the box. Havertz tries to find him but Meyer is out to smother it. Had Havertz found Gyokeres, it would likely have been a simple tap-in for the Swede.

Odegaard appears to be through one-on-one but then goes down just outside the Dortmund box. Mane pleads his innocence but referee Chris Kavanagh does not agree, giving a free-kick. If this was a competitive game, Mane would potentially have been sent off.

Gyokeres will take and opts for power over accuracy. It is safe to say his effort is terrible, blazing over the bar and missing the target by some margin.

Calafiori trips Bellingham as Dortmund attempted to counter. If this was a competitive fixture, Calafiori likely would have been booked for that foul.

Bellingham and Havertz are involved in quite the collision. Both players go for the header and Havertz just gets to it first. Havertz is awarded the foul and is ok.

The German side take the lead inside the opening seven minutes. Nmecha slides a lovely pass through the Arsenal defensive line to pick out the run of Inacio into the Arsenal penalty area. It is a clinical finish from Inacio, who slides his effort into the far corner,

Dortmund’s first proper foray forward causes Arsenal issues and Tzolis is forced to put it behind for Dortmund’s first corner of the game. The inswinger though to the front post is poor and Gyokeres easily heads away from danger.

Gyokeres wins Arsenal their first corner of the game out on the right. Odegaard’s delivery into the near post causes problems for Dortmund and forces Dortmund keeper Meyer to tip over his own bar for another Arsenal corner. Meyer this time punches Odegaard’s delivery away and Dortmund clear their lines.

Moments after Bruno Guimaraes’ unveiling, both sides now emerge from the tunnel and we are moments away from kick-off at the Emirates.

Just before the two sides emerge the tunnel, there is a special guest who comes out first in the form of Bruno Guimaraes. Chants of “Bruno! Bruno!” ring around the Emirates as the Arsenal fans get their first glimpse of him in an Arsenal shirt, although the Brazilian is not involved today.

Arsenal: Kepa; White, Mosquera, Gabriel, Calafiori; Lewis-Skelly, Havertz, Odegaard; Dowman, Gyokeres, Tzolis.Substitutes: Meslier, Setford, Hincapie, Jesus, Martinielli, Vieira, Nwaneri, Nelson, Ibrahim, Kabia, Ogunnaike, Julienne, O’Neill, Salmon.
