Reports are that Jobe’s older brother Jude is at the Emirates today, not that Arsenal fans should think that Jude is swapping Real Madrid for the red half of north London.

Arsenal took the Premier League trophy with them to Dublin on Wednesday night and it is on show today at the Emirates. They kick off the defence of their crown on opening night against newly-promoted Coventry is just under two weeks.

Counting down until kick-off ⏰ Make sure you're in your seats by 1.45pm (UK), Gooners - we have a very special guest in store 👀

When Bruno Guimarães signed for Newcastle United from Lyon in January 2022, much was made of the idea that he had rejected Arsenal in favour of a move to St James’ Park. The Brazilian played along with it, posting a video on his social media pages which featured multiple newspaper headlines about Arsenal wanting to buy him.

The Newcastle fans, still delirious about the recent takeover by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund, understandably lapped it up. Their dream was to overthrow the established powers in English football, and the capture of Guimarães was regarded as a sign that they were truly ready to challenge teams of Arsenal’s stature and wealth.

Even the lyrics to the midfielder’s chant referred to the north Londoners, as Newcastle fans sang that Guimarães “could have signed for Arsenal” but chose instead to play “in the famous black and white”.

Yesterday Arsenal announced the signing of Brazilian midfielder Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle for £75m on a four-year deal, with the option of a further year. Here is what the Brazilian had to say:

“I feel good, I feel amazing. I am glad for the opportunity. Since the first time I spoke to (Andrea) Berta and Mikel (Arteta) I was excited. I just felt inside of me that I need a new challenge in my life and I think to be an Arsenal player is going to be an exciting challenge in my life.

“I think after playing two World Cups, I am at the point of my life, I think I need a challenge like this. I want to win trophies, I want to make history and I think I am in the right place to do it. I am so excited to start. We have tough games to play this season so the squad is going to be very, very important and I am hopeful we can achieve our dreams.”

Premier League champions Arsenal continue their preparations for the new season as they take on Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup. Arsenal beat Spanish side Athletic Bilbao 3-0 in the 2025 edition, with goals from Viktor Gyokeres, Bukayo Saka and Kai Havertz sealing victory. These sides met during the 2014/15 Champions League group stages, with both games being won 2-0 by the home side.

Arsenal beat Girona 4-1 just over a week ago but fell to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night. Reflecting on that defeat, Mikel Arteta expressed his frustration at the way his side conceded the goals.

“I am disappointed with the result,” Arteta told Arsenal’s in-house media. “We are here to win football matches. We had some fantastic moments in the first half, the way we played, the way we opened them up. We have to score first, clearly, in the two chances that we had before the score.

“I am very disappointed in the manner that we conceded the first goal, the two giveaways leading to the other two goals. It is true that the finishing quality from them was exceptional, but to win a football match, you have to compete at a different level, especially in those areas of the pitch and that is the learning from today [last Wednesday].”

This is in fact Arsenal’s first game at the Emirates since being crowned Premier League champions, as they sealed the title with a game to spare, with that final match of last season being away at Crystal Palace. After today, Arsenal have two more games, including the Community Shield in a week’s time, before they kick off the defence of their Premier League crown at home against newly-promoted Coventry. The likes of Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Martin Zubimendi are still yet to return after their World Cup exploits.

Dortmund, led by Niko Kovac, finished second in the Bundesliga last season, 16 points off winners Bayern Munich. They have played four pre-season friendlies thus far, winning twice and losing twice. The likes of Karim Adeyemi, Julian Brandt and Niklas Sule have left the club this summer.

#1889. Liverpool: Why Brajan Gruda would be perfect Mo Salah successor

By Axel Clody | 19 Nov 2026 12:41

Brajan Gruda has been one of the revelations of the start of the season with Leipzig and Germany. His profile appears ideal to strengthen Liverpool’s attack.

An attacking midfielder by training, Brajan Gruda is shining at the start of the season as a right winger. After a disappointing spell at Brighton, the 22-year-old German bounced back last winter at RB Leipzig. He has been loaned this season by the English club to the German side. Leipzig will sign him permanently in 2027 for £25.5m (€30m). Gruda will then receive a contract until June 2031.

That transfer does not mean he will stay long at Leipzig, however. According to Sky Sport Germany, Bayern Munich have the Germany international on their shortlist. The Bavarian club have not planned any move in this case, unless Michael Olise were to leave. It must be said that, all things considered, the profiles of the two players are quite similar.

Beyond the fact that they are left-footed number 10s shining on the right side of the attack, they are technical players who are rather fond of assists. Brajan Gruda is the fourth player in Europe’s top five leagues with the most successful dribbles at the start of this season, with 36.

He is very efficient in this area, succeeding with 70.6% of his dribbles, a better ratio than Lamine Yamal (58.3%) or Kylian Mbappe (59.7%), who nevertheless attempt more. Beyond dribbles, the 22-year-old is also decisive, with two goals scored and five assists delivered in 13 games for Leipzig.

Those performances opened the doors of the Germany national team. Jurgen Klopp did not hesitate to give him his first two caps, starting him against Serbia (3-1 win) and the Netherlands (5-0) during this November international break. Gruda shone with a solo goal against the Serbs, as well as another goal and two assists against the Dutch.

His feat against Serbia impressed his manager. ‘It’s completely crazy. The defender in front of him? Poor guy!’ - the German manager exclaimed.

On the pitch, in those two games, his understanding with Florian Wirtz, playing as number 10, was also highlighted. Could the two men therefore be reunited at Liverpool?

Liverpool did not sign a genuine right winger this summer, after the departure of Mohamed Salah. Left-footed, technical and provocative, Brajan Gruda has an interesting profile to replace the Egyptian star. He is capable of long solo runs and of shining in tight spaces, relying on his silky left foot. He is a player who has emerged in recent months.

Liverpool therefore seem to have every interest in quickly getting their hands on the Leipzig player. Indeed, if he continues to perform at this level, his market value, which stands at £23.8m (€28m), should rise considerably, while new European heavyweights, in addition to Bayern Munich, will take an interest in his profile.

In this case, Liverpool have two allies who could push Brajan Gruda to join the English giants: Florian Wirtz and Jurgen Klopp.

#1887. Declan Rice bites back at Graeme Souness: Arsenal star claims pundit doesn't understand how the game has evolved over 'old man's football' criticism - and jokes: 'My numbers aren't bad "for a centre-back!"'

Published: 15:30 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 15:40 EST, 14 November 2026

Declan Rice has laughed off criticism from Graeme Souness by claiming his numbers 'aren't bad for a centre back', after he was accused of playing 'old man's football' and 'cheating' by dropping into defence.

Souness has long believed the Arsenal and England star does not do enough for a midfielder and said recently he might as well play centre back, adding that he would not get a game for the likes of Real Madrid and Barcelona.

Rice is aware of what Souness has said but believes his return of 22 goals and 33 assists since joining the Gunners in 2023 disproves the former Liverpool midfielder's opinion.

‘My numbers since I joined Arsenal speak for themselves,’ said Rice. ‘For a “centre back”, I think that’s not bad numbers. I’ve had a lot of assists, a lot of goals. To be a top-class centre back getting those numbers, I’m delighted with that!’

Rice, who will start as an advanced midfielder when England take on Spain here in Madrid on Sunday night, added: ‘Look, Graeme’s got his opinion. I think he’s had his opinion since my West Ham days. I’ve seen his views. I can’t change his opinion. I can only do what I do, which is go on the pitch, perform, play well and block out the noise.’

Rice also believes Souness, 73, may not understand how the game has evolved.

England and Arsenal midfielder Declan Rice has laughed off Graeme Souness' criticism after he was accused of playing 'old man's football' 'cheating' by dropping into defence

Pundit Souness believes Rice would not get a game for the likes of Real Madrid and Barcelona

‘If you speak about the positioning, the “old man's football”, look at Harry Kane, for instance,’ began Rice. 'We played him the other week and he dropped next to the centre backs 20-30 times to pick up the ball. The game is different now. It's what the game demands, to get away from your man, to go into different areas to create overloads, to create two v ones, to progress the ball up the pitch. Football is way different. It's changed a lot, and you're always trying to look for tactical advantages.

‘In terms of me as a midfielder, I'm constantly watching clips with Mikel (Arteta). He's constantly coaching me on the pitch. How I can progress the ball from deep, drop next to the goalkeeper, go to full back to get on the ball, to take the ball up the pitch.

‘So, I feel like we're now seeing something totally different to what he would see, but in his time football was different. He was a top-class midfielder who won lots of stuff. There's no argument against him. As a pundit, as a person, his career, you have to respect what he's done.

‘I didn't get to see him play, but obviously his accolades were top, and I've never got to meet him in person. If I did, there would be no disrespect. I’d shake his hand. I’d chat with him. It’s an opinion at the end of the day. It’s football.’

#1884. Swansea City vs West Bromwich Albion - prediction, team news, lineups

By Carter White | 19 Nov 2026 12:49, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 16:37

Life without Vitor Matos begins for Swansea City on Saturday afternoon, when fellow promotion hopefuls West Bromwich Albion visit Swansea.com Stadium for a Championship battle.

The Swans have lost their Portuguese mastermind to Ligue 1 following a poor run of form prior to the international break, whereas the Baggies come into this South Wales clash full of confidence.

After being linked to vacant roles at Crystal Palace and Sporting Lisbon over the past month, Swansea head coach Matos has been poached by Ligue 1 outfit Strasbourg, leaving the Welsh side without a permanent manager this weekend.

The 38-year-old's departure comes after an overall impressive start to the season for the Swans, however, they have lost four of their past five second-tier matches, falling to defeat by Birmingham City on November 7.

Collecting just three points from Matos's final five games at the helm, Swansea have slid down to sixth place in the Championship standings after 15 matches, still just three points behind the league leaders.

Alarmingly, a once-watertight defence has conceded 11 goals across its last five contests in the second tier, although the Swans were excellent in their most recent home match, smashing Blackburn Rovers by a 4-0 scoreline.

Former Swansea defender Ashley Williams is expected to join Leon Britton and Kris O'Leary in an interim coaching group on Saturday afternoon, when the hosts will look to extend their unbeaten home run against West Brom to eight matches.

Concerns regarding a potential relegation to League One in the spring feel a million miles away from The Hawthorns right now, with West Brom targeting an unlikely promotion push at the top of the Championship.

Since losing to pacesetters Birmingham on October 10, the Baggies have strung together an impressive six-match unbeaten run (W4 D2) in the second tier, enjoying a standout home success last time out.

James Morrison's troops took full advantage of a wounded Lions pack in the Black Country on November 7, when Isaac Price, Jayson Molumby and Norway international Felix Horn Myhre all netted in the demolition of Millwall.

Yet to be defeated by a club below them in the league standings so far this season, West Brom are currently occupying fifth position, just a single point behind Blues, Middlesbrough and Stoke City at the summit of the division.

The Albion were simply awful on the road during the opening months of 2026 but have improved massively under the stewardship of Morrison, who has masterminded wins at Wrexham (2-1) and West Ham United (3-1) over the past few weeks.

Swansea were unsuccessful in their appeal of Marko Stamenic's red card at Birmingham prior to the international pause.

As a result, the New Zealander is sidelined for the next three matches, including the South Wales derby against Cardiff City on November 29.

Goncalo Franco and Stephen Welsh are both doubts for this weekend's game due to muscular problems.

West Brom suffered a major fitness blow during the two-week break, with influential midfielder Ousmane Diakite picking up a calf injury whilst on duty for Mali.

The much-improved 26-year-old faces at least eight weeks on the sidelines, joining fellow midfielder Toby Collyer in the medical room.

The Baggies are also short on options in defence, with Noah Galves (knee) out of action, but captain George Campbell is available for selection.

Vigouroux; Lissah, Cabango, Seelt, Tymon; Widell, Fulton, Iorpenda; Yeo, Eom, Idah

West Bromwich Albion possible starting lineup:

O'Leary; Pereira, Mepham, Phillips, Styles; Whitwell, Molumby, Nzingoula, Price; Heggebo, Morgan

Rocked by the sudden departure of Matos, Swansea will be chasing home comforts in South Wales this weekend.

Even without Diakite, West Brom should be good enough for a share of the spoils with the managerless Swans.

#1883. Everton dispatch Newcastle to give Matthias Jaissle a reality check

Everton appear well ahead of Newcastle United in their preparation for the new Premier League season after a comfortable 3-1 victory at Murrayfield.

On a sobering evening for new Newcastle manager Matthias Jaissle, who changed all 10 outfield players at half-time, Everton’s one and two-touch attacking play proved difficult to contain.

Everton took the lead through Thierno Barry after a defensive error from Sven Botman, before Iliman Ndiaye scored a penalty that was won cheaply by summer signing Hayden Hackney.

Newcastle’s raft of half-time changes helped David Moyes’s team strengthen their grip further, with Tyrique George adding a stylish third and 19-year-old Harrison Armstrong providing his second assist of the game.

Among the Newcastle players introduced at half-time was 18-year-old Sean Steur, the exciting midfield prospect signed from Ajax this summer. Aladji Bamba and Bazoumana Toure also flickered with promise, but a sharp start from Jaissle’s team faded.

They pulled a goal back late on when Jacob Murphy’s cross found Harvey Barnes at the back post, but they offered little as an attacking force throughout the second half.

Newcastle have two more friendlies, against Bayer Leverkusen and Strasbourg, before they begin their Premier League season at home to Liverpool.

The club are reeling from the summer departures of Bruno Guimaraes, Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and manager Eddie Howe, but David Hopkinson, the chief executive, struck a bullish tone when he spoke of this being the start of “Newcastle 2.0”.

Everton look the more settled side and club, and the performances of new arrivals Hackney and George were encouraging, while Thierno Barry was sharp in the centre-forward position that has proved so difficult for the club to fill in recent seasons.

Everton kick-off their new season at home to Crystal Palace, and keeping Ndiaye at the club beyond the end of the transfer window will be a priority.

The scoreline is a fair reflection of the game. Everton looked sharper, as well as fitter, and there are more positives for them to take. They look ready for the new season, Newcastle need reinforcements.

Alcaraz bends a shot not far wide from 25 yards for Everton. The game is meandering towards its conclusion now.

Willock collects the ball between the lines, feeds Murphy wide right, and his ball across goal is turned in at the back post by Harvey Barnes.

Moyes makes another pair of changes: Keane and Hackney off, O’Brien and Foster on.

Everton fans are enjoying themselves now, belting out Spirit of the Blues at Murrayfield.

More defending for Newcastle to do but they deal with Hackney’s corner delivery. All too easy for Everton to slice through their midfield in the build up though.

That goal had been coming, and Tyrique George is heavily involved again. He carries the ball forward and finds Armstrong, who returns the favour. George shoots on the swivel and picks out the bottom corner.

If I were a Newcastle fan in the stands, Edinbugh’s city centre hostelries would be looking very alluring just about now. There is not much for them to watch in this season half, they are chasing shadows. Some of that can be put down to the handful of young plyers in their second-half XI.

Tyler Dribbling drops a shoulder down the right, and wins a corner off Harvey Barnes. Everton are finishing this game the stronger, there are more goals in this should they put their foot on the pedal.

Newcastle, with some youngsters in their defence, looking a little ragged against Everton’s direct attacks now, but George runs into traffic at the edge of the box. Then Alcaraz is booked for a cynical foul.

Three more Everton changes on the way: Beto, Dibling and Alcaraz on for Barry, Ndiaye and Dewsbury-Hall.

Hayden Hackney plays a one-two with Tyrique George for Everton, with the former Chelsea winger backheeling the ball into Hackney’s path, and there were unheeded calls for a penalty. It was more of a penalty than the one Everton were awarded in the first half, Lewis Miley tripped him.

Thierno Barry’s performance has been a positive for Everton, could he nail down the No 9 role this season? It has been a problem position for several seasons now. Barry is tripped and Everton have a free-kick.

Dewsbury-Hall almost sneaks a shot in at the near post, but Hornicek tips the ball around the post.

Joe Willock with what was very nearly an exquisite disguised pass, but the flag was up for offside against Jacob Murphy.

Then an amusing moment: great cheers from the crowd as David Moyes heads a Hornicek clearance back down the line. He didn’t fancy the cushioned first touch off his instep, then.

Everton have played some quick one and two-touch football around the box in this game, and another move ends with George shooting over the bar. Everton are making their first change: Patterson off, replaced by Rohl.

The game is still finding its shape again after all those Newcastle changes, but Murphy did force a sharp save from Travers with a low shot from a tight angle.

He keeps to his word from before the game; Hornicek is the only player still on the pitch.

The players on for Newcastle are: Woltemade, Murphy, Willock, Barnes, Ramsey, Johnson, Steur, Pivas, Miley and Charlton.

It looks like an unchanged team from David Moyes, so Everton have a significantly more mature team on the pitch now.

Newcastle made a bright start, but as the half progressed there is no doubt that Everton have been the more dangerous attacking force and the scoreline reflects that. Here come the changes...

Everton have a late corner to defend, after another burst forward from Newcastle’s left-winger Toure. Newcastle try one off the training ground but the ball is cleared.

Thierno Barry almost finds the run of Hackney into the Newcastle penalty, and after a sluggish start, Everton have played some slick football in the attacking third.

A sign of some Newcastle frustration there was Wissa kicks Tyrique George across the shins. A bit naughty that, may even have been worthy of VAR attention in a Premier League game.

The Senegalese sends Hornicek the wrong way and finds the corner. No chance it was a penalty in the first place though, thankfully this is not a competitive game.

This is very soft, there was not much of a challenge by Joelinton on Dewsbury-Hall, but the Everton midfielder goes down in the box and is awarded the penalty.

It really should be 2-0 to Everton, a high-class moving down their left with Armstrong dinking a pass to Barry. He squared to Ndiaye who was free as a bird in the middle, but his shot was too close to Hornicek.

Joelinton runs down a blind alley before lumping a pass out for an Everton throw, and then the Newcastle man fouls Barry. The big Brazilian still finding his legs and getting up to speed.

A moment to forget for both Newcastle centre-backs. Thiaw was bumped and unbalance by Barry, before Botman steps out of defence and kicks fresh air against the Everton forward. Great recovery from Lewis Hall, but the ball breaks for Armstrong, who feeds Barry and he finishes across Hornicek.

Ndiaye has had a quiet start to the game for Everton, but his jinking qualities were on display there to beat a couple of Newcastle defenders. Everton lose the ball in midfield, and Tarkowski makes a superb last-ditch tackle to deny Osula.

Half-hearted appeals for a penalty from Wissa, but Hayden Hackney did not do much wrong. Looks like we will be spared a first-half hydration break, despite it being a sultry evening.

Osula skips through a couple of challenges at the edge of the area but fails to pick a pass in the box. Bazoumana Touré has looked lively for Newcastle on their left flank, and Bamba has done well for them in midfield.

Everton shake themselves into life as an attacking force. Cracking cross from Patterson into the box and Dewsbury-Hall’s run had gone untracked, but he was just stretching and could not generate enough power to beat Hornicek.

Good save from Travers to deny Elanga, but it was Mykolenko who made a hash of things in the box. The left back simply fell over the ball under no pressure. Newcastle the sharper of the two teams so far.

Joelinton feeds Bamba down the left wing for Newcastle who delivers a cross into the penalty area. Keane can only direct his defensive header back towards the penalty spot, but Wissa volleyed over with a first-time hit. Decent chance.

Thierno Barry makes it stick and proves a strong outlet for Everton. Botman brings him down at the expense of a free-kick just beyond the halfway line. Then Wissa drives into the penalty area for Newcastle after a one-two but he fouls Patterson.

Newcastle, playing in their lilac away kit, are the team trying to take the initiative with the ball, but Everton are quite happy staying compact and absorbing pressure. Elanga’s corner delivery is promising, but Osula does not connect cleanly at the back post.

Newcastle’s defenders enjoying comfortable possession in the early stages, Everton sitting off in their 4-4-2 defensive shape.

Wissa peels behind Everton’s defence inside the opening 90 seconds but he cannot lift the ball over Travers.

Bagpipes greet the players at Murrayfield, where the pitch has been reconfigured for football. There are only fans in the lower tier, and still plenty of empty seats even so.

We know it is a time in the pre-season when the legs are not that fresh, we train very intense but we want to play with an idea of how we want to play football. Intense with a vertical approach for sure, everyone gets 45 minutes except the goalkeeper.

Big Dunc and Moyes catch up pre-match! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/Jh4APHOZvX

A word that keeps being used about Jaissle is “special”. Newcastle’s hierarchy believe they have secured the services of a manager who will soon be recognised in the elite tier of European managers. We shall see how this view of the 38-year-old survives contact with a brutal and relentless Premier League campaign.

Newcastle XI: Hornicek; Shahar, Thiaw, Botman, Hall; Joelinton, Bamba; Elanga, Wissa, Toure; Osula

Newcastle subs: Gillespie, Harris, Charlton, Pivas, Johnson, M Miley, Finneran, Ramsey, Steur, Willock, J Murphy, Barnes, Neave, Woltemade

Your Mags at Murrayfield! ✊ pic.twitter.com/rDXpn0MqCg

Everton XI: Travers; Patterson, Tarkowski, Keane, Mykolenko; Hackney, Deswbury-Hall, Armstrong, Ndiaye; George, Barry

Here's how we start against Newcastle. UTT! 🔵📺 https://t.co/2VsWpyRq02 pic.twitter.com/vpnLPTRmLl

Newcastle United manager ​Matthias Jaissle is ‌refusing to dwell on the departure of key players that has left his club in turmoil going into the new season, as they step up their preparations against Everton at Murrayfield this evening.

Jaissle was recruited from Saudi Pro League side Al-Ahli after Eddie Howe left last month, with the German coach joining a club who have lost Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and captain Bruno Guimaraes in quick succession.

“It’s a challenge, a big challenge, always when there’s a transitional period. ‌But it’s ‌not time to ⁠complain, it doesn’t make sense to see the negative things,” Jaissle said.

“We want to see the chance in that situation and that’s our approach from day one. We are here to do our ⁠best job. We want to support the players, the current squad.

“There will be adjustments to see in the coming days, weeks. But for now it’s only focused on the daily work, the work we can influence. That’s all that ​matters now.”

The 38-year-old coach arrived in Newcastle ‌having won two Austrian Bundesliga titles with Red Bull Salzburg before leading Al-Ahli to back-to-back AFC Champions League crowns.

He remained tight-lipped about new signings.

“Obviously, in that transition phase, the players who left the club were ‌great ​players, great characters, experienced ⁠players. This is now a vacuum,” he said.

“Either we adjust something in the squad, by signing these players, these profiles, or other players ⁠need to step up and fill ​these positions, these leadership roles. I’m quite optimistic, we can work in both scenarios.”

Jaissle said he had a ​clear vision of how he wants his team to play.

“The phrase how Newcastle ‌should play like is front-footed, intense, ​aggressive and of course also successful. ​In the end, it’s all about what ⁠I can ⁠say and it’s also why I’m sitting here,” he said.

“The approach we have as a coaching team and the identity of Newcastle is famed for, it’s so linked so close together - which is a perfect fit in my eyes and ​that’s going to be exciting.”

The latest instalment of the Seville derby will take place at Estadio Ramon on Saturday evening, as Sevilla and Real Betis lock horns in La Liga.

Sevilla have historically dominated this fixture, but Real Betis have had the better of the recent meetings between the two, losing just one of their last eight contests with the White and Reds.

Sevilla have a record of five wins, three draws and four defeats from their 12 league matches this season, with 18 points leaving them in sixth position in the La Liga table.

Luis Garcia Plaza's side have only picked up one point from their last two league games, though, losing at Getafe at the start of November before drawing 0-0 with Alaves in their last fixture in front of their own fans before the international break.

Los Nervionenses have not managed to finish fourth in Spain's top flight since 2021-22, and there is no getting away from the fact that it has been a difficult few seasons for the club, finishing 12th, 14th, 17th and 13th in their last four campaigns.

However, Sevilla are currently showing form that could see them claim a European finish, which would be a major step forward given their recent troubles.

The White and Reds have won 61, lost 39 and drawn 35 of their previous 135 matches against Real Betis in all competitions, with their last success over their Seville rivals coming at home in October 2024.

Real Betis have claimed seven points from the last three league matches against Sevilla, including a 2-0 victory at Estadio Ramon last season, while they have lost just once to their rivals since February 2022.

It has been a busy opening few months of the season for Real Betis given that Pellegrini's team are also playing in the Champions League; a strong start to their league stage has left them 11th in the table, claiming nine points from four matches.

The Seville team finished fifth in Spain's top flight last season and will again be expecting to challenge for a spot high up the division this term.

Sevilla will welcome Manu Bueno back into their squad on Saturday following a suspension, but Marcao, Peque and Miguel Sierra are again likely to miss out through injury.

Ruben Vargas is also a doubt due to the issue that forced him off against Alaves, which could mean that Chidera Ejuke is introduced into the starting side.

Robbie Ure is pushing to be introduced at centre-forward, but a tough start to his career with Sevilla has seen him manage just one goal in 12 league appearances.

Real Betis, meanwhile, remain without the services of Facundo Bernal through suspension.

Diego Llorente and Cucho Hernandez are also major doubts for the visitors on Saturday.

Troy Parrott is expected to continue through the middle for the away side, while Isco and Antony are also likely to retain their positions in the first XI.

#1878. Goalkeeper involved in fatal collision with Spanish footballer Jesus de Miguel given 12-MATCH ban - and may never return to football

Published: 16:25 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 16:42 EST, 14 November 2026

The goalkeeper involved in the collision that killed Spanish footballer Jesus de Miguel has been hit with a 12-match ban - but may never play again.

FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono has been sanctioned after a horrifying foul with Tenerife's De Miguel earlier this month.

Owono was sent off and the match was abandoned with De Miguel, 30, admitted to intensive care, where he later died.

The goalkeeper was subjected to chants of 'murderer' by Tenerife supporters and retreated from public view amid the significant backlash.

Now his manager Carles Manso has said: 'We will ​give him space so that he feels completely free to make ‌any ⁠decision, whether he wants to return, when, or if he does not want to return.

'When he feels it is appropriate and when ​he feels genuinely ready to take a ​decision ⁠like that [he will do so].

Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono has been banned for 12 games and could quit football for good after he collided with Tenerife's Jesus De Miguel, who died

The striker was struck in the chest by Owono's flying knee as the keeper attempted to clear the ball near the halfway line

De Miguel was rushed to hospital following the incident after appearing motionless on the pitch

'What we have to do is support him in every way and be close to ​him.'

Earlier this month, Owono issued a statement describing his 'enormous pain' following the tragic on-field collision.

Owono said: 'These are being the most difficult days of my life. I am struggling to find the words and find it very difficult to assimilate anything that has happened.

'I feel an enormous pain for the loss of Jesús. I think of him, his family, and everyone who loved him. I know there will be many issues to address; I will face whatever comes with the utmost respect.

'But right now, honestly, I cannot think of anything else except Jesús and the pain we are experiencing. Rest in peace, Jesus.'

The tragedy occurred as the game entered the seventh minute of stoppage time, when De Miguel looked set to race away on the counter-attack for Tenerife in search of a winner.

As he watched a long ball drop into his path, the striker was struck in the chest by Owono's flying knee as he attempted to clear the ball near the halfway line.

After initially rolling around on the floor, De Miguel became motionless, and medical staff rushed onto the pitch to attend to him.

Police are investigating the death of De Miguel due to protocol, and they are also now probing the emergency medical response

Owono said he could not 'think of anything else except Jesús and the pain we are experiencing' (Source: Instagram/Jesus Owono)

Tenerife striker De Miguel died in the morning following the horrifying clash with Owono

Owono was initially given a red card for the challenge before the decision was soon taken by the referee to abandon the fixture.

De Miguel was seen to for over five minutes while his team-mates were visibly distressed, with some appearing to be in tears.

The stadium had been in complete silence while De Miguel was being treated, but as he was taken off the pitch the striker was given a standing ovation by the crowd.

He had become a father just last year, and according to El Espanol, his wife and baby daughter were watching in the stands as the fatal incident occurred.

After being taken to an ambulance on a stretcher, there is believed to have been an approximate 15-minute wait before they made their way to the hospital.

De Miguel is believed to have suffered a cardiac arrest while being transported to hospital and had to be revived inside the ambulance, according to Spanish media outlet Marca.

Spanish newspaper AS reported that De Miguel's team-mates had travelled to hospital after he had been taken to intensive care.

In a statement, CD Tenerife confirmed the striker's death, saying: 'Broken with pain, with a lump in our throat and unable to believe that this is true, from CD Tenerife we communicate the tragic death, this Tuesday, November 3, 2026, at 8:00 a.m., of Jesus de Miguel Alameda.'

Tenerife stated: 'We are with his devastated family, with his loved ones, with all the people of Tenerife who today mourn this cruel outcome'

'There are no words of comfort; there is absolutely nothing to mitigate this feeling full of sadness.

'We are with his devastated family, with his loved ones, with all the people of Tenerife who today mourn this cruel outcome.

#1877. Borussia Monchengladbach vs Borussia Dortmund - prediction, team news, lineups

By Lewis Nolan | 19 Nov 2026 13:23

The next instalment of the Borussen derby takes place at Borussia Park when Borussia Dortmund travel to face Borussia Monchengladbach in the Bundesliga on Saturday.

Dortmund come into the clash in second place with 21 points, trailing league-leaders Bayern Munich due to goal difference, whereas the hosts are last in 18th place with just four points.

Gladbach's situation is precarious but not irrecoverable, with the club's tally of four points five fewer than 15th-placed FC Koln, who are the first team outside of the relegation zone.

Head coach Alexander Blessin has only overseen six games as boss, winning twice and losing on three occasions, but his team have taken four points from the last nine on offer in the Bundesliga.

Their latest result was a 3-1 loss against Hamburger SV on November 6, though they did win two and drawn one of their prior three fixtures.

Die Fohlen may ranks as the division's worst defensive team having conceded 25 goals in nine games, but their return of 12 goals in the final third is the second best total in the bottom six.

While Gladbach were defeated in their first three home matches of 2026-27, they have since won once and settled for a stalemate once at Borussia Park, though they are still winless at the ground in the league this season (W0, D1, L3).

Dortmund could find themselves trailing Bayern by three points by the time they face Gladbach due to the fact the Bavarians play against FC Koln on Friday.

Niko Kovac will be delighted by his side's start to the campaign considering 21 points is their joint best tally after nine matchweeks in 13 seasons.

BVB's most recent result was a 2-1 success against Elversberg on November 7, and that was their fifth triumph in six contests.

The club scored at least two goals in five of those fixtures, and though they only managed to keep one clean sheet in that time, no club has conceded fewer goals in the Bundesliga (seven).

Black and Yellow were beaten 1-0 in the corresponding meeting in 2025-26, losing 1-0 at Borussia Park in May, but they emerged victorious in five of their previous six encounters with Gladbach.

Dortmund have taken eight points from a possible 12 on the road in the Bundesliga this term, while they have lost one, drawn two and won just one of their last four outings away from home in all competitions.

#1872. England boss Thomas Tuchel angry at being dragged into race row after being told by Luis de la Fuente: 'There is no racism in Spain!' on eve of Nations League showdown

By OLIVER HOLT, CHIEF SPORTS WRITER and CRAIG HOPE, CHIEF FOOTBALL REPORTER

Published: 16:03 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 16:48 EST, 14 November 2026

Thomas Tuchel was dragged into a bitter race row on the eve of England's Nations League showdown with Spain.

Tuchel had been asked before England's departure for Spain about England's protocols in case their players suffered racist abuse at the Metropolitano Stadium on Sunday evening.

England players were notoriously subject to racial abuse at the Bernabeu in 2004 and England have not played in Madrid since.

But Spain manager Luis de la Fuente reacted angrily when he was told that Tuchel had addressed the subject.

'Tell Tuchel that there is no racism in Spain,' de la Fuente said. 'Just like in England. We are not racist.'

The row then deepened when a Spanish journalist told Tuchel about De La Fuente's reaction and the England coach grew exasperated with the line of questioning.

Tuchel had been asked before England's departure for Spain about England's protocols

'Tell Tuchel that there is no racism in Spain,' de la Fuente said. 'Just like in England. We are not racist.'

'I was polite enough to answer a question from your colleagues,' Tuchel said, 'and you run and ask Spain's coach and tell them that I talked about racism in Spain.

'I never talked about racism in Spain. I answered a question politely. I never expect racism. The dressing room is the most anti-racist place in the world. This is a perfect example of how you create confusion out of nothing.'

Tuchel had earlier said: 'It's important that the players know about the protocol. And then, yeah, we will give our answers if stuff like this happens. Best answers are on the pitch.

'We had a same discussion before the Serbia game [in Belgrade in September 2025]. There is a protocol in place.'

England midfielder Declan Rice said that Tuchel had not yet addressed the group about racism protocols but that they were clear about what they would do if any England players were abused.

England's game against Bulgaria in Sofia in 2019 was halted after allegations of racism against England players but the game was completed.

Thomas Tuchel has revealed that James Trafford will face world champions Spain on Sunday night, raising questions over Jordan Pickford’s status as England’s No 1.

It was assumed that Pickford, who the head coach maintains is his first choice, would keep the jersey given the identity of the opposition and the chance for England to top their Nations League group with victory here in Madrid.

However, Tuchel will hand Leeds stopper Trafford his fifth cap at the Metropolitano Stadium.

’We want to try and see how far Traff is,’ said Tuchel, who rotated his keepers during last month’s international break. ‘So he gets a highly competitive match. We had some changes in the back four in the last match (2-1 win over Croatia on Thursday), so we went for more stability and more experience with Pickers.

‘Tomorrow is a high-pressure match, on the biggest stage, and it's exactly what we need to see where we are with him (Trafford). Hopefully he's not too over-excited or overly nervous, because there's no need to be. We trust him. But it is different to play for England than to play for your club.

'To have the opportunity to play matches where it really matters is the best way to show up, and to show that you're ready.’

It was put to Tuchel that it would make more sense to play the goalkeeper he believes is his No 1 in the biggest game from this round of fixtures.

’It was the circumstances of the last match, that we had some changes in the back four, and that was the decision in the goalkeeping team,’ he said. 'Jordan is at the moment our No.1. I have a very clear picture in high-pressure moments. He played in tournaments and played for me in the World Cup.’

Meanwhile, centre back Ezri Konsa is also set to start after recovering from a knee issue.

‘I’m very pleased with how he has fitted in seamlessly at Arsenal,’ said Tuchel. ‘It just looks like he's always been there. For us, it’s amazing that he plays on the highest level, competes for every title, is in an atmosphere and in a situation where it really matters that you stay focused and you show up every three days. It's only positives for us.’

PROBABLE ENGLAND XI: Trafford; White, Quansah, Konsa, Hall; Anderson, Rice; Rogers, Jude Bellingham, Gordon; Kane

#1871. Mauricio Pochettino confirms Bruno Fernandes captain decision as Manchester United reign begins

Bruno Fernandes will remain as Manchester United’s captain, Mauricio Pochettino has confirmed.

The Red Devils’ new head coach addressed the media for the first time since his appointment at Old Trafford, as he takes over the reins from Michael Carrick.

United are in the Premier League relegation zone as the Argentine arrives, and he will oversee his new side at Anfield against Liverpool on Sunday in his first game at the helm.

A big issue that hangs over the club is the future of captain Fernandes, who has reportedly rejected two offers of a new contract this term.

The Portuguese’s current deal in the north west expires at the end of the current campaign, and come January, he will be able to sign a pre-contract agreement with a foreign club that would see him depart for free.

The No8’s discipline was called into question as well before the international break, when Fernandes called out his former manager’s tactics in the 4-1 demolition by Como in the Champions League.

It led to the Portugal international being benched for the 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth, but he was immediately reinstated for the 2-0 loss at Chelsea after clear-the-air talks with Carrick.

Now, Pochettino has had his say on the attacking midfielder.

“I think the commitment of all the players is amazing from day one,” the former Tottenham and Chelsea head coach said.

“Bruno is our captain and he's a very important player, but all the player must feel they are important.

“We chatted yesterday and spent three hours chatting in my office with all the players. I missed some injured players, but in the next few days, I will talk to everyone.”

The 54-year-old added that there “would be time” to discuss Fernandes’ contract, but refused to be drawn on a straighter answer regarding the skipper’s future.

#1870. Hutchinson admits ‘dream’ is to be bought by Milan and insists Scudetto is possible

Omari Hutchinson has spoken about his preferred role, while praising the AC Milan fans and revealing his belief the Scudetto is a realistic target.

Hutchinson joined Milan on an initial loan deal from Nottingham Forest with an option to buy. He scored his first goal for the club in the away win over Udinese last month, and is getting more regular minutes on the right side.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

In fact, the head coach Ruben Amorim has even deployed him as a wing-back on occasion. Given the injuries to Alexis Saelemaekers and Samuel Chukwueze the Englishman’s role has become an even more important one than first imagined.

Hutchinson met with fans this afternoon at the Milan Store in San Babila in the city centre. While at the event, the winger gave an interview to the reporters who were present, with MilanNews relaying his words.

How have these first few months at Milan been? Are you raising your game?

“It’s going well, the coach is happy, but I think there’s still a lot to do. I’m earning myself some space… From here on out, we have to keep winning.”

We often see you on the wing. Do you prefer to play there or as a second striker?

“Personally, I like to play anywhere, but preferably on the right flank. Then, wherever the coach puts me, I try to adapt, do my job, and perform to my best, following his tactical instructions. He knows what I can do with the ball. He simply tells me to create and give my all.”

“He talks to me about what to do with the ball and to do my best.”

Why this difference in performance between Serie A and the Europa League?

“It’s hard to say… There have been games where we haven’t performed well due to silly mistakes, but I think we need to push forward from now on and get back on track for the Europa League. We have the right team to do it. We need to win and be at our best in every game.”

What has struck you most about the fans in Italy these past months?

“Definitely the passion surrounding the club. At the stadium, everyone is behind the team. It’s fantastic, I’ve never experienced anything like it before.”

“We’ve got the players, we have a good squad, and even though we’re still missing some leaders at times, I think we’re building on that. I think the coaches and the coaching staff are guiding us very well. Once everything clicks together perfectly, we’ll do great things.”

Do you still see yourself at Milan in the coming seasons?

“It’s my dream. After this season, I hope to be signed permanently. I see myself playing here for a long time to come.”

What’s the feeling of playing in a historic stadium like San Siro?

“It’s crazy. The fans, even the away fans… It’s a unique feeling. It makes you want to give your all for the fans, create special moments, and win.”

What are the differences between the Premier League and Serie A?

“They’re both tough. When other teams play against Milan, they always want to give their all. They’re always tough matches. Tactically, it’s more defensive here.

“In the Premier League, you probably have more space and the quality is probably a little higher, but Serie A is a tough league. There’s not that big a difference, there’s not that big a gap.”

Is there any team-mate you’ve grown close to?

“No, I have a good relationship with everyone. They’ve all welcomed me very well, and obviously it’s easier with the guys who speak English.”

Do you dream of making the national team?

“I’m trying to focus on my club. I want to perform well for Milan and then we’ll see.”

#1868. Mauricio Pochettino has made his first big demand as Manchester United manager

Mauricio Pochettino insists that he wants to be involved in "all the main decisions" at Manchester United.

Pochettino has been appointed as "head coach" of Man Utd, a role he held at both Tottenham and Chelsea, rather than be known as the first-team manager.

The main difference between the two job titles is often considered level of input or control of decisions beyond tactics and team selection.

Mikel Arteta has most notably been promoted from head coach to manager during his seven years at Arsenal, and is widely understood to have a say in almost every key aspect of the club's running.

Pochettino is seemingly not asking for such a level of input, but as the January transfer window approached he has made it clear that he wants a greater say on his players in the future.

"I was in all my career a coach, head coach, manager," he told reporters on Friday. "It does not change too much.

"I know as head coach I am the guy who tomorrow will decide the squad for Sunday, pick the 11, make the changes.

"I know in the future I would like to be involved in all the main decisions that affect the squad. At the end of the day, Manchester United is a football club."

Pochettino kicks off his Man Utd reign at Liverpool on Sunday.

Looking to avoid an unthinkable relegation this season, Man Utd are plotting significant additions to the playing squad during the January transfer window, with a Greek striker supposedly catching the eye.

According to transfer specialist Fabrizio Romano via Football Transfers, new Manchester United head coach Pochettino is set to be immediately involved in major talks at the Theatre of Dreams.

#1865. Luke Graham seizes his chance to shine in Scotland back-line... now Stoke defender aims to make himself a fixture for years to come

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 17:30 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 18:01 EST, 14 November 2026

Whatever concerns there may legitimately be about the limited progress seen in Sebastien Pocognoli’s brief time in charge of Scotland, the Belgian has hardly been blessed with good fortune.

In five matches to date in the Nations League, the manager has not yet been able to select the same back-three in two consecutive outings. Injuries and suspensions have seen to that.

For all that, you sense that even if he’d had a full quota of players to choose from, Pocognoli would still be figuring out his preferred defensive grouping.

This does feel like a time of opportunity for those who are fresh on the scene. Catch the eye and there’s a real chance to become established as a mainstay of the team moving forward.

Luke Graham did his chances of doing just that no harm at all in his first start and second cap for his country on Friday.

Playing in between Ryan Porteous and Kieran Tierney, the Stoke City man made a compelling case to stay there with a strong and diligent display.

Luke Graham enjoyed a composed debut for Scotland as they recorded a much-needed win

On the back of a summer move from Dundee to the English Championship, Graham appears to have taken the step-up to international level in his stride.

‘It’s something I’ve always wanted to do since I was growing up, so I have to be ready for the moment and take it when it comes,’ he said.

‘I think there’s good competition. We have a lot of good centre-halves. Obviously, it was unfortunate for Welshy (Stephen Welsh) and Binksy (Luis Binks) to go out with injury, but that opens up a space for me to come in and try to cement a place.

‘When you’re out on that pitch, you have to do everything you can to try and stay in the team. I gave my all and I’ll just need to wait and see what happens going forward.’

Timing can be vital in football. And it’s conceivable that Graham’s might just propel him to become a Scotland regular.

While playing at Dens Park saw him mentioned in dispatches with regards to a call-up, his move to England, coming just before Pocognoli was announced as Steve Clarke’s successor, has seen his dream quickly become reality.

‘I’ve always said that one thing I wanted to do in my career was play for Scotland, so to get it over the line was pretty special,’ he reflected.

Former Dundee defender Graham proudly belts out the national anthem ahead of kick-off

‘Not much is going wrong for me at the moment, so it’s just about maintaining that and keeping it going every week.

‘I wouldn’t say I merited a start as we have a lot of good players in the camp. It’s up to the manager to pick the team and, luckily, he gave me the chance.

‘He just said to go out and enjoy it and do what you’re doing every week at Stoke. I think I did all right.’

Notwithstanding how limited the North Macedonians were on the night, Pocognoli was entitled to take encouragement from the way the back three acquitted themselves.

Playing closer to each other than we’d seen in the previous matches, they were rarely unpicked by balls through the middle. Angus Gunn was not overworked in goal. Tellingly, the only concession of the night came when Scott McTominay lost his man at a corner.

‘I think a lot of it is just being brave,’ Graham reflected. ‘It’s about bravery in going man-to-man with the striker, being brave on the ball, trying to break the lines and keeping possession.

‘So, I think bravery is the main thing and concentration as well.’

Graham keeps a close eye on North Macedonian danger man Elmin Rastoder at Hampden

With the defence solid enough, Pocognoli had a platform for a much-needed win. While the narrow scoreline made the final moments more anxious than they should have been, on balance, Scotland were deserved winners.

‘It’s just about winning games at this stage of the competition, so that was good,’ said Graham. ‘I think, if I’m being harsh, we should have killed the game off before it got to 1-1. We had a few good chances to put them to bed.

‘Then we kinda shot ourselves in the foot by conceding from a set piece. But Ben Gannon-Doak does well for the penalty and for us to go 2-1 up and see it out was good.’

No one would dispute that the display was a long way from perfect. There’s significant room for improvement ahead of the concluding group match with Switzerland on Monday.

‘We’re going through a bit of a transitional spell at the minute, so it’s not going to be all smooth sailing from the get-go,’ Graham said. ‘It’s about adjusting and trying to build on performances in every game. I think it’s going to take time.

‘It’s a different style, a different manager and we just have to keep being patient. You look at the squad now and there’s a lot of new, young players coming through. It’s just about encouraging us young boys and showing we can get a place in the squad.

‘It is going to take time but, once we get there, we’re going to do really well and compete right at the top of the game.’

Graham has been a huge success in Stoke's flying start to the Championship season

Graham does look like he’s moving in the right direction. From watching Scotland compete at the World Cup on licensed premises five months ago, he hopes he too can be the toast of the nation one day.

‘I didn’t go. It was too expensive for me,’ he explained. ‘I think I was just like everyone else, watching in the pub with their mates. It was pretty amazing and hopefully I can be part of something like that one day.

‘I wasn’t too far away (previously), I think. Steve Clarke, the former manager, told me that. It’s just about trusting myself now and hopefully getting there one day.

‘There’s been a lot of hard work and dedication which has led me to this point. I’m very grateful to a lot of people who have helped me in my career so far and just to get this chance is amazing.’

#1864. Brian Madjo, 17, electrifies Villa despite Super Cup defeat by PSG

Unai Emery’s Aston Villa 2.0 remain under construction but from the wreckage of a difficult summer there has emerged a potential star for the future.

Emery may have now suffered four successive defeats in the Super Cup, yet the big positive from a balmy night in Salzburg was the performance of teenage forward Brian Madjo. Aged 17 years and 212 days, Madjo became the youngest player to start and score in this continental showpiece, just over a week after he was given permission to play for his club.

Signed from Metz for £10m in January, Madjo had been prevented from playing because of Fifa’s rules on the international transfer of minors. Villa’s appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport to have him registered was upheld on August 4 and what a prospect he appears.

Born in Enfield but raised in Luxembourg, there has been a huge buzz around him since his arrival in the new year.

Paris St-Germain have produced an abundance of talented teenagers over the years and Madjo did not look out of place here.Désiré Doué’s second-half strike secured PSG the Super Cup – contested by the winners of the Champions League and Europa League – for the second successive year, but Emery will have seen enough to give him renewed confidence.

Desire Doue puts PSG 2-1 ahead despite originally being flagged offside 🫣📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/vnMIZCWJaj

His team played with all the resilience and bravery that has become a trademark, epitomised by the powerful Madjo and another teenager in midfielder George Hemmings.

Emery said: “Brian has scored goals for us in pre-season and has shown his capacity to work in our idea. I am so happy because the young players were involved in our work and not playing last season.

“Of course there is still work to do but they showed they can play with us. They have responded fantastically and will then feel the confidence. With a loss you can never be happy but overall I am proud of all the players and everything we’ve done. Some changes will be needed but we’re confident.”

This was a fine Villa performance to silence the doom merchants who have been fearing a troubled season. After the painful sales of Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne, Villa are clearly a team in transition. They are operating under restrictions to comply with Uefa’s financial rules and there is still the possibility of another important player leaving before the transfer deadline day.

England centre-back Ezri Konsa remains a priority target for Premier League champions Arsenal, and was absent here. Konsa, Emiliano Martínez and Ollie Watkins were all granted extended leave after their participation in the World Cup, which has done little to ease the fears of supporters over more departures. The trio will return to training this weekend.

While some outsiders are predicting a difficult season for Villa, do not bother telling Emery. He has turned putting noses out of joint into an art form since sweeping into Villa Park and with him around anything feels possible.

The Basque remains optimistic about the future and those hopes will only have been underlined by the performance of Madjo. He bullied PSG centre-back Willian Pacho for much of the evening and even managed to steal the limelight from PSG’s magician Khvicha Kvaratskhelia.

Hemmings, 19, has emerged from the academy and already made a real impression on his manager. Despite the high regard for those youngsters, this always appeared likely to be a tough proposition against a full-strength PSG team. Indeed, before this game in Salzburg only 39 per cent of Europa League winners have beaten their Champions League rivals in this fixture.

The French champions did start slowly, but had been cranking up the pressure before taking a 20th minute lead with a spectacular strike from their Georgian superstar.

Doué forced a save from Marco Bizot and, after Villa failed to clear, the loose ball landed in the path of Kvaratskhelia, who cut inside on the left to his right foot before smashing a shot into the roof of the net.

Khvicha Kvaratskhelia puts PSG 1-0 ahead vs Aston Villa 🔥📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/BIf8njpaSx

It was a strike of sheer power and accuracy, catching Bizot by surprise. PSG briefly appeared in control, but Villa responded superbly. In 17 minutes they created six goal-scoring chances before the outstanding Madjo finally made one of them count.

Before his goal, he had narrowly missed the target twice with a pair of headers from John McGinn’s crosses. Villa also had another opportunity 10 minutes before half-time, when Pacho’s mistake allowed Hemmings to run from the centre circle unopposed. As he entered the penalty area, the PSG defenders had raced back to recover and a promising moment ended with Madjo curling a shot wide.

Brian Madjo with a big chance to put Aston Villa level 😮📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/pqsC5Hor15

PSG goalkeeper Matvey Safonov then produced his first save just before the break, turning away Boubacar Kamara’s close-range header. Villa did carve out another golden chance when Madjo’s strength took hm past Pacho, but he hit the outside of the post. Madjo’s moment did come, though, as he once again bullied Pacho to divert a McGinn cross into the roof of the net.

Brian Madjo at 17-years-old scores in the UEFA Super Cup Final 🤯📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/PccX7FxjAr

Villa were buoyant, but it was PSG who scored the crucial second goal after Doué was awarded the goal following a VAR review. Doué was sent clear down the right by substitute Ousmane Dembélé and confidently beat Bizot, with reviews concluding that he had been played onside by Matty Cash.

The game was refereed by Omar Artan, the Somali referee who was supposed to officiate at the World Cup but was denied entry to the United States.

It became rather fractious as time began to tick away, with McGinn booked after complaining over the placement of a free-kick. Madjo was replaced by Tammy Abraham with 17 minutes left and this will be an evening he will never forget.

PSG (4-3-3): Safonov, Hakimi, Marquinhos, Pacho, Mendes (Hernandez 75), Neves (Ruiz 75), Vitinha, Emery, Akliouche, (Dembele 45), Doue (Mayulu 87), Kvaratskhelia (Buraldo 88).Substitutes: Chevalier (g), Zabarnyi, Digne, Fernandez, Barcola, Ndjantou, Mbaye.Villa (4-2-3-1): Bizot, Cash, Lindelof, Torres (Mings 80), Maatsen, Kamara (Bogarde 72), Gomes (Barkley 79), McGinn 7 (Alysson 73), Buendia, Hemmings, Madjo (Abraham 72).Substitutes: Wright (g), Asemota (g), Barkley, Nedeljkovic, Cisse, Rowe, Burrowes, Lynch.Booked: Gomes, Torres, McGinn.Referee: Omar Artan (Somalia).

After the officials and the Aston Villa players receive their medals, it is time for the 2026 Uefa Super Cup winners PSG to receive their medals. The last man up is their captain Marquinhos, who has won a staggering 40 trophies during his time at PSG. He takes the trophy from Uefa President Aleksander Ceferin and lifts it above his head alongside his teammates.

PSG are your 2026 UEFA Super Cup Champions 🏆📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/1qCKEQ0IPK

Both Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye have been heavily linked with moves to Liverpool this summer and neither player came off the bench for PSG tonight. Does that indicate that potentially those moves could be close, with neither played risked of picking up an injury?

Luis Enrique has now won 13 trophies with PSG. Serial winner 🏆 pic.twitter.com/RAsyI1Ui2s

💬 "We are ALWAYS hungry you know... we want more, we want more" Désiré Doué reflects on PSG's UEFA Super Cup Final win.📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nwreU1Skz7

Aston Villa will take on Borussia Mönchengladbach on Saturday in their final game of pre-season before they take on Brighton on the south coast on the opening weekend of the new Premier League season.

PSG play Lens in the Trophée des Champions on Sunday before they kick off the defence of their Ligue 1 crown at home against Rennes.

Possession: PSG 61%- Aston Villa 39%Shots: 12-15Shots on target: 6-4Corners: 0-2Touches in opposition box: 29-34

Buendia has a late chance to equalise for Aston Villa from Maatsen’s cross but his header goes wide.

Not long after, the final whistle goes and PSG win the Super Cup for the second straight year. Last year they beat Tottenham on penalties, this time they beat Aston Villa 2-1. Unai Emery’s side acquitted themselves well and will regret some of their missed chances tonight. An entertaining affair in Salzburg.

PSG win back-to-back UEFA Super Cup's following goals from Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue 🏆📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/vzMx6rGjuo

Dembele feeds a pass into the Villa box looking to pick out the run of Hakimi but there is slightly too much on it and Bizot is out to gather.

Into the final minute of added time we go.

Aston Villa are running out of time to find a late equaliser.

Maatsen brings Dembele down not far outside the Aston Villa box but play goes on as the latter gets up and shoots, with his effort saved by Bizot.

One final change for PSG as their other goalscorer tonight, Kvaratskhelia, is replaced by Beraldo. A defender comes on for an attacker as Luis Enrique’s side look to hold on for the victory.

Mayulu is coming on for Doue, whose goal may well have won back-to-back Super Cups for PSG.

The ball falls to Kvaratskhelia on the right side of the box and the Georgian chips it over Bizot but Cash is on hand to clear. Aston Villa then counter and Abraham feeds a pass forward at the perfect time to pick out the run of Alysson into the PSG box. Alysson then plays it across the six-yard box but neither Abraham nor Maatsen are there to meet the cross.

Double change for Aston Villa as Barkley and Mings replace Gomes and Torres, who were both on yellow cards.

Alysson, only just on the pitch, does brilliantly down Aston Villa’s right and drives into the PSG penalty area. His cross is parried away by Safonov straight into the path of Gomes, whose shot is blocked by Zaire-Emery.

PSG are making a double substitution as Ruiz and L Hernandez come on. Neves and Mendes, who had been struggling with cramp, go off.

Aston Villa are going to make a triple change as Abraham, Alysson and Bogarde come on. 17-year-old Madjo is one of those to be replaced as is McGinn, who has been booked as he goes off. The Aston Villa captain is distinctly unimpressed with the officials.

The space opens up for Mendes to take on the shot from range and he obliges, forcing Bizot into a decent save. Kvaratskhelia is unable to make contact with the follow-up. Mendes seems to be struggling with some cramp.

We are nearly 70 minutes into the game but Unai Emery has still not turned to his bench yet.

Aston Villa have an immediate chance to equalise through Hemmings but the 19-year-old’s effort from inside the box is straight at Safonov. That was a big chance for Hemmings.

Down the other end, Gomes is booked for a challenge from behind on Doue.

The VAR has checked it and there was no offside so the original decision is overturned and the goal is given. Doue is played in behind by Dembele down the right channel and is played onside by Cash on the far side. Doue takes it into the Villa penalty area and gets it onto his left foot. He curls it past Bizot and into the far corner.

Desire Doue puts PSG 2-1 ahead despite originally being flagged offside 🫣📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/vnMIZCWJaj

Doue has the ball in the Aston Villa net but the offside flag has gone up. However, has Cash played Doue onside?

Cash’s cross from the right picks out Buendia at the front post but the latter’s header is off target. Unai Emery will be pretty happy with his side’s performance through the hour mark.

Mendes is a touch fortunate not to be penalised for a foul on McGinn as the Aston Villa captain spun the Portuguese defender on halfway. The referee must have thought both players had a hold of each other but I would lean towards Mendes probably fouling McGinn.

Other than 10/15 minutes in and around Kvaratskhelia’s goal, Aston Villa have put in a good performance and have created more chances than PSG. If anything, it will be Villa who will be disappointed that they have not scored more than once.

Just inside the PSG penalty area, McGinn cuts onto his left to get his shot away and his deflected effort is saved by Safonov diving to his right.

One of Aston Villa’s coaches has been booked for some protestations after Torres is penalised for a foul on Doue. Torres is also booked for that challenge.

Two of Aston Villa’s best players tonight thus far have been teenagers; 19-year-old Hemmings and 17-year-old Madjo. Aston Villa have seen some key, senior players depart this summer but will take joy from the performances of this pair.

Luis Enrique has decided he needed to make a change at the break as Dembele replaces Akliouche, who was quiet on his official debut for PSG after his move from Monaco.

Incredible to think he is only 17 years and 212 days old. He’s been all over PSG centre-back Willian Pacho and thoroughly deserves his goal.

The teenager could even have had a hat-trick. What a second-half this could be.

Madjo has managed to steal the limelight from PSG’s Georgian magician Kvicha Kvaratskhelia, which is quite some achievement.

Possession: PSG 67%-33% Aston VillaShots: 6-10Shots on target: 2-2Corners: 0-2Touches in opposition box: 11-17

After one added minute, the first half is brought to an end and we are all square at 1-1 in Salzburg. Kvaratskhelia had put PSG in front but Madjo’s goal on the stroke of half-time has Aston Villa level at the break.

On the stroke of half-time, the 17-year-old levels for Aston Villa and finally takes his fourth big chance of the night. It is perhaps the hardest chance he has had as McGinn’s cross comes all the way to the back post. Madjo is being held by Pacho but somehow gets his foot to it and his shot goes into the roof of the net. What a moment for the 17-year-old!

Brian Madjo at 17-years-old scores in the UEFA Super Cup Final 🤯📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/PccX7FxjAr

Madjo has his third massive chance of this first half and this shot comes off the post. Buendia feeds a pass forward into the path of Madjo, who appeared to be blocked by Pacho but he outmuscles him. Madjo then fires towards goal but it strikes the outside of the post. In a parallel universe, Madjo could have ahd a first-half hat-trick.

Aston Villa have had a few great chances in this first half and there is another. A free-kick into the PSG penalty area causes issues for the French side and Kamara’s header towards goal is saved by Safonov.

Madjo has his second huge chance of this first half. Once more it is McGinn who provides the cross. The Scot does really well on the right side of the box to fake the cross with his left and instead delivers with his right. He picks out Madjo at the back post and the 17-year-old should score but his header misses the target. What a story it would have been had the 17-year-old scored two goals against the Champions League winners.

Aston Villa have just settled things down. Either side of Kvaratskhelia’s goal, they were on the ropes but have calmed things down.

Hemmings is played in and he could potentially have gone down twice under challenges from Hakimi and then Mendes. The ball then falls to 17-year-old Madjo on the left side of the box. He opens up his body and tries to curl into the far corner but his effort goes wide.

Referees are now hot on players taking too long over throw-ins, with Mendes falling foul of that. That is one of the fairly new rules that will be good for the game.

A huge chance for 17-year-old Madjo to equalise. McGinn picks out the young striker with a sublime cross from the right. Madjo is just eight yards out and has a free header but it goes just wide of the far post. Aston Villa should be level.

Brian Madjo with a big chance to put Aston Villa level 😮📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/pqsC5Hor15

After Aston Villa had made a solid start to this game, it is all PSG right now and Villa are on the ropes at the moment. PSG work it beautifully down their left after a sublime one-two between Mendes and Kvaratskhelia. Mendes drives down the left wing and has a cross into the box first-time which he declines. The Portuguese defender then has four different teammates that he could pick out in the penalty area but his cross misses all four.

PSG want a penalty. Kvaratskhelia shows great feet out on the left to drive into the Aston Villa penalty area. Gomes is on his back and Kvaratskhelia goes down. It did look like he was always looking to go down and it would have been very soft.

A few minutes after I said that Aston Villa had done a decent job of keeping PSG at bay, Luis Enrique’s side take the lead. Bizot had just made a great reflex save to deny Doue but he is unable to stop Kvaratskhelia’s effort. The Georgian cuts inside onto his right just inside the Aston Villa penalty area and gets his shot away quickly after quick feet. There is great venom on the shot and it beats Bizot, who thought Kvaratskhelia was going to go for the far corner but instead hit it at the near post. Could Bizot have saved that? Perhaps but Kvaratskhelia did belt that shot.

Khvicha Kvaratskhelia puts PSG 1-0 ahead vs Aston Villa 🔥📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/BIf8njpaSx

As you would expect, PSG are dominating possession but thus far have been unable to create any genuine chances, much to Aston Villa’s credit. But, with the players PSG have at their disposal, they can cause chaos in a moment.

Tensions just start to simmer. McGinn gives a foul away on Mendes, who then attempts to take the free-kick a good few yards further forward from where it was. McGinn repeatedly tries to stop Mendes from taking it further forward before the referee steps in to end the dispute.

Moments later, Kamara decides to shoot from range and his low, driving effort goes wide of Safonov’s right post. With Onana injured long-term and Tielemans now at Manchester United, Kamara’s importance to Aston Villa is even higher.

In last year’s Super Cup, PSG were stunned in the first hour against Tottenham as went 2-0 down before coming back to win on penalties. PSG have played fewer friendlies than Aston Villa up until this point so there may be a little more rustiness in Luis Enrique’s side than Unai Emery’s.

This is going to be a very tall order for Aston Villa, who look very different tonight to how they ended last season, up against a team of PSG’s calibre. Not only have Villa sold some key players like Rogers and Tielemans but the likes of Konsa and Watkins are yet to return after the World Cup.

McGinn is afforded too much space and time to cut onto his left foot out on the right and whip a dangerous cross towards the far post. Pacho is on hand to head away with a great defensive header.

Moments later, good work from Maatsen out on the left earns Aston Villa a corner. Unai Emery’s side have made a decent start to this game. Buendia’s delivery into the near post is headed away by Marquinhos.

We are under way in Salzburg, where it has been a very hot day but the temperature has cooled a touch with the sun having set in Austria.

Some huge banners are on display on the pitch, displaying not only the emblems of the two clubs but also images of the trophy lifts that have earned these sides a place in tonight’s game. Both sides emerge from the tunnel, past the trophies they won with the two captains carrying them out, and we are moments away from kick-off in Salzburg. Here is a reminder of how the sides line up tonight:

Aston Villa: Bizot, Cash, Lindelof, Torres, Maatsen, Joao Gomes, Kamara, Hemmings, Buendia, McGinn, Madjo.Substitutes: Wright, Asemota, Mings, Barkley, Abraham, Bogarde, Nedeljkovic, Alysson, Cisse, Rowe, Burrowes, Lynch.

💬 " I am confident they're going to play today with the level we need" Unai Emery on the inclusion of João Gomes and Brian Madjo into Aston Villa's lineup. 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/FCjBmGDcNo

Lucas Digne has only just swapped Aston Villa for PSG in recent days but he already comes up against his old teammates. He is on the bench for PSG tonight and could offer some good insight into Unai Emery’s side.

PSG forwards Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye have both been linked with moves to Liverpool this summer and both are on the bench for PSG tonight. As PSG close in on moves for Ferran Torres and Mika Godts, could Liverpool’s moves for Barcola and Mbaye accelerate in the next few days? Barcola has only recently returned to training after the World Cup and is joined on the bench by compatriot Ousmane Dembele. Maghnes Akliouche, who has joined PSG from Monaco this summer, starts tonight.

Brian Madjo is just 17-years-old but he starts up top for Aston Villa tonight against the Champions League winners, with Ollie Watkins yet to return after the World Cup.

“There is a lot of change but when you look at other clubs in England, there is a lot of change. What we have still is our main core, same manager, same methods and same desire to achieve more. A lot thought we reached our ceiling a few seasons ago and we proved them wrong. As long as we have that hunger to achieve more, Aston Villa fans can expect as much as possible.”
