#1825. Arsenal hunger is ominous for rivals as they dismantle Man City

Was it the early goal that should have put Arsenal’s rivals on red alert? No. While Ricardo Calafiori’s intervention was dramatic, it wasn’t that. Was it the seamless introduction of the new signings, then? No, it wasn’t that either, despite the excellence of Bruno Guimarães and Christos Tzolis.

How about the emphatic scoreline – surely that was it? Again, the answer is no. Three unanswered goals against Manchester City will always grab a headline, but scorelines do not always define the nature of a performance or a team’s capabilities.

So what was it that should have those with pretensions of ripping Arsenal’s crown from their grasp shuffling uncomfortably? One word: hunger. The reason this was such an ominous afternoon for the chasing pack is the fact Mikel Arteta’s team played with intensity of a team with everything to prove.

Title wins can sometimes sate ambition. Players don’t always want to climb the same mountain again, not least if reaching the peak was initially so draining, but everywhere you looked on a day when Cardiff was painted red and white was evidence that Arsenal remain ravenous for success.

First Guimarães pounced out of the shadows to mug Jérémy Doku, leaving him in a heap. Then there was Gabriel Magalhães thundering into a befuddled Doku, celebrating in front of City’s fans as if he had scored, before Ben White flung himself in front of the Belgian, denying a clear-cut scoring opportunity.

Ben White to the rescue with an incredible block 🦸📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ZK0cNnFz5N

Another notable incident was Martin Odegaard, not long after he had glossed a fabulous display with a third goal, sprinting 30 yards to spook Gianluigi Donnarumma and make the Italian hurry his clearance. The victory was good, the trophy was nice, but the energy heartened Arteta more than anything.

“They are really good examples,” Arteta said. “The way the team tracks back is unbelievable, especially when, fitness-wise, we aren’t there yet. We had desire and composure on the ball. When you put your soul and your heart into every action, this is what happens. We want to do it again.

“The desire comes from them thinking: ‘I want to live that moment again. I want to have all the moments again and I want them to be even bigger.’ We know what it is going to take. We have never done it [retain the Premier League] at this football club. We know it will demand something special.”

You could flip that and say it will take something special from the chasers. George Graham and Arsène Wenger could never hold on to the biggest prize during their reigns and you must return to Herbert Chapman, in Arsenal’s thriving 1930s, to find the only manager who went back-to-back.

It can feel premature (and can be foolish) to go out on a limb before the first weekend, but there was just something about them that felt different. Often in the past they have been overtly tentative when playing City, but they came out of their corner this time swinging – and they landed.

Enzo Maresca revealed afterwards that he “really didn’t like” how Arsenal had scored their first goal and that was putting it mildly, as there were 10 passes – broken only by the ball bouncing off Elliott Anderson’s shins – before Myles Lewis-Skelly ushered Calafiori into wreak havoc.

You had to go back to 1968, when City played West Brom, to find the last first-minute goal – City’s Bobby Owen was the scorer that day – and how Calafiori enjoyed it, shaking his fist in delight as Arsenal’s noisy fans reminded everyone of their status.

Riccardo Calafiori gives Arsenal the lead after just 24 seconds 🤯The assist from Myles Lewis-Skelly 👏📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/aU0UsCB1Xs

Here was a rude awakening for Anderson, City’s new £116m man. He was ever so slightly off the pace and that allowed Lewis-Skelly to slip a beautiful ball in behind the FA Cup winners’ defence and invite Calafiori to do the rest, which he did with assurance.

When Maresca watches back the video, he will see Abdukodir Khusanov sleeping and Phil Foden failing to press, but that should not detract from the quality of Arsenal’s interchanging – and it should also make whoever is hawking Lewis-Skelly around to clubs to think again. Why would he leave this?

It should not have been the case that a goal so soon should have governed how the game progressed, but that is exactly what happened as Arsenal completely dominated. Whenever they lost possession, they recovered it as a matter of urgency. Without Pep Guardiola on the touchline, City were like Samson after Delilah shaved his hair, devoid of all power.

City, in contrast to their opponents, showed a complete lack of desire and the second goal arrived when Odegaard was allowed time to flip a ball to the back post, where new boy Tzolis was arriving. The Greek headed back into the six-yard area and Kai Havertz did the rest.

Kai Havertz finishes off a well-worked move to double Arsenal's lead 🤩📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/tGkxCIBV8F

Arsenal were criticised – fairly – during their title-winning campaign for being too physical and relying on gamesmanship, but if Havertz and Odegaard can stay fit for a prolonged period, the difference in style will be like night and day.

Throw in Tzolis, who was tricky and dynamic in Cardiff, to the mix and there will be another enhancement. He looks considerably better than Gabriel Martinelli, with more end product, and Bukayo Saka will do more down the right than Noni Madueke, who started here.

Maresca knew, with his team lacking fitness, that it would be difficult to overhaul the deficit once they had gone two goals behind but, really, he was lucky that Arsenal did not administer a genuine hiding which, at one stage, seemed as though they might.

Goal number three arrived just after the interval, again Lewis-Skelly and Tzolis were involved, combining to enable Odegaard to waltz into the area, hoodwinking Donnarumma so he sat down before sliding a contemptuous finish beyond him.

Take a bow, Martin Ødegaard 😮‍💨Arsenal are flying against Man City!📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/cMHbIyJ90D

Had they gone through the gears, there could have been more, but it didn’t matter. What Arsenal showed was far more significant than a couple of more goals when the game was being disrupted by substitutions. The tackles, the running, energy and commitment – that is what brought Arteta joy.

“I’m extremely happy with the performance, the result and winning the first trophy,” Arteta purred.

You would be brave to say it will be their last.

Arsenal (4-2-3-1) Raya 7; White 7, Mosquera 7, Gabriel 7, Calafiori 7 (Hincapie h-t): Guimarães 7 (Rice h-t), Lewis-Skelly 8 (Zublimendi 75); Madueke 6 [Saka 60], Odegaard 8 (Eze 84), Tzolis 7; Havertz 7 (Gyokeres 75). Booked Calafiori, Odegaard. Subs Kepa (g), Merino, Dowman.

Goals: Calafiori (1), Havertz (28), Odegaard (48).

Manchester City (4-2-3-1) Donnarumma 5; Khusnaov 5, Dias 5, Gvardiol 5, O’Reilly 5; Anderson 5 (Lewis 60), Kovacic 5 (Gonzalez 79); Semenyo 6, Foden 5 (Cherki 60), Doku 6 (Grealish h-t); Haaland 5 (Marmoush 53). Booked Gvardiol, Foden. Subs Ait-Nouri, Reis, Nunes, Rulli (g).

It’s really sad. I’ve been fighting with the Premier League to extend & accommodate more players in the squad. They deserve to be in the squad, so hopefully we can change that rule.

I think the goal we conceded after 25 seconds unfortunately affected the game in that moment. I think after the goal, the reaction was quite good before they scored the second one, we had three or four chances to score and draw the game but unfortunately we conceded the second one and it became more complicated.

A really, really good performance so early in the season. To play at the level we did and the desire we showed, I just told them that I really enjoyed watching them.

He makes good decisions when a lot of people rush things, he did it twice in tight areas and two goals.

I joined midway [in pre-season]. This is the third game since I have been back. The feeling has been good. Today is frustrating, and it is a final that we all wanted to win. If there is a lesson to be learnt in the final, let it be this one, as there’s a lot more coming. It is a positive energy.

The feeling of a lot of work to put into. It’s part of any transition for things to be not so perfect in the beginning. You need to push through, you need to communicate, and make things work between us. I feel we’re in a very good way, but we need to keep on working. There’s going to be lots of challenges along the way.

Appears to the Community Shield trophy, which caught him a glancing blow to the face.

Trophy lift gone wrong, featuring Declan Rice 😂🏆📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ghmGZJDxka

The players judge the correct level of celebration judiciously, but then Mikel Merino cracks and starts spraying the champagne. While it is a semi-competitive game, Arteta and his players will point out that they earned their place in the fixture by winning the league.

Arsenal start the season with silverware 🏆The Community Shield belongs to the Gunners!📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/M6GqsGkRF7

What happens to them? I’m not sure the winners’ medals would take pride of place, let alone the silvers.

We played some brilliant football. Great performance and a great way to start the season.

I always want to help the team as much possible with goals and assists. I want to score more goals.

We showed our level today. We’re showed we’re ready. We’re serious and we want to do it again.

We want to attack it. We want to do it again. When you get a taste of how nice it is you want to do it again.

The league champions kick-off the domestic season with a resounding and stylish victory. Shades of 1998 and 2004 when they swept Manchester United aside in this fixture as title winners, only to fail to defend the crown in the season that followed. So maybe it is unwise to make bold forecasts, but it could not have gone better for Arteta. Odegaard, Lewis-Skelly and Tzolis caught the eye, and Arsenal had their usual solidarity defensively. City just completely off the pace, one to write off and move on.

Marmoush is feeling his hip after a challenge by Mosquera. City have a free-kick wide right. Gabriel heads away Grealish’s delivery in trademark fashion.

Just three minutes of added time to play. No City player is there to meet Cherki’s low cross and White can clear under little pressure.

Rice uncharacteristically caught dallying in midfield but City cannot capitalise. Cheers from the Arsenal fans as Saka wins a throw in from Grealish. Marmoush with a chance to run at Mosquera, but his touch is far too heavy.

City have a free-kick in a crossing position right of centre, but many of their fans are now packing up their banners and heading for the exits. If they haven’t already. Cherki’s delivery is poor, and Rice heads away.

Odegaard with a loose touch, and a yellow card for catching Grealish with the resulting challenge. That was the Arsenal captain’s last action of the game, he is replaced by Eberechi Eze. Odegaard has looked back to his 2024 past today, Eze’s best chance of a start might be from the left.

City’s best move of the second half: Cherki gliding through the challenges and finding Semenyo with a lovely reverse pass, and his shot was drilled towards the far corner. Sharp reflexes by Raya to plunge to his right and save.

Nico Gonzalez replaces Kovacic as Maresca makes his sixth change of the second half. The game has felt like a training exercise since Odegaard’s third goal with the occasional flash of quality.

Chance for Saka! Cracking low cross from Hincapie, but Saka sweeps over from near the penalty spot. Too much on it as he tried to help the ball on its way.

Better tempo to Manchester City’s football, and Gvardiol has gone down holding his face in the box. It was more of a shoulder to shoulder with White, and the incident is checked and cleared by VAR.

Here come two more Arsenal changes: Havertz and Lewis-Skelly deserve their ovation, replaced by Gyokeres and Zubimendi.

Chance for Tzolis to play Saka clean through on goal but he delayed a fraction and Gvardiol got back in to defend. It was a great flick on by Havertz to free Tzolis. Gyokeres is ready to replace the German.

Cherki with a shot from distance, saved by Raya. That was City’s first shot on target of the second half.

Odegaard with a disguised ball through to White, who may have been offside, and Tzolis is close to applying the touch that would have made it four. Feels like the game is meandering towards its conclusion.

Arsenal back themselves to play out from a tight spot again, but Semenyo does well to force Hincapie to concede a throw in. Arsenal then soak up another spell of City possession, they have been so much more compact defensively than Maresca’s team. Whenever Arsenal have the ball in City’s half they look dangerous, whereas City’s possession has been sterile.

City chasing shadows when Arsenal play out from the back. Arsenal moving the ball with great assurance, but you suspect everyone has an extra yard of space than they would find in a full-throttle Premier League game.

Semenyo gave Hincapie a tough time in the League Cup final in March, and was not shy in boasting about it after the game. I suspect Hincapie is a defender who keeps a little black book of those who have crossed him.

Lovely moment in midfield from Odegaard, letting the ball run across his box and pushing it beyond Rico Lewis. Saka in acres on the far side after he outmuscles Gvardiol, but he shoots into the side netting. Tried to give Donnarumma the eyes.

City with a spell of possession in the Arsenal half, and Gvardiol glances a header over the bar from a very decent Grealish cross. Arsenal hard to break down once they are in that 4-4-2 shape.

Here come the changes: Foden and Anderson off, Cherki and Rico Lewis on.

Arsenal subs: Saka and Hincapue on for Calafiori and Madueke. Saka has braids this seasons, so a new look.

Arsenal popping the ball around in the sunshine now, to olés from their fans. Maresca is about to make two more changes, so five subs before the hour tells you were City are physically. Saka is going to come on for Arsenal.

Gvardiol booked, and here come more City changes, this is a fitness exercise for Maresca now. Haaland and O’Reilly off, Marmoush and Guehi on. Arteta will surely reply in kind around the hour mark.

That really should be game over now, but given the loosey-goosey nature of these games I suppose you never know. I think the only way this fixture can matter is if one team takes a battering, and there’s a risk of that for City now.

Christos Tzolis registered 29 assists in 52 competitive games for Club Brugge last season. He’s on two assists in 48 competitive minutes for Arsenal.

What composure from the Arsenal captain, running into the box untracked and sitting down first Gvardiol then Donnarumma before finding the empty net. It is clever play from Tzolis, finding Odegaard with the pass for his second assist of the game. The run from Calafiori was important to pull City’s defence out of shape.

Take a bow, Martin Ødegaard 😮‍💨Arsenal are flying against Man City!📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/cMHbIyJ90D

Man City kick off in the second 45 minutes. These matches tend to lose their rhythm in the second half.

So far, Manchester City’s first glimpse of life after Pep Guardiola is inauspicious. Enzo Maresca might be his predecessor’s doppelgänger, but his attempt to emulate the same style has proved abortive: plenty of possession, but minimal impact. It smacks of desperation that Jack Grealish is being thrown in at half-time, his first appearance for the club for 15 months.

Looks like a pre-planned change from Manchester City and Arsenal: Jack Grealish makes an unlikely comeback, replacing Doku, and Declan Rice replaces Bruno Guimaraes. Arsenal’s two big hitters in midfield sharing the game.

7 - Kai Havertz has been involved in more goals against Manchester City (7 - 4 goals, 3 assists) than against any other side in his club career. Occasion. pic.twitter.com/ln7PQnjboJ

00:23 - Riccardo Calafiori's goal for Arsenal after 23 seconds is the first scored in the opening minute of the Community Shield since Bobby Owen for Manchester City against West Bromwich Albion in 1968.Rapid. pic.twitter.com/FCwVKuTOlh

Advantage Arsenal at half time, and they have looked a sharper, more cohesive team. City have had plenty of possession, but much of it was sterile until that late flurry when Raya saved from Haaland and White blocked Doku’s shot. The first 45 minutes will have ticked all of the boxes for Arteta: there has been some strong penalty box defending, some flowing moves from back to front and two well-taken goals.

Flimsy defending from City again, Havertz finding it easy to run to the byline, and the ball is cleared off the line after Odegaard poked the ball towards goal after a Donnarumma parry.

“You’re getting sacked in the morning,” sing the Arsenal fans at Maresca as the whistle blows.

Mosquera defends well against Doku at the expense of a corner, which Raya claims with ease. There is going to be just one minute of added time.

Arsenal playing through the pitch and City’s defensive shape again, this time it was started by a fizzed Raya pass into Tzolis. Three on three, but Madueke’s shot is straight at Donnarummma. The winger is such an outlet for his team, but the final decision is lacking too often, which is not a novel observation.

Madueke then finds White on the overlap, he chips the ball to the back post where Calafiori is free and he volleys over.

Arsenal’s defence stretched for the first time in the game. Raya saved after Haaland was picked out by Doku, with Lewis-Skelly defending well to deny a rebound, before Semenyo picks out Doku with a lofted cross, but White through himself in front of the volley and made a crucial block.

Ben White to the rescue with an incredible block 🦸📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ZK0cNnFz5N

Madueke with a tame shot on goal after O’Reilly went Awol defensively, but the flag was up for offside.

Arsenal come forward again, with Havertz holding the ball up well. Tzolis reverses a pass for Calafiori, but he anticipates a challenge in the area and is rightly booked for diving.

Ben White thought he had nipped in front of Doku to intercept a straight Kovacic pass, but the referee blows for a foul against the Arsenal man.

Then Haaland has a sight of goal for the first time: a peeling run into the right channel, found by Doku, but it was tough angle on his weaker foot. Scooped it over the bar.

Foden takes up a lovely position behind the Arsenal midfield, but his through ball towards Haaland hits Gabriel on the back of the heel. Then Semenyo wins a corner in a joust with Calafiori. Referee blows for some pushing and shoving.

Eventually the corner is taken, cleared initially, before teasing Foden cross drifts beyond the back post. Foden the pick of the bunch for City, which is unsurprising considering he has a full pre-season behind him.

The Arsenal supporters are really, really enjoying this. They’re “doing the Poznan” to mock the City fans.

An ideal outing for Arsenal, so far though it can be easy to over-index these games when players are not fully match fit. But Arteta will be pleased with the fluency in the passing through midfield, which was lacking at times last season.

Christos Tzolis was signed to provide goals and assists, and he’s been doing so throughout pre-season. The Greek winger is perhaps more aggressive in his positioning than Leandro Trossard, the man he has replaced in the squad, and he was in the right place there to pick out Kai Havertz.

The new signing Tzolis is involved with a clever header back across the six-yard box, the left winger was picked out by an inswinging Odegaard cross to the back post. Havertz rose above Dias, and his header down into the turf squeezed beyond Donnarumma. The ball bounced in off the back of the goalkeeper, could well be an own goal.

Kai Havertz finishes off a well-worked move to double Arsenal's lead 🤩📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/tGkxCIBV8F

Gvardiol slides across to win an important challenge when Madueke was running into space, before Odegaard fails with a scooped pass towards White.

Arsenal find Madueke in acres of space again, Bruno Guimaraes with the switch, and the winger keeps things alive despite an unconvincing dribble. Guimaraes then finds space in the box, but takes to long to pick out a man.

City soon on the attack again, and Doku runs off the back of White all too easily, but Gabriel charges in to win a booming slide tackle in the box. He greets it with his own roar of approval.

Raya claims the corner, then Foden is booked for pulling back Tzolis to stop a counter.

In these early days, long before trophies become something tangible, Mikel Arteta will want to see something far more vital than talent - hunger. It’s bursting out of Arsenal’s players, never more apparent than when Gabriel has just thundered into Jeremy Doku and celebrated the challenge like a goal. It reflective of the team’s mentality.

The passion from Gabriel after stopping Jérémy Doku 😤📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/L3D8lHrBNU

City’s best moment so far: Foden with a shot from just outside the box which is pushed clear by Raya, before O’Reilly is penalised for a push on Ben White. It looked like the City man was just stronger in the shoulder to shoulder. Perhaps out frustration, O’Reilly then fouls Havertz on halfway.

The Arsenal fans massively outnumber the City supporters here, and the Londoners appear to have fallen in love with Guimaraes already. He’s snapping into tackles with real venom. There have been lots of cries of “Bruno!” in these opening 23 minutes.

Better from City, with Foden turning after receiving the ball between the lines. Then Anderson flashes a cross across the penalty area from an inside right position, but Haaland was slightly on his heels and it runs out for a goal kick.

Interesting to see Guimaraes drop all the way into Arsenal’s penalty area for their goal-kick a few minutes ago. Arsenal had massive problems playing out from the back against City in the Carabao Cup final last season. The Brazilian’s positioning could be a reaction to that.

Considering Arsenal are missing Saliba, Timber and Rice, their defence has looked relatively untroubled so far. City’s big names in attacking areas are on the pitch, but still finding their level as the new season approaches.

Arsenal have a corner after Gvardiol sticks out a leg to block Madueke’s low cross. Sharp in midfield from Lewis-Skelly and Bruno Guimaraes to spread the play to the right winger. Good delivery from Madueke, headed clear, before White does well to usher the ball behind for another corner.

Gabriel and Khusanov tangle at the back post, appeals for an Arsenal penalty, but Gabriel was the first player to pull a shirt.

Gvardiol with a diagonal cross that floats behind for an Arsenal goal kick. City starting to enjoy some control in the Arsenal half, with Arteta’s team trusting their defensive shape to absorb pressure.

Arsenal with the chance to counter-attack with runners after Kovacic’s loss of possession in midfield, but Odegaard’s pass was slightly behind Madueke, who then had to check before hesitating. Surely more goals to follow, given the ease with which Arsenal are getting at City and the forward quality in Maresca’s team.

Odegaard tries a chipped pass into Havertz’s path in the penalty area but Gvardiol heads away. Moments earlier, Doku claimed he was fouled by White near the touchline but nothing doing.

Arsenal continue to flow forward, finding plenty of space in City’s half, but Tzolis’s cross deflects into the arms of Donnarumma.

There was a check for offside in the build up to Arsenal’s goal but the goal stands. Welcome back VAR, and consider the curtain raised on the new season. City enjoying some possession since conceding.

That’s certainly one way to start a new season. It’s a fabulous team goal, with Lewis-Skelly at the heart of it. There has been a lot of talk about this teenager’s future but, in this reporter’s humble opinion, it should not even be a discussion. Losing a player of this quality, a product of the club’s academy, would be a terrible mistake.

Surely the fastest goal in the history of this fixture, or most fixtures for that matter.

Arsenal were camped in City’s half from kick off, and it was superb from Lewis-Skelly in midfield to let the ball run across his body and find the run of Calafiori with a reverse pass, and the left-back keeps his cool to roll the ball beyond Donnarumma.

Riccardo Calafiori gives Arsenal the lead after just 24 seconds 🤯The assist from Myles Lewis-Skelly 👏📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/aU0UsCB1Xs

Arsenal get the game, and the 2026-27 domestic season, started.

Former Man City player Mike Summerbee, who fans used to hail with a Small Faces-inspired chant, is involved in the preliminaries.

With no Timber, Saliba or Rice, this could be a more open game than some of the recent chess matches between these sides. The lower stakes should help with that. City have a favourable match up down their left with O’Reilly and Doku against Madueke and White. There is more ball retention in Arsenal’s team than at periods of last season, with Guimaraes, Odegaard, Lewis-Skelly and Havertz in the middle.

Sincere commiserations to the Arsenal and Manchester City supporters who have attempted to travel by road to Cardiff today. We should have nothing but sympathy for those diehards who have tried to navigate the car parks of the M5 and the M4 and nothing but scorn for whoever is in charge of planning at Wembley. Who would have thought to check the football calendar before booking a concert for the week before the new season? A total nonsense. Let’s hope the game turns out to be better than the travel.

Always a talking point during the Six Nations, but there is no reason for it to close on a sunny afternoon on the banks of the River Taff. That will mean a slightly annoying shadow across the pitch, always a potential irritant in these August or May showpieces.

I said already in the last days, no matter if we are in August or May, it is a final and when it is a final we need to win.

[Players coming back from the World Cup] Many, many players, for us for them, we are in the exact same situation. It depends how we can manage the game, we will see.

[What he expects from Anderson] Exactly the player he is. We are not asking him something more. He is a good player on and off the ball, always making an effort for his team-mates.

I said in the press conference, we are going to decide the four captains when the window closes. At the moments, Ruben Dias and Erling are with us [no comment on Rodri’s future].

Good afternoon from Cardiff, where the sun is shining and the fans are enjoying the pubs outside the Principality Stadium. The teams are allowed nine substitutes today, which has really highlighted the bloated nature of Arsenal’s squad. There’s no space for Ethan Nwaneri, Gabriel Martinelli, Gabriel Jesus, Fabio Vieira or Reiss Nelson. All five of them could be sold by the end of the month.

I had plenty of rest, some work as well, it was a break that I really enjoyed.

Very much [on if he was impressed with his signings]. Christos [Tzolis] came early which always helps with a new signing, and Bruno joined us last week after a long summer with him but he is in good condition.

I think it is something very individual. [Declan] Rice played more than 65 games, he needed a complete rest and we need to build him. It’s not only physical, it’s mental freshness. For the players not involved in the World Cup it is a bit different. They remain so competitive. They wanted to be involved and that’s good to see as well.

[On Bruno] He is a ball of energy. He has an unbelievable desire to win every ball. You sense he will drive the dressing room and when you bring someone with that competitive nature, it will only drive the boys.

[On retaining the title] Still recognise the big margins that we have to improve as a team, individually and as well the ambition of the club which is unquestionable.

Elliot Anderson makes his first City appearance, and he will be partnered by Mateo Kovacic in midfield with Nico O’Reilly drifting into those areas from midfield. Phil Foden, who did not go to the World Cup, starts ahead of Rayan Cherki and Doku, Haaland and Semenyo is City’s strongest front three. No Rodri, but Jack Grealish is on the bench.

Man City starting XI: Donnarumma; Khusanov, Dias, Gvardiol, O’Reilly; Kovacic, Anderson; Semenyo, Foden, Doku; Haaland

Subs: Rulli, Guéhi, Marmoush, Cherki, Nico, Grealish, Aït-Nouri, Nunes, Lewis

The other interesting snippets are Arteta plumping for Madueke over Max Dowman on the right, Havertz over Gyokeres and Calafiori over Hincapie. Also worth noting that there is no place in the squad for Ethan Nwaneri nor Gabriel Martinelli who have been linked with moves. The same goes for Fabio Vieira, Gabriel Jesus and Reiss Nelson.

Arsenal starting XI: Raya; White, Mosquera, Gabriel, Calafiori; Guimaraes, Lewis-Skelly, Odegaard; Madueke, Havertz, Tzolis

Subs: Kepa, Hincapie, Rice, Zubimendi, Merino, Eze, Dowman, Saka, Gyokeres

🔴 𝗧𝗘𝗔𝗠𝙉𝙀𝙒𝙎 ⚪️Mikel names a strong starting XI 👊🤝Presented by @deel pic.twitter.com/bckDyMazRo

Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka are with the group, but they have not kicked a ball in pre-season. They are looking at half hour of football at the absolute maximum today.

In case any Arsenal fan had forgotten that last season ended with them losing a Champions League final on penalties, City fans are on hand to remind them. They have one European Cup to Arsenal’s zero. Away from the tin foil trophies, I’m sure much bottle-related mirth is on the cards, especially now broadcasters and fans are aware of the viral possibilities. Too aware, I would argue.

The pool of players who can improve the Premier League champions and Champions League finalists is a small one, but it is still fair to point out that Arsenal’s summer has not gone smoothly. They pursued Morgan Rogers and Vinicius Junior without success, and Arteta’s desire to take the team to a “different dimension” has so far gone unfulfilled., certainly in the forward positions.

Arsenal still look strong, but have they passed up a chance to pull away from the rest? Sam Wallace takes a look at their summer so far.

It would have been less stressful for Guardiola to go once he realised the great side of Kevin De Bruyne was nearing its end. Instead he opted to oversee a rebuild that gives his successor a greater chance of immediate success, going close to the title last season in what was effectively year one for a re-emerging City side. Guardiola must have known he was signing Gianluigi Donnarumma, Antoine Semenyo, Marc Guéhi and Rayan Cherki for someone else’s long-term benefit.

The Community Shield returns to Cardiff’s Principality Stadium for the first time since 2006, and a different dynamic is at play between Arsenal and Manchester City.

When the two clubs played at Wembley in this fixture three years ago, it felt like a more significant occasion for Arsenal as they sought to prove that the gap was closing to Pep Guardiola’s champions.

Now it is Arsenal and Mikel Arteta who have a league title behind them, while Enzo Maresca is the manager hoping to build credibility as City turn the page post-Pep Guardiola.

In truth, these two teams will look very different by the time the season gathers pace in autumn. World Cup exertions mean Elliot Anderson, Erling Haaland, Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka will be minimally involved in this game, while transfer plans remain up in the air for both camps.

City appear bound to lose Rodri, in addition to Bernardo Silva and Tijjani Reijnders in central midfield. Rodri’s sale would expedite a move for Lille’s Ayyoub Bouaddi, and possibly Enzo Fernandez despite Chelsea’s insistence that the deadline to sign him for £120m has passed.

Arsenal are also open for business, hoping to add a right-sided defender to help them cope with William Saliba’s absence. The £75m purchase of Bruno Guimarães means the champions’ midfield options look formidable, but so far it has been another summer without a level-raising forward signing. Christos Tzolis in and Leandro Trossard out looks canny business, but falls into the category of like for like.

Although Arsenal held their nerve to see off City in the title race, they failed to win in three attempts against their rivals, including a limp defeat in the Carabao Cup final at Wembley. Arsenal also failed to win, or score, against Liverpool in the Premier League last season so their record in the big games is an area for improvement.

The victors this afternoon will claim to have laid a marker down, the losers will write the game off as a warm up exercise.

#1824. Middlesbrough vs Bristol City - prediction, team news, lineups

By Calum Burrowes | 19 Nov 2026 15:53, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 16:00

Middlesbrough will be looking to move to the top of the Championship table this weekend when they welcome a struggling Bristol City side to the Riverside Stadium.

Boro entered the final international break of the year having missed the opportunity to become league leaders, as a defeat to Wrexham was followed by a goalless draw away to Watford, while the Robins continued their slide down the table after suffering a humiliating 5-0 home defeat to Norwich City just under a fortnight ago.

Kim Hellberg and his Middlesbrough side return to the Riverside Stadium for the first time since Halloween with an opportunity to leapfrog Birmingham City and move to the top of the Championship table.

The Blues have made an unexpected push for first place in recent weeks after winning three consecutive matches, while Boro managed just one victory, alongside a defeat and a draw, leaving both sides level on 29 points ahead of matchweek 16.

Such is the competitiveness of the Championship that Middlesbrough's tally of 29 points provides them with just a three-point cushion over sixth place, highlighting how quickly the standings can change.

Although their form at the start of November was somewhat inconsistent, Boro return to home soil where they are unbeaten in seven matches, collecting 17 points and scoring 17 goals during that run, with only Southampton boasting a better home record than Hellberg's side.

Last season saw Hellberg and his Middlesbrough team miss out on promotion to the Premier League following one of the most dramatic and controversial playoff campaigns in recent memory, despite occupying a place in the top two for much of the season.

Their success during the 2025-26 campaign was built on a prolific attack that scored 72 goals in 46 matches, a total bettered by just three teams, and they have once again impressed in the final third this season, with only one side scoring more than their 30 goals.

As for Bristol City, they entered the international break with serious questions surrounding the future of manager Michael Skubala after a dreadful run of form saw them fall out of the playoff places and down to 17th in the table.

Since the first international break ended in September, the Robins have won just one of their subsequent seven Championship matches and were widely tipped to part company with the former Lincoln City boss during the past fortnight, but the club have opted to stick with him as he prepares to take charge of his 17th match on Saturday.

A short video published by the club last week showed CEO Charlie Boss confirming that they would "give Skubala the opportunity to turn around the home form", with Bristol City's two victories at Ashton Gate representing the fourth-worst record in the division and a stark contrast to that of their upcoming opponents.

The Robins enjoyed a productive seven-day spell in which they collected nine points from a possible nine against Portsmouth, Preston North End and Burnley, but have since suffered a series of disappointing results that have seen their playoff ambitions replaced by growing concerns over a potential relegation battle.

Norwich arrived in the South West in encouraging form, but few would have expected them to inflict such a heavy defeat on Skubala's side, with the 5-0 loss at Ashton Gate subsequently described by the manager as one of the most difficult afternoons of his career.

Although the Robins face one of the division's strongest sides this weekend, they can at least take confidence from their recent record against Boro, with the North Yorkshire outfit winless in their last nine league meetings and without a victory over Bristol City since August 2021.

Middlesbrough could name the same starting XI that drew with Watford almost a fortnight ago, although Hellberg may be tempted to make changes as his side look to return to winning ways.

Former Robins goalkeeper Radek Vitek is expected to retain his place between the posts, while former Bristol City players Tommy Conway, Neto Borges and Luke Ayling could all come into contention to face their old club after starting on the bench last time out.

Rokas Pusktas has suffered another injury setback after undergoing surgery on a hamstring problem and has managed just 12 minutes of football for Boro since joining from Hajduk Split in August.

Hellberg will also be without Alfie Jones, who remains sidelined with a calf injury, but could welcome the Championship's leading scorer back into the fold, with Will Lankshear looking to add to his 13 league goals, which have come at an impressive rate of one every 81 minutes.

Meanwhile, Bristol City are expected to have just one absentee for Saturday's trip north, with Noah Eile likely to miss out through illness.

Although their major injury crisis from last season is very much a thing of the past, the Robins have made several unexpected changes to their recent starting lineups, making it difficult to predict the team Skubala will select.

New goalkeeper Sam Tickle was dropped in favour of Brad Collins after just 11 appearances for his new club but could be reinstated after his replacement made several high-profile errors leading to goals during his four starts, conceding an average of 2.3 goals per game during that time.

Skubala has also alternated between a lone striker and a two-man forward partnership in recent weeks and could once again make changes as he looks to turn around his side's disappointing run of form.

Rio Cardines opted out of international duty with Trinidad and Tobago over the past fortnight after featuring in every one of the Robins' Championship matches during his debut season as a professional, and he is expected to return to the attack this weekend as he looks to build on the impressive six assists he has already provided.

Vitek; Brittain, Phillips, Malanda, Bryam; Berhalter, Morris, McGree; Conway, Strelec, Sarmiento

Tickle; Tanner, Dickie, Eissat, Pring; Williams, Randell; Cardines, Knight, Twine; Tolaj

With one of the division's most out-of-form sides facing a team that has been exceptionally difficult to beat on home soil, we expect the result to go Middlesbrough's way.

Although the Robins boast an impressive recent record against Boro, we expect that run to come to an end on Saturday as Hellberg's side continue their push towards the top of the Championship table.

#1823. On The Road: Overpowered by County, but Accies are making small steps in the long road back from the abyss

Published: 08:28 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 10:25 EST, 15 November 2026

The depth of the descent of Hamilton Accies and Ross County would make it understandable if tickets for a fixture between the two carried warning about the bends when leaving New Douglas Park.

The decompression sickness caused by emerging from a League One fixture for two sides who should be much higher must be severe. There may, however, be a positive prognosis.

Accies, despite their defeat, are whispering about stability, even though ‘legacy debt’ has to be faced, perhaps contested.

County, meanwhile, will not say it even in a whisper but Saturday’s victory takes them eight points clear at the top and heavily fancied for the title. The Staggies have one set of hooves in the Championship.

Scottish football, of course, does not restrict itself to the cliched fare of top of the table clashes so New Douglas Park hosted a striker who is 39 later this month, a winger who was once a Scottish international, and a gentleman in the stands who once played against George Best. And a Ross County fan who regularly travels up from North Wales.

These exotic avenues demand to be explored but perennial questions about the financial health of the Accies had to be asked, too, after reports this week stating that hospitality packages at the club were being suspended.

An Accies fan feels the pain of defeat during Saturday's home loss to Ross County

Allan Currie, chairman, answered them over a half-time pie.

‘We have come on in leaps and bounds but every week seems to throw up different challenges,’ he said. ‘We have a level of debt that we have inherited and we are working with the creditors to try to navigate our way through that.’

Matters on the field are positive, despite Saturday’s defeat.

‘The guys on the pitch, manager, and his staff have been unbelievable. Surviving in this league last season was phenomenal given what they were going through but it couldn’t be better now,’ he said. ‘Off the pitch, we are fighting with the different challenges we have. We are in a much better place even if we are not out the woods yet.’

Asked what the level of pressure on him, he said: ‘I am the guy on the ground but Rob Edwards is carrying out negotiations.’

Edwards, through his Morley Group, took over the club earlier this year but has been sideswiped by a number of claims for payment. However, Currie has faith in the owner.

‘Without him, the club would not survive. Rob should take all the credit,’ he said.

Asked what the short-term aims for the club were, Currie replied with a smile: ‘A goal in the second half would be good.’ A goal was scored but not for the Accies.

But the club remain in second place and the play-offs seem a more than reasonable prospect.

Ross County goalscorer Kieran Phillips battles with Hamilton's Kai Smutek

With 10 minutes to go, Hamilton brought on their latest signing. Barrie McKay, who has played for Scotland and scored for Rangers in a Scottish Cup semi-final against Celtic. His considerable achievements, though, paled in comparison to the subject of a casual conversation in the bar before the match.

‘I played against George Best,’ said Alan McDougall, with an air so off-hand one could have believed he was merely ordering another pint.

‘Yes, I played 200 games for the Accies. Davie McParland brought me here as a 21-year-old and I played for about six years. I went to Stranraer for a year and then went down south. I played against Best with the Accies.’

The Northern Irish genius played for Hibernian in 1979-80. ‘He was well past his best and that was sad,’ said McDougall. Best’s addiction to alcohol had taken a severe toll.

‘I came back to watch games five or six years ago,’ said McDougall. ‘When the club went to Clyde, it destroyed me. What is fantastic is that the people that are now in control seem to be turning it around.’

There was a mood of cautious optimism from other fans. ‘I have been a fan since forever, well the 1980s at least,’ said Gavin Fullarton. ‘I have seen this team in every division. I have seen them in the downs and downs. But I think we are going in the right direction. So far.’

He added: ‘The new guys seem to know what they are doing. They are communicative.’

There were 1,216 fans in the ground on Saturday with 300 stalwarts travelling down from the north. Colin Richardson, an Accies supporter, was asked why so many had stuck by the club.

‘It’s about loyalty,’ he said. ‘You can’t pick and choose when you support your team. At the moment it is all about small steps. It has to be about stability.’

A Ross County fan had travelled up from North Wales. The journey to Scotland is a familiar one for Ian Ellson. ‘I have been all over Scotland to watch Ross County,’ he said. ‘Twenty years ago I visited Ross County and I was spoiled rotten. I decided to follow them.’

A social worker, he averages one visit a month. ‘I live and breathe Ross County,’ he said. ‘This season we are going up.’

Welsh Staggies fan Ian Elson and Englishman Ray Griffiths travelled far for Saturday's game

Brian Graham would not be so bullish. He is 39 this month and has learned enough about football to know that predictions are made only to make the speaker seem foolish down the line.

He was, though, expansive about what is happening at County. He joined the club for the second time in the summer after Stuart Kettlewell, the manager, convinced him of the ambitions in Dingwall.

‘This is a club where I have had success before so I know how good a club it can be,’ he said. ‘It’s not been great for a couple of seasons but in the summer the manager set out his stall very early. It was about leaving egos at the door, building a togetherness and having a change of culture at the club. I think you are seeing that now.’

The early signs were good for the striker who dropped down from Falkirk in the Premiership to play in Dingwall.

‘We had good pre-season performances against Aberdeen and Dundee and that was a solid building block,’ he said.

Brian Graham celebrates after scoring his 21st goal of the season for County

Graham converted a first-half penalty to reach a tally of 21 goals this season and the Christmas trees are not up yet. ‘I get a lot of plaudits for scoring goals but others in the team are scoring a lot too,’ he said. ‘We are scoring team goals.’

Has he set a target for the season? ‘When I came back I knew I had to score 13 to reach 50 goals for the club in two spells,’ he said. ‘I always set down targets in a wee black book but now I might need to readjust that.’

It was a night of adjustment for Darian MacKinnon. He had set a victory target but was condemned to accept defeat. He would not concede the league race was over. ‘We have to play them twice,’ he said.

He added ‘We are going in the right direction. The owners have put money in and they have backed us.’

Asked to pinpoint a factor that has contributed to the team sitting second, he said: ‘The most positive thing for me this season is that this is now a good place to come into your work after the last three or four seasons. We are all actually enjoying coming to our work.’

There is work to be done on and off the pitch but the Accies are surviving. And that is the biggest result.

#1822. GdS: Milan choose Tresoldi with Club Brugge star desperate for move – the situation

AC Milan have chosen the centre-forward they want in January, according to La Gazzetta dello Sport: Nicolo Tresoldi.

The newspaper write this morning that the ballot is settled, and there’s a winner: Milan have opted for Tresoldi as their attacking target in view of the winter. Part of the reason for this is because Endrick – the alternative name – made his intentions clear: “I hope to spend my life at Real Madrid.”

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

In this story of preferences, Tresoldi’s choice is also crucial. The 22-year-old has supported Milan since he was a child, while in Belgium and beyond he has proven himself to be a goal scorer. Inter found this out, as he scored a hat-trick against them in the Champions League at San Siro.

The No.9 shirt and role is currently occupied by Gonçalo Ramos, not a trivial thing due to the record-breaking fee paid for him last summer. However, Ruben Amorim genuinely believes the Portuguese can co-exist with Tresoldi, who can be on hand to finish the chances created by Ramos’ movement.

Tresoldi is a true ‘devil’ in the penalty area. He has 18 goals this season for club (eight in the league, five in the Champions League, and one in the Belgian Super Cup) and another four for Germany’s U21s. This leaves him just shy of 20 goals, in mid-November.

Tresoldi is also desperate to move to Milan and if it were up to him, the deal would be done. His desire to join his boyhood club could prove helpful and provide a boost to the deal’s success, just as it has before. His agents and family are equally positive about a potential Italian move.

Club Brugge are in a different mood, however, and would happily keep him unless offered at least €60m. Just a few months ago, the Belgian giants rejected offers just over half that. This is a figure Milan are willing to negotiate around, because Champions League qualification is crucial and goals are needed to achieve this.

Besides, Cardinale is of the opinion that it’s better to invest now than risk deepening the deficit. Another year without the revenues from the top club competition would be far from ideal for many different reasons.

What about Francesco Camarda? Here too, the debate is over: the club and the coach agree on the need for a loan, perhaps abroad. Camarda agrees: he knows he needs to regain rhythm by playing regularly, to help his development.

For Milan, it would be another negotiation with Brugge after Charles De Ketelaere and Ardon Jashari. The deal for the former was conducted by Paolo Maldini and Ricky Massara, while for the latter it was Igli Tare. Now, Cardinale intends to do things himself.

The owner wants Tresoldi and is ready to sit at the table himself, while Nicolò remains ready to serve him a winning first pass. Milan want him in January, but if that weren’t possible, they would leave the discussion open for the summer.

#1821. Chelsea vs Leeds United - prediction, team news, lineups

By Oliver Thomas | 19 Nov 2026 16:00, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 20:24

Chelsea will be looking to return to winning ways and strengthen their top-four credentials when they take on Leeds United in Saturday afternoon’s Premier League contest at Stamford Bridge.

These two teams served up a nine-goal thriller in the EFL Cup just a couple of months ago, with the West Londoners securing a 6-3 comeback victory in the third round.

Chelsea entered the international break on a sour note with just one win and three defeats to their name in all competitions, crashing out of the EFL Cup to Liverpool and enduring two setbacks in the Premier League.

The Blues responded to a surprise 2-0 home loss to Spurs by beating Man United at Stamford Bridge by the same scoreline, but they came back down to earth a fortnight ago with a disappointing 1-0 defeat to basement club Sunderland at the Stadium of Light.

Five wins, one draw and four defeats have been posted in Xabi Alonso’s first 10 top-flight games for Chelsea, who sit fifth in the Premier League table and just two points behind Liverpool in fourth. However, Aston Villa down in 10th spot are only three points adrift of the Blues.

Having lost three of their first five PL away games for the first time since 2015-16 under Jose Mourinho, Chelsea should welcome this weekend’s return to Stamford Bridge where they have accumulated 10 of their 16 top-flight points this term, scoring the second-most home goals in the division (13).

The West Londoners have also won eight of their last 10 home battles with Leeds across all tournaments (D2) since a 2-0 defeat back in December 1999, though they were held to a 2-2 draw in this exact league fixture last season after letting a two-goal lead slip in the second half.

Following a five-match winless run that placed Daniel Farke under growing pressure, Leeds secured a much-needed 1-0 victory over Tottenham Hotspur at Elland Road to enter the international break on a high.

A dominant second-half display was rewarded with a late strike from substitute Noah Okafor to help Leeds claim their third Premier League win of the season and rise to ninth in the table, six points clear of the bottom three and just two points behind Saturday’s opponents Chelsea in fifth.

Leeds are unbeaten across their last nine Premier League home matches (W5 D4) – their longest run at Elland Road in the top flight since an impressive 15-match streak between January and December 2001 – but they have only won one of their last eight league games on the road (D4 L3).

The Whites are now gearing up for four tricky away trips to Chelsea, Man City, Liverpool and Aston Villa, with Farke hoping that his side can showcase the same relentless character, commitment and unity shown in their win over Spurs as they attempt to improve their fortunes away from home.

Leeds head into this weekend’s contest seeking to end a 10-game winless run away against Chelsea in all competitions (D2 L8). However, having avoided defeat in their last two league meetings (3-1 at home, 2-2 away), the Whites will aim to go three consecutive games unbeaten against the Blues for the first time since between November 2000 and October 2001.

Chelsea’s Reece James (knee), Maxence Lacroix (hamstring) and Jamie Gittens (ankle) all remain sidelined with injuries, but there is hope that Joao Pedro could be ready to return after missing the last four matches with a thigh problem.

Moises Caicedo (illness), Jorrel Hato (back) and Josh Acheampong (unspecified) are all doubtful, but goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez should be ready to start ahead for Mike Penders after recovering from a broken jaw to represent Argentina during the international break.

Morgan Rogers provided four second-half assists in the aforementioned EFL Cup win over Leeds in September, while Cole Palmer and Danny Welbeck both netted a brace. However, Welbeck may have to settle for a place on the bench once again, with Alonso possibly favouring either Estevao Willian or Pedro Neto in a central role alongside Rogers and Palmer.

As for Leeds, young forward Mateo Joseph is making positive progress in his recovery from a serious knee injury, but he remains sidelined, while midfielder Anton Stach is doubtful after missing the win over Spurs with a broken toe.

Farke will consider sticking with a two-man frontline of Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Lukas Nmecha, with Sean Longstaff and Ao Tanaka linking up with ex-Chelsea youngster Ethan Ampadu in midfield.

However, Noah Okafor will hope to force his way into the first XI after scoring as a substitute against Spurs, while Harry Wilson, Brendan Aaronson and Joe Rodon are also contenders to earn a recall, the latter of whom recently recovered from a long-term injury.

Martinez; Acheampong, Fofana, Colwill; Neto, Caicedo, Henderson, Palestra; Estevao, Rogers, Palmer

Trafford; Justin, Elvedi, Muharemovic; Bogle, Tanaka, Ampadu, Gudmundsson; Wilson, Okafor; Calvert-Lewin

Chelsea have not been the same prolific outfit without the presence of Joao Pedro up front, and they could find it difficult to break down a robust Leeds backline without a natural focal point.

Despite only one of the Blues' last six Premier League matches seeing both teams score, we can see the net rippling at both ends on this occasion, with the hosts bouncing back from recent setbacks and edging to a slender victory.

#1820. Lille vs Lyon - prediction, team news, lineups

By Adeyeye Oluwapelumi | 19 Nov 2026 16:04, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 20:37

Lille will be looking to strengthen their position in the Ligue 1 title race when they welcome Lyon to the Stade Pierre-Mauroy on Saturday evening for matchday 11 action.

The hosts sit second in the Ligue 1 table with 21 points from their opening 10 matches, two behind leaders Paris Saint-Germain, while the fifth-placed visitors have 17 points and will be hoping to close the gap on their opponents in Carlos Vicens's first game in charge.

Lille head into the weekend in encouraging form after winning their last two league outings, beating Lens 1-0 before claiming a 2-1 victory away to Rennes prior to the international break, where Nathan Ngoy's second-half goal proved decisive.

Davide Ancelotti will be particularly pleased with how his side have rediscovered their rhythm after consecutive draws against Brest and Monaco derailed the Mastiffs' title charge, with the northern French outfit having lost just once in their opening 10 Ligue 1 fixtures (W6, D3).

Much of Lille's success this season has been built on their defensive solidity, with seven goals conceded representing the best record in the division, while five clean sheets leave them behind only Lorient (six) in that regard.

Les Dogues have also found the net in every league outing this season, although they have scored more than once in just 40% of their 10 top-flight matches, including two of their five fixtures on their own turf.

Nevertheless, Lille have been reliable at the Stade Pierre-Mauroy, winning three of their five Ligue 1 games at the ground and avoiding defeat in the other two to boast the division's fifth-best home record.

Victory on Saturday would not only strengthen the hosts' position in the standings but also provide a timely confidence boost ahead of Wednesday's Champions League meeting with Bayern Munich, with the Mastiffs currently second from bottom in the league phase table after collecting just one point from their opening four continental fixtures.

Vicens will also have one eye on next Thursday’s home meeting with Lillstrom in the Europa League, where Lyon sit 13th in the 36-team table after picking up seven points from their first four matches.

However, the Spanish coach's immediate priority will be to get his new side back to winning ways following a 2-0 defeat at Brest in Lyon's most recent league outing, which came under interim boss Jorge Maciel following the departure of Paolo Fonseca for Sporting Lisbon.

That setback further highlighted Lyon's struggles on the road, having now lost their last three Ligue 1 away matches while conceding exactly two goals in each of those outings, with their only victory in five domestic trips this season coming against Toulouse on the opening weekend.

Lille remain without Tiago Santos, who is expected to miss the remainder of the season after rupturing his cruciate ligament, while Hamza Igamane is also unavailable as he continues his recovery from an ACL injury, although a return is expected in December.

Ayase Ueda is doubtful after sustaining a plantar fascia injury, with the forward having resumed running but yet to return to full training, although Ancelotti previously suggested that the Japanese attacker could be available for this fixture.

Hakon Arnar Haraldsson has operated as a makeshift centre-forward in Ueda's absence and could continue in that position if the latter fails to recover in time, although veteran striker Olivier Giroud also provides an alternative.

Meanwhile, Lyon will be without Tyler Morton, who recently underwent surgery for an abductor problem, while Pavel Sulc is recovering from a meniscus injury and Mohamed Ouedraogo is sidelined for the remainder of the campaign after rupturing his cruciate ligament.

Lois Openda also remains unavailable as he recovers from a fractured fibula, although the forward is expected to return in the coming weeks, while Steeve Kango could be available after rejoining group training following a period under concussion protocol.

Competition: Serie A Date: Sunday, November 22, 2026 Kickoff: 19:45 GMT / 20:45 CET Venue: New Balance Arena, Bergamo

Verdict: Inter to win Best odds: 13/20 Bookmaker: 1xBet

It was Atalanta’s first away league win of the season and a useful response to the 3-0 home defeat against Parma. There were better attacking moments after the interval at Monza, too, with Krstovic and Mario Pasalic having opportunities to extend the lead.

Inter responded to its 3-1 derby defeat against Milan with a convincing 2-0 victory over Como. Francesco Pio Esposito and Marcus Thuram scored inside the opening 19 minutes, giving Cristian Chivu’s side an advantage it protected comfortably.

Lautaro Martinez and Thuram have returned to group training. Lautaro’s minutes are likely to be managed following his longer absence, while Thuram is further along in his recovery from muscular fatigue. Ange-Yoan Bonny and Aleksandar Stankovic remain unavailable.

Atalanta should take encouragement from the win at Monza, but the chances conceded in that match remain a concern against Inter’s attack. Chivu has greater depth available up front, and his side has shown enough consistency to justify favoritism.

#1818. Sonia Bompastor's side show their teeth as Chelsea sink the reigning champions to reclaim top spot in WSL title race: Chelsea 1-0 Man City

By SAMARA WATTS and TARA ANSON-WALSH, FOOTBALL REPORTER

Published: 10:42 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 11:33 EST, 15 November 2026

Chelsea secured a deserved 1-0 victory over Manchester City at Stamford Bridge to leapfrog their rivals and reclaim top spot in the WSL table.

Sandy Baltimore's first-half goal was enough to ensure Chelsea inflicted City's first defeat of the season and blow the title race wide open.

After keeping the reigning WSL champions at bay following an early barrage, Chelsea grew in confidence but still lacked the cutting edge that had seen them held to back-to-back draws in the past week.

A moment of magic from Baltimore in the fourth minute of stoppage time ensured history would not repeat itself.

City goalkeeper Ayaka Yamashita was sent off in the 75th minute for a rash challenge on Alyssa Thompson, a move which appeared to invigorate the visitors, but Chelsea held firm to pick up all three points.

Daily Mail Sport's Tara Anson-Walsh and Samara Watts were at Stamford Bridge to bring you the things we learned...

Chelsea inflicted City's first defeat of the season and blew the title race wide open

City goalkeeper Ayaka Yamashita was sent off in the 75th minute for a rash challenge on Alyssa Thompson

Devastation for Kadeisha Buchanan, who was hooked after 11 minutes by Bompastor. The centre back has been one of Chelsea’s standout performers this season but had an unusually shaky start to this match as she looked out of her depth against Bunny Shaw, ever a precarious place to be against the league’s top striker.

Buchanan gave an early ball away to allow Shaw to race through towards the Chelsea goal, and a few minutes later was again outmuscled and outpaced by the Jamaican striker, although City failed to capitalise on both occasions.

The 31-year-old Canada international looked devastated when her number flashed up on the board after just 12 minutes and reluctantly welcomed a hug from her manager as she headed straight for the tunnel.

Her replacement, the 20-year-old Veerle Buurman, who was outstanding against Shaw in the two sides’ last meeting in the FA Cup last season, changed the game, giving Chelsea a more solid platform to build upon as they grew in confidence.

Bompastor shut down suggestions that the move had been ruthlessly tactical at full time, saying that Buchanan had picked up a head injury during training on Friday.

'She was fine after the training session, she was fine in the evening and we assessed her again this morning and everything was fine,' Bompastor said.

'I had this information on what happened yesterday and I just felt, watching her from the beginning of the game, she was not herself. I took the responsibility to make this substitution. I was almost forced to do that because, I know my player, and I know she was not right in the game.'

For those sceptical, it certainly improved things.

The centre back has been one of Chelsea’s standout performers this season but had an unusually shaky start to this match and was hooked after just 11 minutes

Women’s football royalty Sarina Wiegman and Emma Hayes braved the chilly climes of Stamford Bridge to witness the showdown between the WSL heavyweights on Saturday afternoon.

The freshly anointed honorary Dame Wiegman sat next to Hayes and the pair chatted warmly, with Wiegman laughing as Hayes attempted to encourage her to celebrate Chelsea's victory at full time. This is a relationship that will no doubt drop in cordiality as the sand in the hourglass ahead of next summer’s World Cup continues to run down.

Wiegman had several England players on her watching brief, not least young Lexi Potter, whose stock has risen dramatically this season. The 20-year-old put in another assured performance against the reigning champions, continuing to demonstrate her maturity in the highest stakes, which will no doubt put her in a good position ahead of Tuesday’s squad announcement.

Elsewhere, the Dutch coach will have been alarmed by the number of crunching tackles put in against her right back, Lucy Bronze, in this match. If there is one player that she will want to wrap up in cotton wool ahead of Brazil, it is the recently turned 35-year-old Bronze for her steadfast leadership and relentless athleticism.

One player looking to make an impact ahead of Tuesday’s squad announcement was Aggie Beever-Jones, who has struggled this season and was left out of Sonia Bompastor’s starting line-up. An injury to Melvine Malard saw Beever-Jones gain more minutes than she would have expected, but it felt like another afternoon of deja vu for the 23-year-old forward as she failed to convert a number of chances despite finding herself in good positions.

Meanwhile, in Manchester, Ella Toone's hopes of forcing her way back into Sarina Wiegman's plans suffered another blow as the 27-year-old was once again left out of Eva Olid's starting line-up for United's 2-0 win over Crystal Palace. Toone watched on as fellow Lioness Maya Le Tissier opened the scoring with a superb long-range strike, and the two-time European champion will no doubt be growing increasingly concerned as Brazil draws closer.

The freshly anointed honorary dame Wiegman sat next to Hayes at the WSL showpiece at Stamford Bridge and the pair chatted warmly

Melvine Malard’s absence raises questions about who Chelsea’s main goalscorer will be this season. The squad has lacked a clinical edge without England striker Lauren James, who is out with a hamstring injury until the international break.

The French forward went off injured after 35 minutes with a suspected hamstring injury. Although she missed Chelsea’s opening games after picking up a knock in pre-season, she has been the Blues’ top scorer in the absence of Lauren James with six league goals so far.

Chelsea are averaging 24 shots per game, an unprecedented rate across a WSL campaign, but have recently struggled to convert their chances. They were held to a 0-0 draw against BK Hacken midweek in the UWCL and a 1-1 draw against Everton last weekend.

Malard leaving the pitch meant Chelsea struggled to find a creative spark up front. Her replacement Aggie Beever-Jones has been dealing with an ankle injury, and is still trying to find her feet with only one goal in the WSL.

Head coach Bompastor said: ‘The frustration sometimes comes from us not being ruthless and clinical.’

A moment of magic from Malard’s French international teammate Sandy Baltimore was enough to make it 1-0 just before half time with the team’s first shot on target. However, Baltimore was substituted at half time to manage her minutes, and Chelsea were unable to capitalize on any of their chances in the second half.

Bompastor said: ‘From the outside it seems like we have had a lot of injuries, but we have been playing every three days.’

‘I knew coming into the game we were not as fresh as we would like to be, but that’s our environment.

‘We want to play in every competition but the players are not robots,’

Melvine Malard’s injury could cause more problems for the Blues’ attack, as they registered just two shots on target today and scraped the three points.

Malard limped off in the first half and meant Chelsea struggled for a creative spark up front

Stamford Bridge was in uproar as City goalkeeper Ayaka Yamashita rushed out of her box and took down Alyssa Thompson, who had a clear chance on goal in the 75th minute.

The Blues were mounting a rapid attack down the left hand side, with Thompson just outside the box when Yamashita missed the ball and brought her to the ground.

The Japanese goalkeeper was shown a straight red card and was sent off the pitch. This was City’s first red card in the WSL since November 2023, and a rare moment of madness from the usually-composed 31-year-old.

The referee allowed City three minutes to replace the Japanese goalkeeper, with Scotland’s number one Eartha Cumings coming on to replace forward Aoba Fujino.

Her first test arrived only a minute later, as Aggie Beever-Jones' right-footed shot from the resulting indirect free kick dropped dangerously, but she was saved by the crossbar.

The bigger question now is whether Yamashita's absence - which could amass to three games - will have a lasting impact on their title race.

In the short-term against Chelsea, City reacted well. Andree Jeglertz said at full time: ‘The players dealt with it in a good way, so even though we were one player down we had a couple of great opportunities to score a goal. Of course it affected the game but that is not why we lost.’

Stamford Bridge was in uproar as Manchester City goalkeeper Ayaka Yamashita rushed out of her box to take down Alyssa Thompson, who had a clear chance on goal

Chelsea’s win at the Bridge blows the title race wide open, as they are now just one point ahead of City at the top of the WSL table.

Bompastor’s side ended City’s unbeaten streak, and they now have 24 league goals compared to City’s 16 after 10 games.

However, with seven shots and just one on target this game, Chelsea will need to look at their attacking options as they take on Liverpool and London City Lionesses before the international break.

Bompastor said: ‘It’s a nice feeling to be top of the table right now and to win against these top sides, but I know we still have a lot of work to be done and it’s early on in the season so many things can happen.’

City were unable to create opportunities in front of goal, with the WSL’s all-time leading goalscorer Vivianne Miedema’s return overshadowed by Ayaka Yamashita’s nightmare in goal.

City head coach Andree Jeglertz said: ‘They managed to score on their big chance and (it was a) great finish.

'We also had some great opportunities where we didn’t manage to score, but I think we deserve more than going away from here with no points.’

London City Lionesses face Arsenal tomorrow at the Emirates, and a win in north London could bring them four points behind the new WSL leaders, and really start to make things interesting.

#1815. Liverpool vs Man United: Why England's biggest rivalry still matters amid United crisis

By Naim Beneddra | 19 Nov 2026 16:09

Liverpool and Manchester United will renew one of English football's fiercest rivalries at Anfield on Sunday, but rarely have the two clubs approached this fixture from such contrasting positions.

Liverpool sit fourth in the Premier League under Andoni Iraola, while United arrive in the relegation zone following a disastrous start to the 2026-27 campaign that cost Michael Carrick his job.

Mauricio Pochettino's appointment has offered supporters renewed hope, although the Argentine could hardly have been handed a more demanding introduction. His first match in charge will be against the club United have historically regarded as their greatest rivals.

The circumstances are extraordinary. United have collected just eight points from their opening 10 league matches, winning only once, and are already 10 points behind Sunday's opponents.

Yet the gulf in the table has done little to diminish the significance of the occasion.

For Liverpool and United supporters, this fixture has never depended entirely on league positions. Its importance comes from generations of competition for domestic supremacy, the history of two neighbouring cities and the enduring desire to establish which club holds the greater place in English football.

Debates about England's greatest football rivalry inevitably produce different answers.

Arsenal and Tottenham Hotspur share one of the country's most intense local rivalries. Newcastle United and Sunderland have a derby rooted deeply in regional identity, while Manchester City and United have spent recent decades competing for the same major honours.

The historic tensions between Leeds United and Manchester United, or between Liverpool and Everton, are equally significant to the supporters involved.

Liverpool against United, however, occupies a distinctive position because it combines the prestige of two of England's most successful clubs with a rivalry between cities that predates professional football.

Liverpool developed into one of Britain's principal ports, while Manchester became an industrial powerhouse during the 19th century.

The opening of the Manchester Ship Canal in 1894 allowed goods to reach Manchester without passing through Liverpool's docks, becoming an enduring symbol of the economic competition between the two cities.

Football subsequently provided another arena for that rivalry.

Liverpool dominated English football during the 1970s and 1980s, winning league championships and European Cups while United struggled to match their domestic consistency.

The balance shifted dramatically under Sir Alex Ferguson.

United won 13 Premier League titles between 1993 and 2013, overtaking Liverpool's longstanding record of 18 English league championships in the process.

Ferguson's ambition to surpass Liverpool helped define United's most successful era, with the two clubs competing for supremacy even when they were not direct rivals for the title in a particular season.

Liverpool eventually ended their 30-year wait for a league championship under Jurgen Klopp in 2020 and drew level with United on 20 English top-flight titles by winning another in 2025.

That shared record has reinforced a rivalry measured across decades rather than individual seasons.

The head-to-head figures also demonstrate how closely contested the fixture has been historically.

Across 218 competitive meetings, United have recorded 85 victories to Liverpool's 72, with another 61 matches ending level.

However, those overall figures tell only part of the story.

Liverpool's extraordinary 7-0 victory at Anfield in March 2023 remains the largest winning margin in the fixture's history, while United demonstrated their ability to upset their rivals with a 3-2 victory at Old Trafford in May this year.

Results of that magnitude become part of the clubs' collective memories, ensuring that each new encounter carries the weight of previous triumphs and humiliations.

Sunday's meeting arrives at a particularly delicate moment for Manchester United.

The club's decision to replace Carrick with Pochettino reflects the scale of its problems, with a single Premier League victory leaving the Red Devils fighting to escape the bottom three.

The former Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea manager officially began work on November 18, giving him only a few days to assess his squad before travelling to Merseyside.

As previously examined in Sports Mole's analysis of Pochettino's appointment and his preferred approach, the Argentine has built much of his reputation around pressing, collective organisation and developing young players.

Those principles will take time to establish, particularly in a squad that has struggled defensively throughout the campaign.

Anfield nevertheless provides an immediate opportunity to change the atmosphere surrounding the club.

A positive result would not erase United's difficult start, but taking points away from Liverpool could offer Pochettino an early foundation on which to build.

Defeat, particularly a heavy one, would bring another wave of scrutiny to a side already facing questions about its competitiveness.

Liverpool have their own reasons to attach considerable importance to the match.

Iraola, who replaced Klopp's successor Arne Slot in the summer, is preparing for his first competitive encounter with United as Liverpool manager.

His team remain in the Champions League positions, although their fourth-place standing leaves them with ambitions of closing the gap on the leaders.

Sunday therefore represents an important test of Liverpool's progress under their new coach, as well as an opportunity to deepen their rivals' difficulties.

The stakes are different from those during the Ferguson era, when United regularly pursued championships, or the period when Liverpool were establishing themselves as Europe's dominant force.

But the nature of the rivalry means that United's current league position cannot make the match an ordinary fixture.

Both managers will experience this contest from their respective dugouts for the first time, while Pochettino faces the added challenge of beginning his United career in one of English football's most unforgiving away environments.

When Liverpool and Manchester United meet at Anfield on Sunday at 4.30pm, their immediate objectives will be markedly different.

For Liverpool, victory would strengthen their position near the top of the Premier League. For United, the occasion offers a chance to begin repairing a damaged season.

The rivalry itself has survived far greater changes in the fortunes of both clubs, and Sunday's encounter will be another reminder of why their meetings continue to command such attention.
