#1799. FIFA Slaps Real Madrid, Atletico Madrid With 1-Year Transfer Bans

Home » Home 2 » FIFA Slaps Real Madrid, Atletico Madrid With 1-Year Transfer Bans

The ban will start from the July transfer window this year and finish with the January transfer market in 2017.

Atletico were also fined 900,000 Swiss francs (820,000 euros) and Real 360,000 (330,000 euros).

“The two clubs were found to have violated several provisions concerning the international transfer and first registration of minor players as well as other relevant provisions with regard to the registration and participation of certain players in competitions,” said a FIFA statement.

Barcelona has just ended a one year ban for similar reasons.

Real and Atletico were “issued with a reprimand and given 90 days in which to regularise the situation of all minor players concerned,” FIFA said. They can still sell players during the transfer ban.

FIFA said the alarm was raised over the two clubs by FIFA’s Transfer Matching System and its disciplinary committee completed the inquiry.

Under international football rules, players under 18 cannot be transferred to another country, except in limited circumstances. All transfers need the approval of a special FIFA committee.

“The investigations concerned minor players who were involved and participated in competitions with the clubs over various periods between 2007 and 2014 (Atletico Madrid) and between 2005 and 2014 (Real Madrid),” FIFA said.

The ban follows a similar sanction handed to European champions Barcelona, who were unable to register new players during 2015.

Barca were initially banned in April 2014, but managed to delay the sanction taking affect until the transfer windows in January and the summer 2015 by launching an ultimately unsuccessful appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS).

By delaying the ban, Barca managed to sign the likes of Luis Suarez and Ivan Rakitic in the summer of 2014 to propel them to a treble of La Liga, Champions League and Copa del Rey.

The news is just the latest institutional embarassment for Real Madrid just over a week after they appointed French legend Zinedine Zidane.

Madrid have sacked two Champions League winning coaches in Carlo Ancelotti and Rafael Benitez in the past seven months, as well as being thrown out of the Copa del Rey for fielding an ineligible player.

The sanction could also be bad news for the likes of Paris Saint-Germain and Manchester United, who had targeted Madrid stars Cristiano Ronaldo and Gareth Bale with Real highly unlikely to dispose of their best players without the chance to sign suitable replacements.

La Liga leaders Atletico Madrid’s usually hectic transfer policy will also be put on hold. However, Diego Simeone’s men look better placed to cope with the ban having invested heavily in young talent over the past year.

Neither Real no Atletico made an immediate comment on whether they would appeal.

#1798. Amed SK vs Caykur Rizespor - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joshua Cole | 19 Nov 2026 16:47

Amed SK will be looking to maintain their perfect home record in the Turkish Super Lig when they welcome Caykur Rizespor to Diyarbakir Stadium on Saturday afternoon.

The hosts sit third in the table with 23 points from 11 matches, while the visitors are 11th on 14 points, nine behind their opponents, although the visitors will arrive with renewed confidence after ending their winless run before the international break.

Amed had enjoyed an impressive run of results before their league outing against Galatasaray, remaining unbeaten in eight consecutive games (W6, D2) and winning three successive matches against Konyaspor, Samsunspor and Eyupspor.

Besnik Hasi's side beat Konyaspor 1-0 at home, secured a 2-1 victory away to Samsunspor and then produced an emphatic 5-1 win over Eyupspor, but that positive run was eventually brought to an end by Galatasaray.

Amed were far from overawed in Istanbul, scoring three goals in a thrilling 4-3 defeat, their second loss in 11 league matches, which has left them third with seven wins, two draws and two defeats from their opening 11 fixtures.

The hosts have been carried by their attack, scoring 28 goals during that period to become one of the most productive sides in the division, with only Fenerbahce (29) finding the net more times.

Their home form has been particularly impressive, as they have won all six of their league matches at Diyarbakir Stadium, scoring 19 goals and conceding just four, a run they will be confident of extending against a Rizespor side that has struggled for consistency.

This will be the first league meeting between these sides, although they have faced each other twice in the Turkish Cup, with both teams recording a home victory.

Rizespor, meanwhile, have endured a difficult spell, losing three consecutive league matches against Fenerbahce, Corum and Trabzonspor before drawing 0-0 away to Kocaelispor, following an earlier 2-2 stalemate with Goztepe.

However, Recep Ucar's side finally returned to winning ways before the international break, beating Erzurumspor 2-1 at home, with the victory ending a five-match winless run in the league and providing a much-needed boost ahead of their trip to Diyarbakir.

Their away form has been considerably stronger than their results at home, with three wins, two draws and one defeat from six road matches, although they are now winless in their last three away outings (D2, L1).

The Black Sea Sparrowhawks failed to score in an away game for the first time this season in the goalless draw at Kocaelispor, while the last time they failed to find the net in consecutive away matches was towards the end of the previous campaign, during a six-match winless run on the road.

Amed will be without Samuel Ballet, who is serving a suspension following his red card against Eyupspor, while Berat Percin and Veysel Sapan are also unavailable.

Ermal Krasniqi and Lumbardh Dellova are injury doubts, with both players facing uncertainty over their availability for Saturday's match, while Gokhan Gul could also be absent.

Ballet's suspension is a significant blow to Amed's attacking options, although Gift Orban is expected to lead the attack, with Dia Saba supporting him and Mbaye Diagne also in contention to feature.

Rizespor are expected to be without Can Bozdogan, Valentin Mihaila and Gennaro Borrelli, who are all dealing with injury problems.

Meanwhile, Khusniddin Alikulov remains sidelined as he continues his recovery from a cruciate ligament injury.

Lafont; Meras, Bates, Yesil, Acer; Raveloson, Soyalp; Lutin, Saba, Sor; Orban

Caykur Rizespor possible starting lineup:

Gorgen; Pala, Mocsi, Bakayoko, Ariss; Diakite; Mebude, Olawoyin, Laci, Kutucu; Sowe

Amed have been outstanding at home this season, winning all six of their league matches at Diyarbakir Stadium while scoring 19 goals and conceding just four, and their attacking record makes them difficult to oppose, which is why we expect Hasi's side to return to winning ways and extend their perfect home record.

#1797. Same old Spurs given reality check of epic proportions

The players and the transfer fees might be different, but this was same old Tottenham Hotspur. The same Tottenham that finished each of the last two seasons in 17th. The same Tottenham that folded in adversity. The same Tottenham that opposition fans loved to laugh at.

Of course, it is very early days and the good news for Spurs fans and head coach Roberto De Zerbi is the side that started the opening day humiliation to Brentford may well never play together again this season.

But in a summer in which Tottenham have allowed their fans to dream of good times ahead by breaking the bank in the transfer window, this was a reality check of epic proportions.

The Spurs supporters who have become sick of being made the butt of their rivals’ jokes had to listen to Brentford fans singing “Thomas Frank, he’s laughing at you” in reference to the Dane’s unhappy spell in north London.

The impending arrival of Savinho will take Tottenham’s spending over £300m, but none of their big-money debutants at the Gtech Community Stadium hit the ground running.

There was only one man who looked anything close to a £100m player and it was not Sandro Tonali.

Tottenham’s first-ever £100m signing was completely upstaged by Brentford’s Mamadou Sangaré on his first competitive start for the club, as Spurs were run ragged.

Sangaré might not have scored on his Brentford debut, but he had a major contribution in two of his side’s goals and bossed the middle of the park. He deservedly received a standing ovation when he was substituted with 15 minutes remaining.

“He is a top player, no doubt about it,” said head coach Keith Andrews. “He is the one we were after in the window. The club deserve a lot of credit because a lot of clubs were looking at him.

“He deserves a lot of credit too, because he could have gone elsewhere for a few more bob. He recognised this would be a good place to come and he has settled quite nicely.”

A club-record £39m signing from French club Lens, Sangaré may prove to be a steal for Brentford. He ran the game for long periods and was responsible for Keane Lewis-Potter’s opening goal.

Having played a lovely one-two with Dango Ouattara, Sangaré kept his cool to brilliantly pick out Lewis-Potter and give him the easy task of finding the back of the net.

Keane Lewis-Potter scores Brentford's first goal of the new season!Brilliant play from record signing Mamadou Sangaré 👏 pic.twitter.com/Ua9HklQaWh

Later in the first half, Sangaré won a free-kick in his own half thanks to some quick feet and the action produced a big cheer from the home fans.

Tonali was the subject of chants of “what a waste of money” from Brentford supporters. It was a volley that sailed high over the crossbar that prompted that particular song, but Tonali was not just off target with his shooting.

He lost possession on a couple of occasions at both ends of the pitch and allowed Brentford players to glide past him during the opening stages of the match. He struggled to get around the pitch and Tottenham generally lacked desire and fight – two things that clubs cannot buy.

Richarlison, Lucas Bergvall and goalkeeper Antonin Kinsky can all be disappointed with Brentford’s second goal. Richarlison’s hold-up play was terrible, Bergvall produced a weak challenge that allowed Mathias Jensen to take the ball and shoot, and Kinsky parried the ball straight into the path of Vitaly Janelt, who scored.

Kinsky has been trusted to take over from Guglielmo Vicario as Tottenham’s number one this season, but this was not a good start.

Vitaly Janelt doubles Brentford's lead! 🐝 pic.twitter.com/AYh5BGhJBQ

De Zerbi spent much of the first half telling his back four to get higher up the pitch and it was perhaps understandable that captain for the day Archie Gray, Jan Paul van Hecke, Marcos Senesi and Andy Robertson looked like a group of strangers.

This was the foursome’s first competitive game together, but De Zerbi will need his Tottenham players to get to know each other as fast as possible if they are to challenge for Europe this season or even finish in the top half of the table.

Bergvall and Conor Gallagher were hooked at half-time, with Tottenham two goals behind and De Zerbi clearly unimpressed. But the Italian’s changes did not prompt an instant response. In fact, things got even worse.

Once again, Sangaré was heavily involved. He produced a well-hit shot that Kinsky had to save. For the second time, the goalkeeper failed to push the ball out of trouble and Michael Kayode was able to score.

Michael Kayode with a third for Brentford just three minutes into the second half! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/40kOIlV5MU

Igor Thiago missed a penalty after substitute Rodrigo Bentancur fouled Kevin Schade, as Spurs threatened to completely collapse with the result already pretty much decided.

Igor Thiago's penalty CRASHES off the post! ❌ pic.twitter.com/jZUEoIA44h

De Zerbi can console himself with the fact his Spurs team will quickly look a lot different. There are more new faces to come in, with winger Savinho on the brink of joining and Tottenham hoping Omar Marmoush will follow him from Manchester City.

Mikey Moore, who forced Brentford goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher into two second-half saves, is expected to join Cologne on loan and Mohammed Kudus is close to returning from injury, while Micky van de Ven and Pedro Porro will come back in.

But if ever there was proof that spending a fortune offers no guarantee of happiness, then this was it.

Roberto De Zerbi has admitted that big-spending Tottenham Hotspur “are not a team yet” after watching his new-look side fall to an opening-day defeat to Brentford.

Tottenham have splashed out over £200m on new players, but head coach De Zerbi has warned it will be impossible to set any targets until they become a team.

Record £100m signing Sandro Tonali made his competitive debut for Tottenham, along with fellow new signings Jan Paul van Hecke, Marcos Senesi, Mateus Fernandes and Andy Robertson.

Tottenham have been tipped to challenge for European qualification, having finished 17th in each of the last two seasons, but De Zerbi acknowledged those optimistic predictions may have come too soon.

His team looked like strangers in their humiliating loss at Brentford and the Italian said: “We are not a team yet for a lot of reasons. We can fix the target [for the season] when you become a team. Before you become a team, you can’t say what you can do.

“You can’t become a team from the transfer market on paper. You become a team when the players find a connection, a spirit, a soul.

“We are not at the right point in our physical condition for a lot of reasons. Late from the World Cup and because in Australia [on pre-season], we don’t work in the right way. But no excuses, it’s a normal situation when you are building a new project. I don’t want time but we have to pass through these problems.

“I am surprised by the result and performance. They [Brentford] deserved to win and we played very bad. I knew we were not in the right condition. We can’t find an excuse. I am sorry for the result and performance.

“Marcos Senesi, Jan Paul van Hecke and Sandro Tonali are not in the best physical condition. We knew that before the game. We have to improve on that and many other things, like organisation and pressing.

“We can improve quickly but first, we have to understand this game better. I know their physical condition and [they are] new players but we have to put something more.

“We had to fight more. Players know I have a lot of confidence in them and we hope to improve quickly. Until we reach these conditions we have to suffer and today is an important defeat. Maybe we can wake up stronger.”

We had some problems with the timing of the pressure, we arrived too often late. We lost too many duels to compete with Brentford. I am sorry for that and sorry for the defeat. We have to improve in the physical condition and the organisation.

It was the first game and part of our journey, we knew we had a lot of new players. To become a team I said before the game we need two things, soul and style of play. We didn’t fight in the right way. Brentford is maybe one of the most important teams in the Premier League in terms of duels.

It was a game, especially in the first half, in one direction. We were not in the right position to make the high pressure, with Mikey Moore on the left centre.

We didn’t play well, we didn’t play in the right way. I think not because we don’t remember last season, because these players are good people but we lost too many duels. One of the best qualities of Brentford is the one-to-one, the man-to-man and the set-pieces.

Really pleased. Felt like there was a performance coming, you never really know after pre-season. The reality is the first game of the season comes and it can quickly come unstuck. I felt good for a number of weeks about how we were coming together. I was pretty pleased.

Our fans were amazing today. There is a genuine connection here that helps. I thought we started the game brilliantly and they were fully engaged. We want to be relentless. We looked like a real team.

That’s what we wanted, we wanted to start sharp, we want to show people what we’re made of and we did that today. We know last season we were one point off, this year, we’ve added quality people to the squad.

He’s been unbelievable, I can’t praise him high enough. He’s one of them players that we might lose the ball you just know he is going to win it back and he gets us on the counter-attack so quickly.

Is that Pedro Porro, Micky Van de Ven and Mohammed Kudus could be back for the next game against Newcastle, and Savinho ought to be through the door.

According to Opta, Brentford won the xG battle 3.96 to 0.47, taking 26 shots to Spurs’s nine. De Zerbi’s team finished the game with 59 per cent possession, but that is inflated by Brentford sitting off when three up. It’s the most xG Spurs have conceded in a single game since a 6-3 defeat by Liverpool in December 2024.

Less Christ the Redeemer more Christ, that was terrible.

"I think that sums it up"Fair to say this Spurs fan wasn't pleased with their performance 😅 pic.twitter.com/ZAdVaVbjlS

Possibly Brentford’s best performance under Keith Andrews, though that may be overstating the strength of the opposition. This was a complete display: they pressed Spurs, they played through Spurs, they played over Spurs, they dominated Spurs from set-pieces and their defenders bullied Spurs’s forwards. It will be interesting to hear from De Zerbi and whether he is philosophical or irate. This is far from Spurs’s ideal projected team, but still unacceptable.

Kinsky palms away a Damsgaard corner, and Yarmoliuk slices his shot over the bar. We are deep into stoppage time, and Brentford’s players are still pressing Bentnacur and Senesi and making them play with their heads down.

Just four minutes of added time to play but Spurs have more defending to do in the shape over another Brentford corner. They survive, but Brentford quickly establish possession again.

It would appear Lord Sugar is still watching:

To all Spurs fans don't worry this is all tactical to lure other teams into believing we are a easy touch. #coys

Another Brentford debut: Callum Wilson replaces Igor Thiago. Destiny Udogie has replaced Archie Gray for Spurs. “You should have signed for a big club!” sing the Brentford fans, in reference to the club almost signing Gray two summers ago. Football fans never forget.

Another Brentford goal would put them top of the table, for what that is worth. Spurs enjoying some possession in the Brentford half now, but it is entirely sterile.

Igor Thiago’s shot is blocked, Brentford still look the more likely team to score the next goal. Jadon Anthony shows he has a long throw, which might be a small reason why Brentford decided to sign him. Janelt then drags back Maddison.

Jadon Anthony involved in some Brenford pressure that results in a long throw and a corner, but the new man then slices a volley over the bar. Standing ovation at the Gtech for Sangare as he makes way for Damsgaard, while Hickey replaces Kayode. Be tough to beat his performance as debut of the weekend.

Michael Oliver letting some meaty challenges go, the game is quite feisty despite the scoreline. Schade launched himself into a tackle on Solanke but he did not really catch him with his studs.

A few Spurs fans may have thought better of staying to watch the final 20 minutes. I wonder “if” this Spurs fan has switched the television off?

First match if season . Smiling before the game. Hope to be smiling after. pic.twitter.com/hsTc79PBti

Richarlison beats the turf and Ajer punches the air after the Brentford defender wins the foul. Andrews is making another couple of changes: Jensen and Ouattara off, Yarmoliuk and new signing Jadon Anthony on.

Two more Spurs changes too: Maddison and Solanke on, Moore and Richarlison off.

Really sharp save from Kelleher to keep out Moore’s powerful shot from close range. Moore has at least carried a threat for Spurs in the second half, but they are struggling to sustain much pressure.

Tonali with a hit from 25 yards but it deflects comfortably into the arms of Kelleher. Surely a (Kew?) bridge too far for Spurs to dig out any kind of result from here.

De Zerbi looks a little resigned on the touchline, he will know that this is far from his ideal Spurs team on the pitch but that cannot excuse such poor standards.

He fails to open his account for the season. Sent Kinsky the wrong way, but he dragged the penalty just a touch and it cannoned off the post. The lead remains three.

Igor Thiago's penalty CRASHES off the post! ❌ pic.twitter.com/jZUEoIA44h

Spurs are being overpowered here, they cannot cope whenever Brentford come forward. There were appeals for handball against Van Hecke after Janelt swivelled and shot, but the foul is given against Bentancur for bundling over Schade. A complete mess for Spurs.

Any hope that the half-time double change would bring a revival now appear forlorn.

But here is a chance for Mikey Moore! Robertson forward to good effect, and his low cross arrives to Moore at the back post but his shot was too close to Kelleher. Almost crept through his legs.

Well that is surely game over. Cracking strike from Sangare from the edge of the box after a Brentford corner is cleared, they have always been so good at winning those second balls. Driven strike, good save from Kinsky and Kayode is first to the rebound to score from a couple of yards.

Michael Kayode with a third for Brentford just three minutes into the second half! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/40kOIlV5MU

Important defensive header from Van Hecke to repel Sangare’s dangerous cross, and we enjoy our first look at a Kayode long throw. Some Strictly Come Dancing moves from Senesi and Collins in the penalty area, and the referee has a word with them. It continues when the throw is taken, and Sensi has a chunk of his shirt, but VAR says the Spurs man was fouled beforehand.

Will we see a different Tottenham in the second half.

Gallagher and Bergvall hooked, replaced by Bentancur and Fernandes who makes his Spurs debut.

15 - There was 15 passes in the build-up to Keane Lewis-Potter's opening goal for Brentford, only Michael Kayode's goal v Wolves in March (19) and Rico Henry's goal v Bournemouth in December (18) have seen more in a Premier League goal for the Bees under Keith Andrews.Busy. pic.twitter.com/8j5RZWFxvH

This has been a dreadful start to the season by Tottenham. Sandro Tonali has barely looked like a £10m player, let alone a £100m midfielder and, maybe unsurprisingly, De Zerbi’s players look like strangers. He will demand a major improvement in the second half. Keith Andrews will be delighted - maybe other than the fact the game isn’t already dead. His team have been dominant.

Brentford utterly dominant, there has been an alarming gulf in industry, precision and class between the two teams. Spurs will surely improve, both in the second half and as the season goes on, but this has fallen well below the standards you expect of a team with European aspirations. If a few of these players never played for De Zerbi again they could have no complaints.

No sign of a Spurs revival at half time, Brentford playing through their press with ease and then have space to run into. Kayode wins his header at the back post but no player was there for the knockdown.

Important block from Ajer after Spurs’s best piece of combination play around the box, before Tonali slashes a volley well over the bar from distance. Cue “what a waste of money” from the home fans.

Richarlison has been non-existent up front for Spurs, bullied by Collins and Ajer.

Tonali with a stray midfield pass to Outtara which rather sums up the Spurs performance so far. Surely there will be sweeping changes from De Zerbi at half time. Solanke, Maddison and Fernandes are the three players you’d have in mind.

“You’re going down with the Fulham,” is the chant from the Brentford fans.

Lewis-Potter swings in a dangerous cross, headed down by Kayode, and Van Hecke stoops to block Outtara’s shot. The whistle goes for a high boot.

This is far from Spurs’s strongest hypothetical team but they are being taken to the cleaners here. Spurs caught in that Brentford man-to-man press again and the ball bounces off Richarlison. Jensen shoots with power from the edge of the box, and Kinsky bats the shot back into danger, and there was Janelt to poke the rebound home. Brentford in total control.

Vitaly Janelt doubles Brentford's lead! 🐝 pic.twitter.com/AYh5BGhJBQ

Spurs’s defence breached again, and Outtara really should have made it two but his first touch was far too heavy and Kinsky was able to clear. Spurs will not be the only team to struggle against this Brentford front three. Schade won the flick on, Thiago swept the ball across the box, but the finish was lacking from Outtara.

Outtara fouls his former Bournemouth team-mate in the Spurs box. A lovely chipped pass forward from Schade releases Thiago in the left channel and another spell of home pressure begins. Lewis-Potter roaming everywhere. Then Brentford win a free-kick which will go in the mixer. Senesi fouled Outtara.

Bergvall floats in a decent cross from the left but it splits Richarlison and Moore. Sweden manager Graham Potter is in the stands watching Bergvall. Van Hecke is known for his progressive passes, but he overhits one through for a Brentford goal kick.

Spurs players not happy with Michael Oliver. Conor Gallagher feels he was pulled back in midfield, before Oliver blows for a 50:50 in Brentford’s favour.

All so simple for Brentford to get at Spurs again, and it takes some excellent defending on the cover from Robertson to deny Outarra who could have been through for a second goal.

Igor Thiago’s header hits the bar but the flag goes up for offside. Brentford’s man-to-man press is smothering Spurs at the moment, they cannot break through it to establish any territory higher up the pitch.

Igor Thiago makes enough of a nuisance of himself to force Senesi to put the ball out for a throw, Brazil vs Argentina in the match up. Brentford just look sharper and more match-ready all over the pitch.

Half a chance for Spurs to reply with a quickfire equaliser, but Tel’s free-kick was tame and deflected through to Kelleher. De Zerbi can have no complaints, it was one-way traffic before the goal.

Well that’s a good early impression from Sangare. He played a lovely one-two before picking out Lewis-Potter for Brentford’s goal.

To say this opening Brentford goal was on the cards would be a mammoth understatement. The home team are finding it so easy to progress the ball to dangerous positions around the Spurs box.

The new man Sangare is involved, playing a one-two at the edge of the area, before picking out Lewis-Potter who was unmarked on the penalty spot. Brentford’s left back popping up in the box, and it is a simple finish.

Keane Lewis-Potter scores Brentford's first goal of the new season!Brilliant play from record signing Mamadou Sangaré 👏 pic.twitter.com/Ua9HklQaWh

Pretty much Spurs’s first meaningful foray over the halfway line, but Gallagher’s shot from distance is wild. In other news, Jon Bon Jovi is in the stands. He popped up at a few games at the World Cup.

Brentford continue to make inroads down their left, Lewis-Potter driving at Gray and whipping in a dangerous cross that glanced off Van Hecke at the near post and only just wide of the far post. The corner is swung to the unmarked Sangare at the back post, and his header loops well over.

Brentford continue to look the better team, moving the ball at pace in the final third, but Schade stumbles up against Bergvall in the box. Spurs yet to settle of establish any possession in the game so far.

Collins then catches Gallagher on the foot, as the Spurs man rushed into a challenge to close the defender down. Not much in it.

From that free-kick, Jenson’s delivery was a wicked one: inswinging and flat to the near post, and the ball glanced off Robertson’s head and behind for a corner.

Jensen then tees up Lewis-Potter for an ambitious volley from the edge of the box, and there are hopeful appeals for a handball penalty against Gallagher, and then Collins fails to divert to follow up cross on target.

Not the most distinctive contrast between the two kits, but not as bad as Newcastle vs Bayer Leverkusen in pre-season.

Brentford on the front foot in the early exchanges, Sangare involve in their first attack, but Tel runs back to defend well against Kayode.

Schade then wins a free-kick from Van Hecke in a crossing position wide left, the forward’s feet were too quick for the Dutch defender.

The usual rendition of Hey Jude before the game in south west London.

[On three of the back four being new signings] I have a big confidence because all three are very important players with experience and qualities. They have been working for one month and we have no problem with them.

[On Gray wearing the armband] He’s very young but he is a big personality. great behaviour and he deserves to be a captain today. He cannot suffer too much pressure because he is an important player for us for a long time.

[On if there is more business to be done] We have not the right or complete squad today but no excuse we have the qualities to compete against an important team with a clear style, they are very strong in set-pieces and long balls especially.

This will be a first look at new signing Mamadou Sangare for Brentford fans. Lots of people have tipped him to be one of the signings of the summer. I haven’t seen enough of him to give an opinion but it will be interesting to see how he gets on against Tottenham’s first-ever £100m man Sandro Tonali.

There’s a decent chance this Tottenham starting line-up will not play again together for the rest of this season. Mikey Moore is expected to move to Cologne on loan, while Savinho’s arrival will relegate Mathys Tel to the bench. Spurs also have Mohamed Kudus and Xavi Simons to return from injury. De Zerbi will want a good start to the season, but this is not the Tottenham side he will be relying upon moving forwards.

There will be no easing into life at Spurs for Robertson, who faces Dango Outtara in one of the game’s key duels. The Scot has plenty of experience of course, but there were signs towards the end of time at Liverpool that he had started to struggle in one-on-ones against wingers.

Archie Gray will become Tottenham’s youngest-ever captain tonight. Aged 20 years and 163 days, he will beat Steve Perryman’s record of 20 years and 260 days. On Friday, De Zerbi listed all of his captains with Gray down in fifth place. New permanent captain Micky van de Ven misses the trip to Brentford through injury.

If we include the league goals Mikey Moore scored while on loan at Rangers last season, Spurs’s front three scored 22 league goals combined last season. By contrast, Igor Thiago, Kevin Schade and Dango Outtara scored 37 between them in the Premier League. Brentford are firm favourites with the bookies for this one, and that difference in firepower is probably why. Omar Marmoush could help matters.

Seventeen-year-old Luca Williams-Barnett is one of the outstanding players in the country at his age group, and there is a lot of excitement about him at Spurs. Post-Kane, the club’s academy has not delivered much bona fide first-team quality, but Williams-Barnett appears on that trajectory.

Brentford XI: Kelleher, Schade, Jensen, Thiago, Ouattara, Sangare, Ajer, Collins, Lewis-Potter, Janelt, Kayode

Subs: Valdimarsson, Hickey, Henry, Pinnock, Yarmoliuk, Wilson, Anthony, Damsgaard, Schuster

Your Bees to kick-off the 26/27 season 🐝 pic.twitter.com/nJO5emjgQM

Spurs XI: Kinsky; Gray, Van Hecke, Senesi, Robertson; Gallagher, Tonali, Bergvall; Moore, Richarlison, Tel

Subs: Dubravka, Danso, Maddison, Udogie, Fernandes, Solanke, Bentancur, Davies, Williams-Barnett

Our Spurs side on the opening day 🤍🔢 @krakenfx pic.twitter.com/Uh5z221aTc

Starting the season in west London 📌 pic.twitter.com/uglTu9zDvA

Former managers Mauricio Pochettino, José Mourinho, Antonio Conte and Ange Postecoglou will all be scratching their heads about Spurs’ change of strategy in the club’s first post-Levy summer.

It was Postecoglou who publicly shared his belief that Spurs would never spend £100m on a player and yet, just over a year after his departure, the club splashed out exactly that on midfielder Tonali.

Whereas Postecoglou and his predecessors often had to answer questions over Spurs’ perceived profligacy, De Zerbi has been able to tease fans with promises of “bomba” signings.

Good evening and welcome to our live coverage of Brentford vs Tottenham Hotspur in the Premier League, a London derby between the smart spenders and the big spenders.

That is probably an unfair dichotomy, because Spurs’s squad has been crying out for investment, and that has certainly arrived this summer. The club’s new leadership team has overseen more than £300m worth of purchases.

The arrival of Jean Paul van Hecke and Marcos Senesi, two of the league’s best progressive passers from centre-back, makes it clear that improving Spurs’s build up play is a priority for Roberto De Zerbi.

De Zerbi wants his teams to draw pressure from opponents and progress down the middle of the pitch with short passes, so it was imperative that Spurs upgraded in midfield. They have done just that by buying Mateus Fernandes and Sandro Tonali, for a combined £185m.

Spurs’s forward options remain much the same though, which could prove a drag in the season’s early weeks. Compared to Manchester United, Chelsea, and Liverpool, Spurs do not have the same firepower, but they should have more control and solidity this season.

Brentford lost just three league games at home last season, and they were unfortunate not to qualify for Europe. A lighter workload offers Keith Andrews the chance to consolidate on an excellent first season as head coach, and perhaps overtake some of those clubs with continental commitments.

Midfielder Mamadou Sangaré, signed for £39m from Lens, looks the pick of their summer business, tipped to be a £100m sale to one of the big boys (which is an unromantic perspective on the transfer, but very much Brentford’s model).

Asked about the Mali international, Andrews said: “He’s a very talented midfielder who can do lots of different aspects of that role.

“He’s a very focused, very determined and very ambitious young man. He’s very humble but equally as hungry to achieve impressive things. He’s certainly a player on an upward trajectory.”

Forwards Jadon Anthony and Callum Wilson are other arrivals, and Michael Kayode’s long throws will continue to be a serious weapon.

Luis Suarez and Jeremy Mathieu, who were also left out by Luis Enrique for the midweek Copa del Rey clash, have also returned to the FC Barcelona squad against Malaga.

Neymar Jr. on the other hand, has been left out the Matchday squad by Enrique owing to a minor hamstring injury. Although the initial scans have discounted any major tear in his hamstring, Luis Enrique is unlikely to take any risks with his star Brazilian forward.

#1794. Sampdoria swept aside by rampant Napoli – are the Partenopei on course for their first Scudetto in 26 years?

Home » Home 2 » Sampdoria swept aside by rampant Napoli – are the Partenopei on course for their first Scudetto in 26 years?

Dries Mertens celebrating with his team-mates on the touchline after his decisive goal in the 4-2 victory at Sampdoria is typical of the spirit and togetherness that has seen Napoli storm to the top of the Serie A title. It was in dedication to Chelsea loanee Nathaniel Chabolah who recently lost his mother a a nice touch to show that there is much more to life than football, even though they have put themselves in a wonderful position to end Juventusa dominance and end a 26-year wait for the Scudetto.

Five straight wins have put Maurizio Sarria s team two points clear at the top, with the former Empoli manager breathing a new lease of life throughout a team that have always looked capable of competing for the title, yet ultimately fallen short when the pressure to deliver grew. He has transformed the entire dynamics of how Napoli play, with clinical attacking movement combined with a rock-solid defence within a 4-3-3 system that is getting the very best from the players at his disposal. This seasona s statistics proved that point; Napoli are far and away the highest scorers in Serie A this season, while only Inter Milan and Juventus have a better defensive record. Just one defeat in the twenty league games since the opening day loss at Sassuolo is another illustration of just how good Napoli have been this season, with the crushing 4-0 win at AC Milan in early October a sign of what the Partenopei are truly capable of.

Juventus were always likely to be favourites for the Scudetto on Coral and any other football odds site as their dominance of Italian football threatens to extend into its fifth season, so it is perhaps refreshing from a purista s perspective that Napoli have emerged as real contenders to challenge the Bianconeri. Massimo Allegria s side have stormed up the table in ominous fashion following a surprisingly slow start to the season, with eleven straight victories serving a serious warning to Napoli that they will make them fight all the way for the 2015/2016 Serie A title. It remains to be seen how Sarri and his team handle the pressure of having Juventus breathing down their necks, but the fact they have scored twelve goals in their last three games would indicate that

Some may have been surprised by Gonzalo Higuaina s decision to swap Real Madrid for Naples in the summer of 2013, but the 28-year-old has become one of the most feared strikers in Italy. The Argentine international has formed a wonderful strikeforce at the front of a three-man attack, with Jose Callejon and Lorenzo Insigne adding searing pace and skill on either side of a frontman who has made a career from being a true predator inside the box.

Twenty-one games in as many Serie A games this season puts him amongst the most in-form strikers in world football, with his clinical finish which opened the scoring against Sampdoria proving just how good he has been in front of goal. It is the sort of purple patch that any striker worth their salt would dream to be in; Coral have unsurprisingly backed Higuain as favourite to score in their next game against Sarria s former employers Empoli who have kept just one clean sheet from their last five league fixtures. Napoli will need Higuain to carry his rich vein of form throughout the rest of the season if they are to have any chance of maintaining their wonderful pace and sprint clear of the chasing pack.

Napoli have won many admirers across Europe for the quality of football they have played this season, but it remains to be seen if they have the mentality to pass the acid test and keep the momentum going between now and the end of the season. Recent history would suggest that their chances are not great; the Partenopei, then managed by Walter Mazzarri, put themselves in a wonderful position in 2012/2013, only to finish runners-up behind Juventus as the odd slip at the wrong times proved costly in their pursuit of Juventus. A number of third-placed finishes would also suggest that Napoli have lacked the mentality and guile to end their long wait for a Scudetto, but there is real excitement in Naples that the current crop of players have what it takes to stop the Old Lady from making it five titles in a row.

#1793. Kocaelispor vs Fenerbahce - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joshua Cole | 19 Nov 2026 16:48, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 16:53

Kocaelispor will be looking to extend their unbeaten run when they welcome Fenerbahce to Turka Arac Muayene Kocaeli Stadium on Saturday evening in the Turkish Super Lig.

Both teams are tied on 19 points from their opening 11 matches, with the hosts seventh in the table, one place below the visitors in sixth, although the Yellow Canaries have scored considerably more goals this season and therefore boast a significantly better goal difference.

Kocaelispor have responded positively to consecutive defeats against Besiktas and Goztepe, going unbeaten in their last three league matches.

Their latest outing produced a 2-0 victory away to Eyupspor, following a goalless draw at home to Caykur Rizespor and a 2-1 victory over Alanyaspor, while they also recorded a 3-0 win over Mazidagi in the Turkish Cup during that run.

Selcuk Inan's side have built their season around a solid defensive foundation, with the hosts having conceded nine goals, a tally bettered only by Trabzonspor (8), giving them the second-best defence in the league, although the Gulf have scored the fewest goals among teams in the top half of the table (13).

Their home form has also been encouraging, with three victories, one draw and one defeat from five league matches at Kocaeli Stadium, where they have scored six goals and conceded just two, although they have failed to win either of their last two home fixtures (D1, L1).

However, Kocaelispor have struggled in this fixture over the years, failing to win any of their last 14 meetings with Fenerbahce, losing nine and drawing five, while they have also lost their last three home encounters.

Fenerbahce, meanwhile, arrive in Kocaeli after producing an emphatic response to their recent domestic setbacks, beating Corum 5-0 away from home in their last outing to return to winning ways.

The Yellow Canaries had previously suffered consecutive league defeats against Goztepe and Galatasaray, both by 2-1 scorelines, with the latter result particularly damaging as they fell further behind in the title race and prompted Ismail Kartal's resignation.

Emre Belozoglu subsequently took charge and has made an impressive start, recording a 3-2 victory over Liverpool in the Champions League before overseeing the emphatic win against Corum.

Fenerbahce's attack has been particularly productive this season, scoring 29 goals in 11 league matches to give them the most prolific frontline in the division, while their 10 goals conceded also represent the third-best defensive record, although they remain nine points off the top.

Kocaelispor are expected to be without Bruno Petkovic, who is dealing with a muscle injury, while Tanguy Zoukrou and Massadio Haidara are also doubtful with respective hamstring and tendon problems.

Aleksandar Jovanovic is another absentee, while Show is sidelined with an adductor injury, leaving Inan with decisions to make in midfield and defence.

Fenerbahce will be without Archie Brown, who is suspended, while Nathan Ake, Marco Asensio and Jayden Oosterwolde remain sidelined through injury.

Amara Diouf is also unavailable with a muscle problem, leaving Belozoglu without several options as he looks to maintain the momentum generated by the victory over Corum.

Oztasdelen; Yildiz, Dijksteel, Ortakaya, Rivas; Bingol, Kutlu, Susoho; Agyei, Aye, Baku

Ederson; Semedo, Skriniar, Oppong, Mercan; Guendouzi, Yuksek; Greenwood, Kahveci, Aydin; Lukaku

Kocaelispor have been considerably more reliable at home than away, conceding just twice in five league matches at their own stadium, but Fenerbahce's attacking record makes them difficult to overlook.

The hosts should be capable of making the contest competitive, particularly if they maintain their defensive discipline and exploit spaces on the counter-attack, but we expect the visitors' quality in the final third to ultimately prove decisive.

#1792. EPL Prepares for Most Exciting Title Race in Years

Home » Home 2 » EPL Prepares for Most Exciting Title Race in Years

Now that all of the top four English Premier League teams have had a chance to play each other, we find ourselves looking at one of the most wide open title races in recent memory. As of this writing, the league leaders are only separated by a mere six points. With the exception of Manchester City, we could very well see a new face hoisting the Premier League trophy at the end of the season.

For much of the year, it looked like Arsenal would be in the running for its first league title in more than a decade. With the Gunners’ recent victory against Leicester City, they are very much back in the conversation. Danny Welbeck returned to the pitch for the first time this season and made an immediate impact for Arsene Wenger’s squad, scoring the last-minute, game-winning goal to propel the team to within two points of the top spot. Given that even more key players are set to return to action for Arsenal in the coming months, this is easily the best shot they have had of winning a championship since their undefeated 2003-04 season.

Another surprise team that certainly deserves its own mention is Tottenham Hotspur. Following the club’s controversial defeat of Manchester City, the Spurs sit in second place, a mere two points behind Leicester City and ahead of Arsenal on goal differential. Tottenham have yet to win a title in the Premier League era and they have not won an English championship since 1961. The team has done a superb job of backing up star striker Harry Kane with a glut of promising young players, and their goal tally only helps to reinforce the wisdom behind the strategy of manager Mauricio Pochettino.

Meanwhile, Manchester City is still hoping to snag its third title as something of a swan song for exiting manager Manuel Pellegrini. It was recently announced that the club had hired Pep Guardiola . from Bayern Munich to take charge of the team beginning with next season. Thus, Pellegrini has been forced to endure the rest of the campaign as a dead man walking. Despite the impending exit of Pellegrini, City are still in the race for the Premier League title in addition to both the F.A. Cup and Champions League. Theoretically, the club could pull off a treble, if it can manage a solid string of performances during the final half of the season.

At the beginning of the season, it was expected that the usual suspects would once again dominate the league. Many predicted the reigning champs at Chelsea to repeat their success. However, a shocking season has seen the team part ways with controversial manager Jose Mourinho and struggle to remain in the top half of the tables with hopes of a Champions League spot dashed long ago.

For the first time in years, there’s a chance to see a completely new team win the league. No matter which club you support, there’s no denying that this has made for one of the most thrilling contests in recent memory. In a league where money talks, small fish like Leicester City are surprising everyone, and we can only hope that this means a new era of parity for the Premier League.

#1791. Jacobone: Milan and Juventus launch ‘preliminary enquiries’ for Man Utd striker Sesko

AC Milan and Juventus are both keeping tabs on Benjamin Sesko’s situation at Manchester United, according to a report.

United paid around €80m to sign Sesko from RB Leipzig, hoping he would be the long-term fix for the No.9 position. Last season he performed reasonably well, scoring 11 goals in 30 Premier League games which was not bad for a 22-year-old in a new league.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

This season, however, he is stuck on one goal in four league games, having spent time out injured too. With big changes at Old Trafford – including the arrival of Mauricio Pochettino as the head coach – it is another blank slate for the squad.

For example, club captain Bruno Fernandes has been linked with a move to Milan. Now, according to journalist Alessandro Jacobone, a new idea has emerged for the centre-forward position, perhaps if the pursuit of Nicolo Tresoldi does not go to plan.

“Juve and Milan are keeping an eye on things. But summer is the most realistic scenario. Benjamin Šeško could leave Manchester United, with Juventus and Milan having already made some preliminary enquiries to assess the financial feasibility of a potential move,” he said.

“For now, these are only preliminary discussions, useful for finding out the figures, conditions and possible deal structures. No concrete negotiations have been initiated.

“Sources close to the player’s camp are also playing down the possibility of a transfer as early as January, making a potential move in the next summer window considerably more likely. One to watch.”

Four of those 11 goals in his debut campaign came off the bench too as he developed a knack for being an impact substitute. This could give Milan food for thought, given they are looking for an alter-ego to Goncalo Ramos rather than someone to solely take over the striker role.

#1790. Super Mario! Dons hand rebuild job to Swiss success story Frick

Published: 14:14 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 14:45 EST, 15 November 2026

Aberdeen have appointed former Liechtenstein international Mario Frick as their new head coach.

The 52-year-old will take charge at Pittodrie, subject to the completion of UK visa formalities, following a successful spell with Swiss side FC Luzern.

Frick arrives in the north-east after five years in charge of Luzern, where he transformed the club’s fortunes after taking over in December 2021 with the team rooted to the bottom of the Swiss Super League. He guided them away from relegation trouble before leading them to a fourth-place finish and qualification for European football.

Announcing the appointment, Aberdeen chief executive Adrian Bevington said the club had undertaken an extensive recruitment process before selecting Frick as the man to lead the Dons forward.

Bevington said: 'We are delighted to welcome Mario Frick and his assistant coach Roman Matter to Aberdeen Football Club.

'Mario has significant experience as a head coach and has delivered impressive results with both Vaduz and Luzern. He has a proven track record of building competitive teams and developing young players.

'Throughout our discussions, he demonstrated a clear vision, strong leadership qualities and a deep understanding of what is required to build a successful team.'

Sporting director Lutz Pfannenstiel also welcomed the appointment and believes Frick has the qualities to make a major impact at Pittodrie.

Pfannenstiel said: 'Mario is a strong personality with clear ideas about how he wants his teams to play. He brings energy, ambition and a winning mentality, and knows how to build a strong team environment.

Aberdeen have appointed Mario Frick as their new manager

'We were looking for the right person to lead the next chapter of Aberdeen FC, and I’m convinced Mario has the qualities, character and vision to make a real impact.'

Before his spell with Luzern, Frick managed FC Balzers and FC Vaduz, winning promotion to the Swiss Super League with the latter. Across almost 290 senior matches as a head coach, he built a reputation for developing young talent, handing top-flight debuts to more than 30 academy players.

As a player, Frick represented clubs including FC Basel, FC Zürich, St Gallen, Grasshopper, Siena and Ternana. A striker who could also operate in defence, he won 125 caps for Liechtenstein between 1993 and 2016 and remains his country’s record goalscorer with 16 international goals.

Frick said: 'I’m excited to be joining Aberdeen FC. It’s a club with a proud history, passionate supporters and big ambitions.

'Together with the staff, my aim is to create an environment where the players can thrive, develop and perform at their very best, while working towards our goals as a team.'

Frick and assistant coach Matter are expected to arrive in Aberdeen at the start of the week and will begin preparations for next weekend’s Premiership clash with Kilmarnock.

#1788. The Rock of London: Looking back at John Terry’s Chelsea FC career

Home » Home 2 » The Rock of London: Looking back at John Terry’s Chelsea FC career

At the start of this season, John Terry leaving Chelsea was the last thing on anyone’s mind. All was rosy at Stamford Bridge, the home of the newly crowed English champions. In over 21 years at the club, there was no indication that Terry would not retire a Chelsea man.

The Blues’ skipper’s announcement in January 2016, then, came as a shock to the Chelsea faithful, bringing notice to the seemingly premature — even if inevitable — fall of the curtain on a legendary career.

After making his debut in the League Cup against Aston Villa late in 1998, John Terry made sporadic appearances under Gianluca Vialli, before joining Nottingham Forest on a short loan spell. He broke into the first team in 2000-01, when manager Claudio Ranieri handed him 22 Premier League appearances during a season that the 20-year-old would finish as the club’s Player of the Year.

It would be the first of several achievements to come.

Terry’s importance to the team grew as Ranieri relied on his partnership with then-captain Marcel Desailly to mastermind Chelsea’s progression from a fashionable mid-table club to a Champions League team that meant business. They received a major shot in the arm when Russian billionaire Roman Abramovich bought the club in 2003. It was also a significant year in Terry’s international career as he made his England debut against Serbia and Montenegro in June.

The season that followed saw Chelsea finish above perennial winners Manchester United for the first time in Premier League history, and defeat Premiership invincibles Arsenal en route to the club’s first Champions League semifinal. Terry ended the season making a first of four appearances in the PFA Team of the Year, and went to Portugal for the European Championships having displaced Sol Campbell as England’s first choice centre-back.

In the summer of 2004, Chelsea brought in Jose Mourinho, who was fresh from winning a treble with the unfancied FC Porto and raring to take on bigger challenges. The 23-year-old Terry was named captain as Chelsea embarked on the most successful period in the club’s history. In the three seasons that followed, Chelsea won 2 league cups, 2 Premier League titles and the FA Cup — success built on a core of John Terry, Frank Lampard, Petr Cech and Didier Drogba, Chelsea’s ‘old guard’.

This was also a period when Terry picked up several individual accolades. He was named PFA Player of the Year in 2005, the first defender to win the award since Paul McGrath in 1993. He would make a first of five consecutive appearances in the FIFPro World XI in 2005, as well as a first of four appearances in the UEFA Team of the Year.

He was also voted Chelsea’s Player of the Year for the second time in his career in 2006. Steve McClaren, hired as England manager after an underwhelming 2006 World Cup, named the Chelsea skipper as England captain.

Terry was now, beyond argument, one of football’s best.

However, more testing times were to come.

September 2007 saw the departure of Mourinho after a falling out with the club board. The season itself promised much but left a Chelsea squad dejected on three occasions as they saw the League Cup, the Premier League and the Champions League trophies go elsewhere.

For the European Cup in particular, Terry was left with no one but himself to blame as he slipped for the crucial penalty, a moment he has said will haunt him forever. Chelsea and Terry experienced further European heartbreak the following season as Tom Henning Ovrebo had a refereeing performance to forget at Stamford Bridge, handing Barcelona a berth in the final and eventually the trophy.

In early 2010, when he was revealed as the English footballer who had an affair with Vanessa Perroncel, Wayne Bridge’s ex-girlfriend — a horrendous personal error that cost him his status as England captain — it made him the perennial recipient of passionate booing across English grounds. After the revelation, Chelsea travelled to Burnley. Amidst a frosty reception, he scored a late winner to put Carlo Ancelotti’s side back on track in the title race, one they would go on to win in some style. All of this typified John Terry — imperfect, but unshakeable.

Terry had built an unflappable reputation as a top class defender, leader and hard man. He said about himself, “I still say if the ball is there to be won I will go for it, whether with my head or whatever, and if it means us scoring or stopping a goal, I won’t think twice.”

The period that followed, however, was not good for Chelsea or their captain. The team finished the 2010-11 season trophyless, and Carlo Ancelotti paid for it with his job. This was the first of two times in Terry’s career where he and his club would have an extremely underwhelming season following a dominant one, and it also marked the first attempt to phase him out of the first team.

New manager Andre Villas-Boas attempted to introduce a high defensive line that left Terry exposed on a number of occasions, and saw the young Portuguese manager fall back on quicker defenders to implement his system. He was also determined to make lesser use of Frank Lampard and displace Didier Drogba with Fernando Torres. These were unpopular moves that led to poor results and eventually his sacking. Terry was not helped by another personal abberation, mouthing racial profanity at Anton Ferdinand of QPR, an act that saw him land a lengthy ban and damage his position in the England squad almost beyond repair.

Interim manager Roberto Di Matteo reinstated the old guard, and was rewarded with the ultimate prize — the first Champions League in Chelsea’s history.

Terry retired from international football following EURO 2012, leaving him to focus on his club career. However, further rotation was to follow during the reign of Rafael Benitez, who played Terry only in games of lesser importance. This was something he could do with relative impunity owing to the fact that his stock could not have fallen any further among Chelsea fans.

The writing was seemingly on the wall, however. Unsavoury incidents were fresher in the memory than individual accolades, the skipper was out of favour for two seasons running, and was well over 30 years of age. Was John Terry done?

Mourinho did not share the views of Benitez and Villas-Boas. Where they saw a slowing, easily-exposed has-been, he saw an experienced warrior with an excellent reading of the game who could form a title-winning partnership with the quicker Gary Cahill.

Terry grabbed the opportunity he was handed with gusto, performing with excellence in Mourinho’s lower defensive block. The English pair formed the core of a defence that would go on to win the club’s fourth Premier League title in 2015, leading the table from the opening day to the end. It was a landmark achievement for Terry in particular as he played every minute of a league campaign for the first time in his career, aged 34.

Once again they tried to put him down. Once again he fed off it and rose tall.

Chelsea did not start the defence of their title well at all, gathering just 4 points from the first 4 matches. Mourinho, who asked Terry to take the club on his shoulders in 2004 and stood by him for two seasons in his second stint, hauled off his skipper at half-time at the Etihad in the second game of the season, and began to rotate him out of the team, giving an increasing number of starts to the young Kurt Zouma.

The season did not take much of a turn for the better even under interim manager Guus Hiddink, particularly in a defensive sense as the Blues continued to let in goals during a meek climb to the top half of the table, with or without Terry in the side.

A sending off at the Stadium of Light following an injury layoff is not the kind of ending that the fans desired for their beloved captain, who has emerged from the dugout 703 times in Chelsea colours and has been the face of the club through the most successful period in their history.

Offered a new deal by the club last week, the skipper responded, “The contract extension the club has offered me is a different role and I hope everyone will understand I want to take the time to consider it carefully before making a decision.” While fans will hope — for reasons emotional as well as those to do with football — that Terry stays on, the chances look slim.

Should the captain leave the ship, the Blues supporters’ emotions are best summed up by a certain banner that embellishes the Shed End: Captain, Leader, Legend.

#1787. Genclerbirligi vs Gaziantep - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joshua Cole | 19 Nov 2026 16:48

Genclerbirligi will be looking to return to winning ways when they welcome Gaziantep to Eryaman Stadium on Saturday afternoon in the Turkish Super Lig.

The hosts sit 14th in the table with 11 points from as many matches, three points clear of the relegation zone, while the visitors are 16th and in the drop zone with eight points after losing seven of their opening 11 league fixtures.

Genclerbirligi head into Saturday's encounter after suffering a 3-0 defeat away to Besiktas in their last league outing, having been unable to build on the confidence gained from their emphatic 5-0 victory over Alanyaspor a week earlier.

That win was their biggest of the campaign and followed another 5-0 success against Karakopru Belediyespor in the Turkish Cup, but their return to league action in Istanbul brought them back down to earth as Besiktas scored twice before half-time and added a third after the break.

The Red-and-Blacks have now lost three of their last four league matches and won just one of their last nine, with their only victory during that period coming against Alanyaspor, while they have conceded 21 goals in 11 league fixtures, the third-highest total in the division.

Their defensive record has been a particular concern away from home, where they have conceded 14 times in five matches and scored just once, although their performances in Ankara have generally been more encouraging.

Genclerbirligi have collected eight points from six home league matches, winning twice, drawing twice and losing twice, and they have scored nine goals at Eryaman Stadium in the competition, with their 2-1 victory over Fenerbahce representing the highlight.

Bernd Storck's side will hope to avoid another winless streak by bouncing back immediately, with optimism stemming from their home results and the fact that they beat the visitors on this ground in their last meeting here, while they have also never lost to them at home (W4, D1).

Gaziantep, meanwhile, have endured a much more difficult spell, losing their last six league matches and failing to score in each of their most recent two outings.

Their latest defeat came at home against Kasimpasa, who secured a 2-0 victory with both goals coming before the break, while they had previously lost by the same scoreline away to Trabzonspor.

Those results followed defeats against Erzurumspor, Istanbul Basaksehir, Corum and Kocaelispor, leaving the Red-and-Blacks with just two wins and two draws from their opening 11 matches, alongside seven defeats.

The club subsequently parted company with coach Orhan Ak by mutual agreement following the loss to Kasimpasa, leaving Gaziantep to prepare for this fixture amid another managerial change.

Assistant coach Mustafa Aksoy oversaw the first training session after Ak's departure, but Volkan Demirel has been appointed as their new head coach, and the club will be hoping that a change in the dugout can bring an immediate response.

Genclerbirligi will be without Metehan Baltaci, who is suspended after receiving a red card for two yellow cards in the defeat to Besiktas, while Dimitrios Goutas remains sidelined with a serious knee injury that has ruled him out for the season.

Thalisson Kelven is also unavailable through injury, while Kevin Rodrigues remains sidelined and Peter Etebo is a doubt, leaving Storck with decisions to make in defence and midfield.

Pedro Pereira is also doubtful with a muscle injury, while Gokhan Akkan and Muhammet Ensar Cavusoglu are among the other unavailable players.

Gaziantep are expected to be without Kacper Tobiasz, who is recovering from a hamstring injury, while Nazim Sangare and Fuat Bavuk are also sidelined.

Sontje Hansen is another absentee, leaving the visitors without several options as they look to improve on a difficult run of form.

Egribayat; Celik, Dursun, Thalisson, Aydar; Niasse, Ulgun; Traore, Tongya, Gouveia; Mendes

Dadakdeniz; Perez, Abena, Sylla, Calhanoglu; Bacuna; Sorescu, Camara, Maxim, Kozlowski; Stewart

Genclerbirligi have been inconsistent this season, but their home performances offer encouragement and they should be favourites against a Gaziantep side that have lost six consecutive league matches and failed to score in their last two.

#1786. Erling Haaland cuts off his trademark blond hair

Erling Haaland has unveiled a dramatic new look after cutting off his trademark blond locks.

The Manchester City striker revealed his new buzzcut hairstyle on Sunday morning ahead of his side’s Premier League opener at home to Bournemouth later in the day.

Later in the episode, Haaland called a host of famous faces, including Oasis singer Noel Gallagher and former City manager Pep Guardiola, to get their opinions on his transformation.

Pep Guardiola's reaction to Erling Haaland's new haircut. 😭😂📲 Watch: https://t.co/4KvxC9e5mx pic.twitter.com/QQBCKKpGkP

Haaland, 26, has not sported short hair since his time at Borussia Dortmund, where he played three seasons before joining City in 2022.

Haaland removed his hairband during a 4-1 win over Arsenal in 2023 on a raucous night at the Etihad as City beat their title rivals to move one step closer to winning the league. There will be no need for one now, though, with a close-cut look to mark a new campaign.

It is a new-look City in more ways than one this term with head coach Enzo Maresca looking to kickstart a new era following Pep Guardiola’s exit.

Maresca is hoping for an immediate return to form in City’s Premier League opener after a chastening 3-0 defeat by Arsenal in the Community Shield last week.

So far, only Elliot Anderson has arrived but Maresca is hopeful the club will be active in the transfer market. Rodri has left for Barcelona while Savinho is closing in on a move to Tottenham.

“I’ll try to find a new Rodri – it is what it is,” the former Chelsea manager said. “Rodri, before he arrived here, he didn’t win the Ballon d’Or, he didn’t win the Champions League, he didn’t win the Club World Cup. Then he joined the club and then after he achieved many important things. Now the target for us is to try to find the new Rodri.

“When David Silva was here, everyone was worried - Kevin [De Bruyne] arrived. When Sergio Agüero was here, everyone was worried – Erling [Haaland] arrived. When Ferdinando left, Rodri arrived. It’s just about this.

“When they leave, you need to be good and recruit the next one. They are all similar – David, Kevin, Fernandinho, Rodri, Agüero, Erling. It’s just normal, it’s a change. It’s not a problem, just go again and try to do the right things.”

Maresca added: “Hopefully we can do the things that we need to do. It doesn’t help that there are players that for different reasons want to leave, this is for sure.

“But we need to adapt and we don’t want to keep players here that don’t want to stay.

“The normal thing in transfer windows is that you have to wait because all the clubs try to keep players until the last week and then sell for more money.

“It’s normal, I’m not worried about that. When the transfer window closes and we have all the squad there, for sure it will be different.”

#1785. Galatasaray vs Samsunspor - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joshua Cole | 19 Nov 2026 16:49, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 20:30

Galatasaray will aim to stretch their lead at the top of the Turkish Super Lig table when they host struggling Samsunspor on Saturday afternoon.

The match has been moved from RAMS Park because of pitch problems and will now be played at Basaksehir Fatih Terim Stadium, with the league leaders given extra time to carry out maintenance and improvement work ahead of their upcoming UEFA Champions League fixture against Aston Villa.

Galatasaray went into the international break on a six-game winning streak in all competitions, a run that began with a 1-0 victory over Genclerbirligi before they beat Lille 4-2 in the Champions League and Fenerbahce 2-1 at home in the league.

The Lions then won 4-0 away to Konyaspor, beat Stuttgart 2-0 in the Champions League and edged Amedspor 4-3 just before the break, with their attacking output particularly impressive as they scored at least twice in five of those six matches.

In the victory over Amed, Galatasaray raced into a 3-0 lead through Rafael Leao's early strike, an own goal from goalkeeper Alban Lafont and Alexey Batrakov's effort before the hour mark, but they subsequently conceded twice before Baris Alper Yilmaz restored their two-goal cushion in the 80th minute, only for the hosts to concede again in stoppage time before holding on for the victory.

Okan Buruk's side have suffered just one league defeat this season, a 4-0 loss away to Trabzonspor, which has left them with 28 points from 11 matches, having also drawn 2-2 at home against Corum in their opening game of the campaign.

Keeping opponents off the scoresheet at home has been an issue for Cimbom, who have conceded in five of their six home league matches this season, including each of their last three.

Samsunspor won the last meeting against Galatasaray to end a nine-game losing streak in this fixture, but the visitors arrive in considerably worse form this season.

However, they received a much-needed boost just before the break, beating Konyaspor 1-0 at home to end an eight-game winless streak, which had been a club record.

It was also the first victory under Nenad Bjelica, who was appointed in October to replace Thorsten Fink, who was dismissed after nine months in charge following just one win in his opening seven matches.

Samsunspor are 17th on seven points, one place above the bottom and one point from safety, and while they finally recorded some positivity before the break, they travel to a venue where they have lost eight consecutive games, leaving them with a difficult task after the international hiatus.

Galatasaray have major absentees, with Victor Osimhen undergoing surgery on a loose fragment in his left knee after the Stuttgart game and expected to be out for several weeks.

Leao is also sidelined through injury, while goalkeeper Ugurcan Cakir picked up a shoulder problem on international duty and is not expected to play, with Gunay Guvenc tipped to start between the posts.

Davinson Sanchez is also unavailable after withdrawing from Colombia's squad with a muscle problem, while Roland Sallai is sidelined through injury and Batrakov is also listed as unavailable.

Samsunspor have fewer concerns, although Celil Yuksel is sidelined through injury and Fatih Kaya remains a doubt.

Mohamed Bayo is expected to lead the attack, with Tanguy Coulibaly, Oskar Ohlenschlæger and Afonso Sousa providing support from the attacking midfield positions.

Argentine goalkeeper Ezequiel Bacher scored perhaps the most bizarre own goal ever during his side's recent Primera B play-off game.

Comunicaciones were taking on Arsenal Sarandi at the weekend with the score 0-0, and the goalkeeper had caught the ball from a cross with the aim of getting the game back under way.

#1782. Parma vs Roma - prediction, team news, lineups

By Jonathan O'Shea | 19 Nov 2026 17:07, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 17:12

Still unbeaten in Serie A this season, free-scoring Roma will return to action with a trip to lowly Parma on Saturday evening.

Sitting third - just behind reigning champions Inter Milan and city rivals Lazio - the Giallorossi averaged four goals per game as they posted three consecutive league wins before the break.

Despite suffering two agonising Champions League defeats in recent weeks, Roma have hardly faltered on the domestic front; they are one of only two teams still undefeated in Serie A, alongside surprise leaders Lazio.

Soon after swatting Cagliari and Udinese aside, the Giallorossi signed off for the international period with a comfortable 3-0 home victory over Sassuolo, in which rising star Rodrigo Mora scored for a third straight league game.

It was an increasingly rare clean sheet for a club boasting the most lethal attack in Italy's top flight: Roma are only the fourth team in 65 years to hit the 30-goal mark by Serie A’s 11th matchday.

Dating back to last term, Gian Piero Gasperini’s side have scored at least twice in all but one of their last 16 league fixtures, only failing to do so in Como, where Donyell Malen was sent off.

Allowed to roam freely into the opposition area, defenders have collectively contributed eight goals this season, easing any pressure on Malen, Mora and their fellow forwards.

Beginning the build-up to next month’s Derby della Capitale, Roma will now seek a fifth straight win over Parma, who they beat 3-2 on their most recent trip to Stadio Tardini, with Malen inevitably scoring twice.

In fact, Parma have lost 13 of the past 20 league meetings on home turf, so history will not be on their side this weekend.

The hosts have endured a rocky start to the season, already changing coaches, and new boss Alberto Gilardino only celebrated his first victory shortly before the break.

However, days after stunning Atalanta with a shock 3-0 win in Bergamo, his side were beaten by Bologna in the Derby dell'Emilia.

Parma were reduced to 10 men within eight minutes at the Tardini, after Abdoulaye Ndiaye was dismissed following a VAR review, and they ultimately ended up losing 2-1.

As a result, the Gialloblu sit just one point above the bottom three, with only eight points on the board so far.

The club’s second-highest Serie A scorer during his playing days, Gilardino has a more modest managerial record, and he surely faces another survival scrap after last term’s fruitless fight with Pisa.

Roma have welcomed Paulo Dybala and first-choice goalkeeper Mile Svilar back during the break, but the latter’s deputy Pierluigi Gollini remains a doubt after missing two games with a back injury.

Devyne Rensch (adductor) and Lorenzo Pellegrini (thigh) are still sidelined, but Gasperini should have everyone else available.

A sure starter up front, Malen sits joint-second in the Capocannoniere rankings with eight Serie A goals, and the Dutch striker also scored for his country in the UEFA Nations League last week.

Meanwhile, Parma will be missing Argentine forward David Romero, who sustained a serious shoulder injury against Bologna.

Diego Carlos is also struggling with a thigh strain, injury-prone midfielder Adrian Bernabe is a big doubt, and Ndiaye must serve a one-match ban.

In the absence of Romero, teenage starlet Simone Lontani could partner El Bilal Toure, but Nesta Elphege is another contender.

Daffara; Delprato, Troilo, Drobnic; Britschgi, Fabbian, Sierro, Keita, Valeri; Lontani, Toure

Svilar; Mancini, Ndicka, Hermoso; Molina, Cristante, Kone, Wesley; Soule, Mora; Malen

Roma can pick up where they left off before the break, as a limited Parma side will struggle to match their intensity and flair.

A fourth straight win in Serie A will warm the Giallorossi up for next week's tough trip to Paris Saint-Germain.
